stories.title: ‘All my efforts failed, it takes two to tango’:Chandrasekhar says he made efforts to work with Mayawati but she was unwilling
stories.summary: Chandrasekhar, the Nagina MP and chief of the Azad Samaj Party, made a major statement about Mayawati on Tuesday. During a press conference in Sambhal, Chandrasekhar said, "Society wants Behenji and us to come together in the elections, but it takes two hands to clap. I made several efforts from my side, but they were unsuccessful." On the question of EVMs, Chandrasekhar accused the Election Commission of electoral malpractice. The MP said that the 2024 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election should be cancelled. Describing the upcoming MLC election as a test for 2027, he said it would give the government an idea of the Opposition's strength. Chandrasekhar says, ‘MLC elections are a test for the Opposition’ Chandrashekhar said, "Today, educated young people in Uttar Pradesh are roaming around unemployed. Schools are closing, while liquor shops are opening. There is violence in colleges, while student union elections have been stopped. Farmers' crops have been destroyed. Hospitals lack facilities. There is no recruitment exam in which the paper is not leaked or a scam does not take place." Our party is not contesting the MLC elections, except for one seat. The Opposition is contesting them. How strong they are will become clear in this MLC election. If they are well prepared and in a position to defeat the BJP, it will become clear before 2027 how capable the Opposition is. Government cornered over unemployment, paper leaks and law and order Chandrashekhar said, "What is the state of crime under the Uttar Pradesh government? There is chaos everywhere. Murders are taking place every day. If law and order is good, why are people losing their lives? People are being forced to live in extremely difficult conditions. People want to somehow bring an end to the BJP government in 2027." MP Chandrashekhar also answered questions from the media at the press conference. Read the details ... Question: Mayawati has accused you of working as the BJP's B-team? Answer: Accusations and counter-accusations are a regular feature of politics. Opposition leaders are now making allegations against her. I have been listening to all this. Let me tell you my side. It is not my wish, nor Behenji's, but society's wish that we work together. I am ready to contest the election again, relying on the dedicated workers of the Azad Samaj Party and the Bhim Army, and on the great, self-respecting people of Nagina-Bijnor. It will become clear who the people stand with. Question: Samajwadi Party MP Ramji Lal Suman said that the BJP-RSS is not humanitarian and wants to implement the Manusmriti. They want to end reservations...? Answer: Which party of theirs is humanitarian? They too changed everything that existed in the names of Babasaheb and Kanshi Ram Sahib. What kind of humanitarian party is that? Ramji Lal is a good man. In that party, they have now demolished his house and other properties, and the poor man is distressed. What can he do? Everyone is moving around, but he is not being allowed to do so. Question: Asaduddin Owaisi and Chandrashekhar Azad have been seen together several times. Will there be an alliance in the 2027 Assembly elections? Answer: When elections were held for the chairpersons of nagar panchayats and municipal corporations, we contested together with Jayant Chaudhary, from Saharanpur across Uttar Pradesh. He joined the BJP, Akhilesh ji joined the INDIA alliance, and we were left among the people. This is an electoral alliance. I cannot announce today what will happen tomorrow. I do not make predictions. Question: No party is ready to take you and Asaduddin Owaisi along. Is this because they fear losing votes or the party coming into existence? Answer: That is what you are saying. How would you know what is happening behind the scenes-whether anyone wants to take us along or not? Others only want the votes of our people in the name of taking us along. This is a political matter. You have sources; find out why the BJP could not be defeated in 2017 and 2022. They have previously lost 250-300 seats. They do not want to defeat the BJP by bringing people together; instead, they want to make the BJP's path easier. If they were concerned, they would bring everyone together. The BJP contested the Lok Sabha election with 44 parties. The Opposition does not want to contest alongside strong leaders who have votes. They are looking for ways to ensure the BJP wins. Question: How many seats is the alliance preparing to contest in Uttar Pradesh in the 2027 Assembly election? Answer: We have announced 87 in-charges and will issue another list after a week. We have been working hard since 2022. We contested elections on only two seats in 2024. This time, our workers are in full swing. The workers believe that the Azad Samaj Party will defeat the BJP in the election and form a government of the people.

stories.summary: A man performed the last rites of his daughter’s effigy after she eloped from home and married her lover in Prayagraj. The girl released a video on Tuesday, accusing her family of performing the last rites of her effigy and declaring her dead after she got married. Her father named Ganesh Pandey considered her dead and wrote “Late” before her name in the caption of her photograph. The family completely severed ties with the girl after learning about her marriage. According to them, the man she married was someone she used to call her brother and had been tying a rakhi to him for 15 years. The incident has caused a stir in the village. The case is from the Industrial police station area of Prayagraj. Check out the pictures below : Read the full story below : Ganesh Pandey, a resident of Teluawan village, lives with his wife, Mansha Pandey, and their four children. His second daughter, Nandni Pandey (20), was in a relationship with Shashwat Gupta (22), a young man from the same village. Shashwat used to visit Ganesh’s house. His father, Chhedilal, works in the electricity department, while Shashwat is pursuing an LLB. Nandni and Shashwat had regarded each other as brother and sister. Nandni had also been tying a rakhi to Shashwat for the past 15 years. However, the two eventually fell in love, which their families did not realise. On September 20, Nandni and Shashwat eloped and got married. Nandni said they liked each other and married of their own free will. She also appealed to people not to harass them. Girl releases a video accusing family of harassment In the video, Nandini said, "My family performed my last rites on 22 August. The day my family declared me dead, I too considered them separated from my life." My husband's name is Shashwat Gupta. I am currently living with him. My father, Ganesh Pandey, constantly harassed me. He physically and mentally abused me. I had been unwell for a long time, but my family did not even arrange proper treatment for me. I am now receiving all the facilities and medical treatment I need. I am happy with my husband's family. Nandini also denied the allegation that she had fled from home with ₹2 lakh. She said, "Our family never had that much cash." Father performs last rites after making an effigy of his daughter Nandini's father, Ganesh Pandey, learnt about his daughter's marriage on 21 September. He then presumed that his daughter was dead and performed her symbolic last rites. Nandini's mother, Mansha Pandey, said, "Shashwat had been visiting our home for a long time. Nandini had considered him her brother and tied a rakhi on his wrist for 15 years. They left home and got married." This boy has lured my daughter away. This marriage will not last long. This is what is happening nowadays. He will kill my daughter. We even observed my daughter's death anniversary on 22 September. We no longer have anything to do with the girl.

High Court judge said, ‘I thought I’d never smoke’:First mistake became a habit; no hookah bars in UP
stories.summary: The Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court has ruled on the operation of hookah bars in Uttar Pradesh. The court clarified that restaurants or other establishments providing hookahs even in designated smoking areas at public places is illegal. A bench comprising Justice Shekhar B Saraf and Justice Abdhesh Kumar Chaudhary dismissed all petitions related to hookah bars. During the proceedings, Justice Shekhar B Saraf advised young people to avoid smoking. Sharing an experience from his student days, he said that a cigarette started as a joke gradually became a habit and was difficult to give up. The court said that providing hookah services in public places violates Rule 4(3) of the amended Prohibition of Smoking Rules, 2008, introduced in 2017. Preparing or renting out a hookah is not merely an activity Justice Saraf said, "Do not take your first cigarette lightly." The court also made it clear that preparing a hookah, filling it with material and handing it to a customer constitute a 'service'. However, such a service is illegal if it leads to a violation of the provisions of the Constitution. The bench also rejected the argument that a customer could simply rent a hookah device and use it himself. The court said that the entire process of operating a hookah involves an element of service. Therefore, it cannot be regarded as merely renting out equipment. Breathing Clean Air Is Also a Fundamental Right The court said that while the fundamental right to carry on a business was important, avoiding involuntary exposure to tobacco smoke in public places and breathing clean air were also fundamental rights under Article 21 of the Constitution. It said the rights of non-smokers could not be curtailed to protect the commercial interests of an establishment. The bench also referred to the state’s duty to protect public health under Article 47 of the Constitution. Municipal Corporation Has No Authority to Grant Hookah Bar Licences The court also clarified that the Food Safety and Drug Administration Department and municipal corporations in Uttar Pradesh do not have the authority to issue licences for regulating hookah bars. Under the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act, police officers are authorised to ensure compliance with the provisions of the law. The court said that this includes conducting searches, making seizures and taking punitive action against establishments violating the rules. The court clearly concluded that operating a hookah bar in a designated smoking area at a public place in Uttar Pradesh, and restaurants providing hookah services, are contrary to the law. The bench subsequently dismissed all the related writ petitions. Judge recounts his own story: He vowed never to smoke, but a single puff became a habit Allahabad High Court Justice Shekhar B. Saraf shared his experience from his student days in verse while hearing a case related to smoking. Warning young people, he said that smoking often begins with a single cigarette taken as a joke or out of curiosity, but can gradually turn into a habit. Justice Saraf said that during his law school days, he used to mock smokers and had resolved never to smoke a cigarette. However, it began when he jokingly took a puff of a cigarette while having tea with a senior. The occasional cigarette gradually turned into a regular habit. Tried nicotine patches and chewed gum, but could not quit smoking He also mentioned the difficulties caused by smoking in his account. The judge said he later tried measures such as nicotine patches and chewing gum to quit the habit, but giving it up was not easy. Through his experience, Justice Shekhar B. Saraf conveyed a message to young people that considering the first puff of a cigarette insignificant can lead to problems later.

stories.title: SP needs 12 MLAs for third Rajya Sabha seat:Akhilesh Yadav promises a surprise candidate, Ram Gopal’s name decided
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav is yet to reveal the name of the third candidate for the Rajya Sabha seat, promising a surprise pick. The names of Ram Gopal Yadav and Alok Ranjan are considered final for the other two seats. The suspense over the third seat continues. Akhilesh called the party’s MLAs to the party office again on Tuesday. The nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha election had already been obtained. During the meeting, the MLAs signed Ram Gopal Yadav’s nomination paper as proposers. The MLAs have been asked to stay in Lucknow for now so that they can sign the nomination papers of the other candidates as proposers once their names are finalised. The remaining two names are expected to be finalised by Wednesday morning. Yadav held a meeting with the party’s MLAs at the party headquarters on Monday regarding the Rajya Sabha election. The SP may field candidates for three Rajya Sabha seats. While 37 MLAs are needed to win one seat, the party currently has 100 MLAs, including one who is in jail. This means the election of two SP candidates to the Rajya Sabha is certain, while the party will need the support of at least 12 more MLAs for a third candidate. The party has not yet revealed how it plans to arrange the additional support. During the meeting, Akhilesh Yadav sought suggestions from the MLAs, who authorised him to select the Rajya Sabha candidates. Meanwhile, the nomination process began in Room No. 8 of the Vidhan Bhavan. Candidates will submit their nomination papers there. On the first day, 11 nomination forms were sold, with the BJP buying eight and the Samajwadi Party buying three. 37 MLAs needed to elect one Rajya Sabha member The Uttar Pradesh Assembly has 403 seats, of which seven are currently vacant, leaving 396 MLAs. Elections will be held for 10 Rajya Sabha seats. The formula for the election is 396/10+1, which means 396 will be divided by 11 and one will be added to the result. Therefore, 37 first-preference votes will be needed to elect one Rajya Sabha member. The Samajwadi Party currently has 100 MLAs. Of these, Ramakant Yadav is in jail, reducing the party’s effective strength to 99. The SP will therefore need at least 12 more votes to get its third candidate elected. The party is now looking for a candidate who can secure the additional support. The BJP, meanwhile, will need at least 25 votes to elect its eighth candidate. In this situation, second- and third-preference votes could become important. MLAs are given instructions on how to mark their first preference and whom to choose as their second and third preferences. During counting, a candidate is declared elected once they secure the required quota of votes. If an election is held, cross-voting could therefore become a factor. SP candidates to file nominations on Wednesday Meanwhile, Akhilesh Yadav’s absence from the INDIA bloc meeting scheduled in Delhi on Wednesday is reportedly linked to the filing of nomination papers for the Rajya Sabha candidates. Congress stages protest by planting paddy on road:Mayank Chaubey says Kashi roads turn into ponds during rain, demands permanent drainage
stories.summary: Congress workers staged a protest over waterlogging and the poor condition of the roads in UP's Varanasi on Tuesday. The incident took place in Shankarpuram Colony, located in Paharia-Benipur Pokhara. Led by the Mahanagar Congress Committee, the workers planted paddy on the waterlogged road to protest against the Municipal Corporation and the government. The protest was led by Mayank Chaubey, vice-president of the Mahanagar Congress Committee and in-charge of the North Assembly constituency. He demanded that the drainage system be repaired and a permanent solution be found to the problems affecting the roads. According to the Congress workers, so much water had accumulated on the road that there was no longer any difference between the road and a field. Rice planted on a waterlogged road Congress workers reached the middle of a waterlogged road in Shankarpuram Colony and planted rice seedlings. The workers described it as a symbol of protest. They said that waterlogging on the road after the rain was causing problems for people travelling through the area. They planted rice on the road to highlight the problem and protest against it. Mayank Chaubey says basic problems persist in Kashi Chaubey said that Kashi's condition remained poor despite the double-engine government. Despite being Prime Minister Narendra Modi's parliamentary constituency, residents are struggling with waterlogging, poor roads and drainage problems. He said that the BJP had controlled the municipal corporation in Varanasi for a long time. The mayor, MP and MLA are from the BJP, and the state government is also led by the BJP. Despite this, people have to contend with waterlogging during the monsoon. Chaubey also questioned the functioning of Mayor Ashok Tiwari. He said accountability should also be fixed for the growing disorder in Kashi, waterlogging and the poor condition of its roads. He said the public now wants not just assurances but a permanent solution to the problem of waterlogging. Demand solution in all waterlogging-affected areas Congress demanded that drainage arrangements be immediately improved in all waterlogging-affected areas of Varanasi, including Shankarpuram Colony. It also called for a permanent solution to the problem of damaged roads.

stories.title: Live-in relationship with aunt, killed her over suspicion of affair:Buried pregnant woman's body, then went to temple; told police she died by suicide
stories.summary: Police arrested the accused on Tuesday for allegedly murdering a pregnant woman in Jaipur and burying her body in the lawn of a house. The accused had brought the woman, who was his relative aunt, from Uttar Pradesh and was in a live-in relationship with her. He allegedly strangled her to death over suspicion of an affair and buried her body. After the murder, the accused went to Samod Hanuman Temple. During interrogation, he allegedly tried to cover up the crime by claiming that the woman had died by suicide. He told police that he panicked and buried the body. The body of Kiran (32) was found buried at a house in Prestige Colony under the Bindayaka police station area on September 27. Switched off phone and fled Jaipur DCP (West) Prashant Kiran said police arrested accused Pravesh Rawat (22), son of Ramu, a resident of Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh. After the body was found, police began conducting raids to trace Pravesh. To evade police, he switched off his mobile phone and fled Jaipur. During the investigation, police found that while fleeing after the murder, Pravesh had gone to a factory on the morning of September 27 and borrowed ₹500 from a contractor. Police teams began tracking him using CCTV footage. When he switched his phone on, his location was traced near the Uttar Pradesh border, where a police team arrested him. Suspected the woman During interrogation, police found that Kiran, the deceased, was Pravesh’s aunt by relation. He had allegedly brought her from her home in January. Pravesh and Kiran had come from their village just two months earlier. As Kiran was pregnant, he was living with her in a live-in relationship and taking care of her. The two used the same mobile phone. Pravesh would leave the phone at home when he went to work. He suspected that Kiran was talking to someone else on the phone. Troubled by this suspicion, Pravesh allegedly strangled Kiran to death early on September 23. Dug a pit in lawn, buried body with salt After the murder, Pravesh allegedly sat near the body in the room for a long time. He kept thinking about how to dispose of the body to evade police. Based on crime scenes he had seen in films, he allegedly planned to bury the body in the lawn in front of the house. He locked the body inside the room and went out to buy salt. At night, he dug a pit in the lawn. He placed the body inside, sprinkled salt over it and covered it with soil. Foetus came out of the body Prashant Kiran said the accused dug the pit and buried the body on the night of September 23. Three to four days later, the foetus came out of the deceased’s body. Kiran was around six months pregnant. Visited temple after murder After the murder, the accused allegedly left the house the next day, claiming he wanted to “wash away his sins”. He locked the house, visited Samod Hanuman Temple and returned home in the evening. He continued working at the factory normally for two days, on September 25 and 26, without raising anyone’s suspicion. On the night of September 26, he called his family and told them that Kiran had died. Planned to flee Rajasthan As the body was around four days old, it had started decomposing and a foul smell was coming from the lawn. Pravesh had also run out of money. He then allegedly planned to flee the state to evade police. On the morning of September 27, he locked the house, switched off his mobile phone and left Jaipur. House rented by the accused A murder report had been filed in the case by 52-year-old Krishna Kumar Meena, a resident of Brijmandal Colony in Jhotwara. The report stated that he owned a house in Prestige Colony in Bindayaka. The house was built on 100 square yards of a 200-square-yard plot, while the remaining 100 square yards at the front lay vacant. Two months earlier, he had rented the house to Pravesh Rawat, the brother-in-law of Mangal Kumar, a resident of Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, at Mangal's request. He had said that Kiran was his wife. Lawn had been dug up and there was also a foul smell The report stated that he had arrived at the house at around 10:30 a.m. on 27 September to check on it. He tried to contact the tenant, Pravesh, but found that his mobile phone was switched off. When he went into the lawn inside the house, he saw that the soil had been dug up. A foul smell was also coming from the area. He immediately called Pravesh's brother-in-law and questioned him. When the soil was removed, a woman's hand was found visibly buried underneath. After the police control room was informed, personnel from Bindayaka police station reached the spot. The body, which had been buried after digging up the soil, was exhumed. Once it was brought out, the body was identified as that of Kiran, who was also around six months pregnant. After nearly four hours of effort, the police, with the help of the FSL team, gathered evidence and sent the body to Kanwatia Hospital. Told this story after being arrested During interrogation after his arrest, the accused tried to save himself. He said that Kiran had committed suicide by hanging herself. He said that when he reached his house, he found Kiran hanging from the noose. He took the body down, fearing that the police would arrest him. After Kiran's suicide, he buried her body to dispose of it. To mislead the police, he kept repeating that the only mistake he had made was burying the body.

stories.title: Important files missing from mayor’s office:Pramila Pandey says, ‘Inquiry underway; action if files not found’
stories.summary: Kanpur Mayor Pramila Pandey claimed on Tuesday that several important files had gone missing from her office, taking the dispute at the Kanpur Municipal Corporation House meeting to a new turn. The files have not been found despite searches of the rooms and cupboards. The mayor said that a search for the files and an investigation into the matter were underway. She said, “If the necessary files are found, that is fine; otherwise, further action will be taken.” They showed the House proceedings live to a senior leader On Tuesday, Mayor Pramila Pandey said several important files were found to be missing when all three rooms in her office were searched. She alleged that some councillors had come to the House meeting with the intention of creating a ruckus. She said they were also showing the House proceedings live to a senior leader. The mayor said Pawan Gupta had earlier attended the first House meeting with a box on his head, yet he was later included in the executive committee. She added that MPs, MLAs and MLCs are also invited members of the House. There is no objection to them sitting in the House and watching the proceedings. What was the issue During the Municipal Corporation House meeting last Saturday, rebel BJP councillors Alok Pandey, Pawan Gupta, Lakshmi Kori and Vikas Jaiswal alleged that Manish Bajpai, the Mandal minister from Kaushalpuri, had been held hostage in the mayor's office. The councillors alleged that Manish Bajpai had gone to the House to get a letter received when he was allegedly misbehaved with and his mobile phone was also snatched. Manish Bajpai had also lodged a complaint with the organisation in the matter. My son was sitting in the rest room : Mayor Pandey also explained why her son, Amit Pandey, was present in her office. She said she had already anticipated that there could be a ruckus during the House meeting. For this reason, she had asked her son to sit in the rest room. The mayor alleged that some people entered the rooms in her office while she was attending the House meeting. She questioned why the councillors needed to enter the office in her absence. According to her, the move was an attempt to frame her and her son. She said she had not expected the BJP president to make such statements and also questioned the role of the organisation’s office-bearers. stories.title: Five from family die during shraddh ritual:All drown while trying to save one in Jhansi; father-son, nephews among dead
stories.summary: A major accident occurred in Jhansi during a shraddha ritual at 12 noon on Tuesday. Five members of the same family drowned in the river. Five people, including a father and son, a nephew and a sister's son, died in the incident. It is being reported that they had all entered the deep waters of the Sukhnei River for the shraddha ritual. During this, one person lost his balance and began to be swept away by the strong current. One by one, all of them drowned while trying to save him. After hearing the cries for help, people nearby informed the police. The police reached the spot with divers. After conducting a rescue operation for around 30 minutes, they recovered all five bodies. The incident occurred in the jurisdiction of the Mauranipur police station.

stories.title: Handpump in Kanpur supplies water without being operated:Villagers call it rain miracle every year; engineers say check valve may be faulty
stories.summary: For nearly a month, a handpump in Kanpur has been doing something unusual — pouring out water without anyone operating it. The 110-foot-deep handpump is currently releasing around 2 litres of water every 5 minutes. The flow gets stronger when the rain picks up and slows down as the rain eases. Once the rain stops completely, the water also stops flowing after some time. After a video of the handpump went viral on social media, it became a subject of curiosity in the surrounding area. However, the handpump is not faulty. On normal days, it works like any other handpump, with water flowing when it is operated. Workers at the nearby salt factory also collect drinking water from it. Villagers say the same thing happens every year during the rainy season. Two handpumps have been installed outside Magrasa village in Bidhnu block, about 25 kilometres from the city and around 100 metres from a salt factory. While one supplies water when operated normally, the other has been producing water on its own. The second handpump has been continuously releasing water for about a month since the rains began. Patri, a labourer from Nyori who has been working at the salt factory for around 10 years, said the handpump starts producing water on its own as soon as the rains begin. According to him, the same thing happens every year during the monsoon. After producing water for about two months, the handpump automatically stops when the rainy season ends. The flow increases during heavy rain and stops when the rain subsides The handpump has been producing water this year as well since the rains began. At the site, its flow was measured at around 2 litres in 5 minutes. According to the labourers, the flow increases when the rain becomes heavy and decreases when the rain slows down. The water stops flowing some time after the rain ends. Because of this, villagers are linking the phenomenon to nearby water sources and underground water pressure. Pandu River 1 km away, Ramaipur drain 700 metres away The Pandu River is located in Bingawan village, about 1 kilometre from the handpump. The Ramaipur drain is also around 700 metres away. Both the river and the drain are overflowing due to continuous rain. Villagers believe that the rising water levels in the river and drain may be increasing underground water pressure in the surrounding area. They speculate that this could be causing water to rise on its own from the 110-foot-deep handpump. However, there is no technical confirmation yet that the handpump water is directly connected to the river or drain. Junior engineer says check valve may be faulty Abhishek, a junior engineer with the Minor Irrigation Department in Bidhnu, said the handpump's check valve may be faulty. He said that if the water flow in the area is high, increased underground pressure could force water to rise through the handpump on its own. He added that this could happen if the flow of water around the area increases during rainfall. However, the exact reason for the water coming out of the handpump will be known only after a technical investigation. Some call it a miracle, while others say it is a natural process The handpump producing water on its own has become a topic of discussion in the village. While some people are calling it a miracle, others believe it is a natural process linked to rainfall, groundwater levels and underground water pressure. For now, the flow of water from the handpump clearly changes with the intensity of the rain. The water also stops some time after the rain ends. A technical investigation will determine how the water is rising through the 110-foot-deep handpump and what is causing the phenomenon.

stories.summary: BJP announced candidates for six Uttar Pradesh MLC seats on Tuesday. Employee leader Hari Kishore Tiwari has been fielded from the Agra Graduate seat. Dhruv Kumar Tripathi has been named the candidate for the Faizabad-Gorakhpur Teacher seat. Tripathi has not yet joined the BJP. Pramod Mishra has been fielded from the Kashi Teacher seat and Kedarnath Singh from the Graduate seat. Dinesh Goyal has been named the candidate from the Meerut Graduate seat. BJP had already announced candidates for five Teacher and Graduate MLC seats. All five are sitting MLCs. With this, the BJP has now fielded candidates for all 11 seats. Of the 11 candidates, five are from the Brahmin community. Voting for the 11 MLC seats will be held on October 23, with results due on October 27. The BJP currently holds eight of these seats, while the SP has three. The SP has also announced candidates for all 11 seats.

stories.title: Revenge for father’s murder after 21 years:Two brothers and uncle hack killer to death with sickles
stories.summary: Two brothers and their uncle hacked their neighbour to death with a billhook in Pilibhit, 21 years after he allegedly killed their father. The three surrounded Vedram, 48, while he was out for a morning walk in the village at around 5 am on Tuesday and repeatedly attacked him on the head. He collapsed in a pool of blood, while the attackers fled. The incident took place under Puranpur police station, around 55 km from the district headquarters. Police said Vedram had killed his neighbour Nandram in 2005 and was sentenced to five years in prison. The dispute between the two families continued even after his release in 2012. Police said the old feud was behind Vedram’s murder. The two brothers have been arrested, while their uncle remains absconding. Now read the full case in detail... Ved Ram (48), a resident of Bilhari village, was a farmer. His family comprises his wife, Madhuri Devi, two daughters, Pushpa and Anita, and a son, Saurabh. His elder daughter, Pushpa, is married. Ved Ram was the second eldest of four brothers. Nand Ram's house is around 400 metres from his. Murder took place in 2005 over a dispute concerning a garbage heap In 2005, Ved Ram had an argument with Nand Ram over a dispute concerning a garbage heap. In anger, Ved Ram killed Nand Ram. A case was registered against eight people, including Ved Ram, in connection with the murder. After serving a five-year sentence for the murder, Ved Ram was released from jail in 2012. Revenge for father's murder after 21 years Nandram's family had been waiting for an opportunity to take revenge ever since Vedram was released from prison. Nandram had two sons, Ramdev (28) and Shyamdev (27), and one brother, Sridev (50). At around 5 a.m. on Tuesday, Vedram went out for his daily walk. It is alleged that as soon as he reached the front of Nandram's house, the three brothers, who were already present there, surrounded him after finding him alone. Accused of launching a flurry of blows with a banke According to information, before Vedaram could understand what was happening, the three brothers repeatedly struck him on the head and body with a banka. He fell to the ground in a pool of blood after suffering serious injuries. The accused then fled the scene. Fear and shock spread across the village The incident sent shockwaves through the village. The family was devastated. Villagers informed the police. ASP Himanshu Gaurav reached the scene and inspected the site. The police took the body into custody and sent it for a post-mortem examination. The family members have submitted a complaint against 8 people. Police have taken Ramdev and Shyamdev into custody. The other named accused, including the third accused, Sridev, are being searched for. Puranpur Circle Officer Vidhi Bhushan Maurya said: “The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination. The allegation is that the murder was committed over an old enmity. A team has been deployed to investigate the case. The accused will be arrested soon and the case will be solved.”

stories.title: Gas cylinder blast kills 5, including 4 brothers:2 nearby houses collapse, cracks appear in 15 homes; neighbours say, 'It felt like a bomb blast'
stories.summary: Five people have died so far in a gas cylinder blast in Fatehpur, Uttar Pradesh. The two-storey house of fruit vendor Suresh Gupta in Malwan town collapsed after two cylinders exploded. Suresh and four members of his family died in the incident, while three people were injured. The incident took place at around 5 p.m. on Monday, about 20 kilometres from the district headquarters. A fire broke out in the house while food was being cooked. The women in the family ran outside screaming. The two filled gas cylinders kept inside the house then exploded with a loud blast. The blast was so powerful that people in the surrounding area felt an earthquake-like tremor up to about 200 metres away. Two neighbouring houses also collapsed. Fortunately, no one was inside either house at the time of the incident. Ten to 12 other houses in the vicinity were also damaged. A total of four gas cylinders were kept in the house at the time of the incident. Two were empty and two were filled. According to preliminary information, gas may have leaked from one of the cylinders. However, this has not yet been confirmed. District Fire Officer Jasveer Singh said an investigation was under way to determine which gas agency the cylinders belonged to. Three pictures of the accident... Eight people trapped under the debris pulled out A team of 16 police and fire brigade personnel reached the spot after being informed. As the house was located in a narrow lane, the fire brigade vehicle could not reach the site. The debris-clearing operation was then begun with the help of bulldozers and JCB machines. With the help of local residents, the police and fire brigade teams pulled eight people out from under the debris and took them to the Medical College. Suresh's sons Kunal (19), Ved (14), Yash (8) and Arpit (15) and his nephews died at the medical college. His nephew Alok Gupta (23) succumbed to his injuries at around 9:30 p.m. late at night. He had suffered burns over around 90% of his body. Suresh Gupta (50), his nephew Om (7) and niece Shivani (23) were injured in the incident. SDRF team arrives from Lucknow After the accident, an SDRF team arrived at the site from Lucknow late at night. The team helped remove the debris and in the rescue operation. Raised platforms outside several houses were demolished to bring the JCB to the site. It has also emerged that around 15 houses in the vicinity developed cracks due to the blast. Two neighbouring houses completely collapsed In the blast, the houses of Suresh Gupta's neighbours, Mahesh Singh and Pradeep Singh, also completely collapsed. Meanwhile, the walls of Anmol Singh's and Roopa Singh's houses fell. At the time of the accident, the members of Mahesh and Pradeep's families were outside the houses, averting a major tragedy. Boundary wall collapsed up to 200 metres away Navin Shukla, a resident of Malwan town, said Suresh Gupta's house is in a lane about 100 metres from the highway. The blast damaged 10 to 12 houses in the surrounding area. The roofs and concrete slabs of several houses were damaged, while some houses collapsed completely. A boundary wall also collapsed up to 200 metres from the house. Neighbour Mahesh Singh said the blast was so powerful that it sounded as though a large bomb had exploded. Before people could understand what had happened, Suresh Gupta and his house had been caught in the blast. The area is gripped by panic following the incident. Police, fire brigade and SDRF teams are engaged in relief and rescue operations. See 2 more pictures... SP Abhimanyu Manglik said- Seven people were pulled from the debris. Four of them died at the hospital shortly afterwards. One person had suffered burns over more than 90% of his body. He succumbed during the night. Two people, including the landlord, Suresh, are undergoing treatment. The debris is being cleared. The accident is being investigated.

stories.title: 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment candidates protest in Lucknow:Gherao Rajbhar’s home, chant ‘Rajbhar uncle, do justice’; clash with police
stories.summary: Candidates from the 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment protested for the second consecutive day in Lucknow on Tuesday. They surrounded the residence of Cabinet Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar, sat outside his house, and raised slogans, “Rajbhar chacha, nyay karo.” They protested for around 30 minutes, demanding appointments. There was also a scuffle between the police and protesters. Police tried to remove them from the spot. The protesters alleged that police forcibly removed them and sent them to Eco Garden. They also accused the police of misbehaviour and tearing their clothes. The protesters raised slogans such as, “What is the compulsion? It is reservation theft” and “The Backward Classes Commission has accepted it; there is a reservation scam.” During the protest, Om Prakash Rajbhar invited the candidates for talks and met them. The candidates are demanding appointments under the 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment. Photos:- ‘Ministers, officials admitted there was a scam’ Naveen, who participated in the protest, said the candidates had met Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh and Secondary Education Minister Gulab Devi on 10th September. Several officials from both departments were also present. He claimed that the ministers and officials admitted during the meeting that there had been irregularities in the recruitment process. He said the State Backward Classes Commission and the National Commission for Backward Classes had also acknowledged the issue. “Now the government’s ministers and officials are accepting it too. Despite this, why are the candidates still not being given jobs?” he asked. ‘We have worn out our slippers for 8 years’ Ashutosh Verma said the protest would continue until the recruitment schedule is released. “We have been waiting for jobs for the past 8 years,” he said. He alleged large-scale reservation irregularities in the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers. The state and national backward classes commissions have also acknowledged irregularities in reservation and directed that the rules be followed. Ashutosh said the candidates want these orders to be implemented. The recruitment was announced in 2018, and they had applied then. “For the past eight years, we have been wearing out our slippers in the hope of getting jobs,” he said. ‘Demand 5% relaxation in qualifying marks’ According to the protesters, the 68,500 assistant teacher recruitment was announced in 2018, with a provision for 5% relaxation for candidates from the disabled, ex-servicemen, Scheduled Caste and Other Backward Class categories. They alleged that candidates from these four categories did not receive the benefit and the results were released using the same criteria as for general candidates. The candidates are demanding a 5% relaxation in the qualifying marks. They want the result revised and a fresh selection list issued, with 60 marks, or 40% of the 150-mark exam, treated as the qualifying score.

stories.title: SC quashes NSA detention of Sambhal violence accused:Imposes ₹10 lakh cost on Yogi government in UP
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that a confession statement made by an accused cannot, by itself, be used as the basis for preventive detention under the National Security Act (NSA). A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu delivered the ruling while quashing the detention of Mulla Afroz, who had been detained by Uttar Pradesh Police under the NSA in connection with the 2024 communal violence in Sambhal. The court also imposed a ₹10 lakh cost on the government, holding that the preventive detention order was illegal. NSA detention challenged before Supreme Court Uttar Pradesh authorities invoked the NSA against Afroz in October 2025, citing his alleged role in the Sambhal violence. The Supreme Court's ruling means that a confession statement cannot independently provide the legal foundation for detaining a person under the stringent preventive-detention law. A detailed copy of Tuesday's judgment is awaited. While delivering the verdict, Justice Dipankar Datta also paid tribute to his law clerk, who died four days before his 27th birthday. What does the National Security Act allow? The NSA allows the Centre and state governments to order preventive detention when authorities believe an individual may act in a manner considered "prejudicial to the defence of India". Unlike ordinary criminal arrest, preventive detention is intended to prevent a potential future threat rather than punish a person for an offence already committed. A detention order can remain in force for a maximum of 12 months, although it can be revoked before that period. The law allows the local administration to invoke preventive detention, subject to review and ratification by an advisory board headed by a former High Court judge. Since NSA detention is preventive rather than a conventional arrest, the detainee is not required to be produced before a court in the same manner as a person arrested in a criminal case. Sambhal violence forms backdrop The case stems from tensions that erupted in Sambhal, Uttar Pradesh, in November 2024 during a court-ordered survey of the Shahi Jama Masjid. The survey was being conducted following claims that a Harihar temple had previously stood at the site. The situation escalated on November 24, when a second round of the survey triggered clashes between protesting locals and security personnel. The violence resulted in the deaths of four people, while dozens of others were injured. Afroz was subsequently booked under the NSA in October 2025 over his alleged involvement in the violence. Preventive detention faces judicial scrutiny The Supreme Court's decision places the focus on the evidentiary basis required when authorities use preventive-detention powers under the NSA. The court's intervention came as it examined the legality of Afroz's detention rather than merely the allegations surrounding the Sambhal violence. By quashing the detention order and imposing a ₹10 lakh cost on the government, the Bench has also set aside the preventive action taken against him. Kunal Kamra moves SC over legislative privilege Comedian Kunal Kamra has approached the Supreme Court seeking to intervene in a case before its seven-judge Bench that examines how far legislative privilege can extend when it comes into conflict with a citizen’s right to freedom of speech. Kamra has sought permission to become a party to N Ravi and ors v. Speaker, Legislative Assembly, Chennai, in which the court is examining the relationship between legislative privileges and fundamental rights, including freedom of speech and the right to life and personal liberty. Maharashtra privilege proceedings prompt plea Kamra’s intervention plea comes against the backdrop of breach of privilege proceedings initiated against him by the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly over a satirical song performed during his comedy show ‘Naya Bharat’. The performance referred to the 2022 split in the Shiv Sena, a political development that resulted in the resignation of then Maharashtra Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray and the subsequent formation of a new state government led by Eknath Shinde. Kamra’s song reportedly referred to Shinde as ‘Gaddar’ (traitor). The performance subsequently became the subject of privilege proceedings in the Maharashtra Assembly, with allegations that Kamra had disrespected and insulted the then chief minister.

stories.title: Congress workers protest in Gorakhpur:Cops beaten while stopping effigy burning; FIR against party workers, one arrested
stories.summary: Police attempted to stop Congress workers from burning an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner during a protest in Gorakhpur on Monday. This led to heated exchanges and clashes with the workers for quite some time. It is alleged that during the incident, some Congress workers, angered by the situation, forcibly grabbed the sub-inspector deployed on duty and assaulted him. Acting on a complaint filed by Cantt Sub-Inspector Vinod Singh, police registered a case late at night against Congress workers Munna Shahi, Kodai Tiwari and unidentified persons on charges of assault and obstructing government work. Police detained one of the accused, Munna Shahi. He was brought to the police station and is being questioned. Congress workers, however, said they were holding a peaceful protest, which was their democratic right. They alleged that the police behaved very poorly and that the action was taken to please the Chief Minister. See 3 pictures... Read the full story... Congress workers staged a strong protest in Gorakhpur on Monday following discussions across the country about irregularities in the Election Commission's functioning. At around 12 p.m., hundreds of workers gathered at Ram Prasad Bismil Park. Together, they raised slogans against the government and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They reached the DM's office while taking out a march. They tried to burn an effigy of Gyanesh Kumar to register their protest. They also demanded that the President resign. However, whenever the workers tried to set the effigy on fire during the protest, the police tried to stop them. A heated exchange and scuffle also broke out between them as the police tried to snatch the effigy from the workers. During the incident, one worker pushed Sub-Inspector Vinod several times, forcing him back, while other workers accompanying him held the officer from behind. They then proceeded to burn the effigy. The incident has caused a stir in the police department. The worker accused in the incident is being searched for. This is police anarchy and dictatorship-district president District president Rajesh Tiwari said that this was complete anarchy and dictatorship by the police. It was a direct conspiracy to destroy the democratic process. Effigies were burnt everywhere across the state. He said, "We did not engage in any misbehaviour, disorder or hooliganism. We are followers of Gandhi. We believe in democratic values. We were protesting peacefully. But the police's conduct was very poor." He further said, "We were neither burning an effigy of the Prime Minister nor that of the Chief Minister, so what did the police object to? What have these people got to do with the Election Commissioner? All this was done because the Chief Minister was in the city. If they had been Samajwadi Party workers, they would have beaten them up and taken them away."

stories.title: ₹4.5 lakh cash, 65.8g jewellery stolen from Varanasi medical store:Thieves broke wall from railway track side to enter
stories.summary: Thieves broke into Ajay Medical near the western end of Shivpur railway crossing in Varanasi on Monday night and fled with ₹4.50 lakh in cash and around 65.8 grams of gold jewellery kept in a steel trunk. They broke through the wall at the back of the shop, on the side facing the railway track, to enter. The shop operator found the wall broken when he arrived on Tuesday morning, after which the police were informed. Thieves broke through the rear wall to enter the shop Ajay Kumar Verma, a resident of Tewar (Baraicha) village in the Cholapur police station area, lives in a rented house in Bhawanipur in the Shivpur police station area. He runs a shop named Ajay Medical near Shivpur railway crossing. According to Ajay, his rented house in Bhawanipur had been burgled before. That is why he kept the cash and gold jewellery from his home in a steel trunk at the shop. On Monday night, thieves broke through the wall at the back of the shop, on the side facing the railway track, and entered. They then stole the cash and jewellery kept in the trunk and fled. Four chains and three rings stolen According to Ajay, the thieves took four gold chains along with ₹4.50 lakh in cash kept in the trunk. The four chains are said to have had a combined weight of around 50.5 grams. In addition, three gold rings were stolen, with a combined weight of around 15.3 grams. In total, around 65.8 grams of gold jewellery was stolen. Case came to light when he reached shop at 5 a.m. Ajay reached the shop at around 5 a.m. on Tuesday to open it. He discovered the theft after seeing that the wall at the back had been broken. Items were scattered inside the shop, and the cash and jewellery were missing from the steel trunk. After seeing the scene inside, he informed the police and submitted a written complaint. Police examining CCTV footage After receiving the information, Shivpur police reached the spot and inspected the scene. Footage from CCTV cameras installed nearby is also being examined. According to the police, an investigation is underway to identify the thieves. A case will be registered based on the complaint, and necessary action will be taken.

stories.title: Kashi royal family’s elephant breaks chains, jumps into pond:Screams in anger over delayed food; comes out after mahouts persuade it for hours
stories.summary: A royal family’s elephant, Dhanraj, broke his chains and jumped into a nearby pond after getting agitated over a delay in his food on Monday morning. The elephant had come to take part in the world-famous Ramnagar Ramleela. His sudden entry into Pampasar pond caused panic among people bathing there. As soon as they received the information, the mahouts reached the spot and, after several hours of coaxing, managed to bring the elephant out. Every year, four elephants are brought from Jiyanpur in Azamgarh to Ramnagar for the Ramleela. The elephants stay with their mahouts in an open garden at Panchvati Ground. On Monday morning, Dhanraj, one of the elephants, reportedly became angry after he did not receive his food on time. At around 11:30 a.m., he broke his chains and entered the nearby Pampasar pond. As soon as Dhanraj entered the pond, panic spread among the people present there. Within a short time, a large crowd gathered at the spot to see the elephant. After receiving the information, other mahouts, including chief mahout Israel, also reached the pond. They tried to bring Dhanraj out and calm him, but he refused to leave the pond for several hours. The mahouts tried to coax him out by showing him tree branches to eat from a distance. After several hours of efforts, Dhanraj finally came out of the pond at around 4 p.m. He was fed soon after coming out. The mahouts then calmed him and kept a close watch on his behaviour and condition. Special Connection With the Kashi Royal Family Dhanraj is also said to have a special connection with the Kashi royal family. For nearly six years, Anant Narayan Singh of the Kashi royal family has watched Ramnagar’s Ramleela while sitting on Dhanraj’s back. Because of this, news of Dhanraj becoming upset and entering the pond during the Ramleela caused concern among those involved in organising the event. After the mahouts calmed Dhanraj and he returned to his normal behaviour, he was taken back to the Ramleela venue. A large crowd remained gathered around the Pampasar pond for some time during the incident.

stories.title: ‘Over 8,500 heart attack patients saved every year’:Lari Cardiology doctor says medication and follow-up are crucial; 25 cases reported daily
stories.summary: Around 25 heart attack patients reach the Lari Cardiology Centre at KGMU in Lucknow every day. About 95% of them recover after treatment and return home. Between 150 and 200 patients visit the emergency department at Lari Cardiology every day. Of these, 35 to 40 are in serious condition and are admitted. Around 9,000 heart attack patients are treated here every year. On the occasion of World Heart Day, Dainik Bhaskar spoke exclusively to Dr Rishi Sethi, head of the Lari Cardiology Centre. He said that it is extremely important for heart attack patients to reach hospital on time and for treatment to begin immediately. Read key excerpts from the conversation with Dr Rishi Sethi... More than 8,500 heart attack patients receive a new lease of life here every year According to Dr Sethi, more than 8,500 heart attack patients are treated at Lari Cardiology every year. After treatment, most patients are called for regular follow-ups so that their health can be monitored and they can lead normal lives. He says that more than half of the patients who survive a heart attack can lead normal lives for several decades. For this, it is essential that patients continue taking their medicines as advised by their doctors and undergo regular check-ups. Now focus on the age of your heart, not your age since birth Dr Rishi Sethi said that we determine our age from our date of birth, but every organ in the body has its own age. For a long and healthy life, it is most important to keep the heart and arteries healthy. Their health has a direct impact on our life expectancy. He said that, besides the heart and arteries, hormones, the liver and the brain also have different ages. Therefore, it is essential to take care of the health of every organ in the body. His former teacher used to say, "We are only as old as our heart." Risk of blockages rising at a young age According to Dr Sethi, stress, working for hours on screens and eating outside are harming heart health. Cases of blockages in the heart arteries are now being reported even among younger people. He said that a few years ago, younger patients generally had blockages in one or two arteries. Now, more than one artery is being found to be affected in many patients. Angioplasty may be required in such cases. Patients with high blood pressure and diabetes face a higher risk of heart-related complications. Therefore, it is essential to take medicines as advised by a doctor, undergo regular check-ups, and look after heart health. Tips for keeping your heart healthy Walk every day: Walk and do light exercise daily. Avoid suddenly undertaking strenuous physical activity. Watch what you eat: Increase your intake of fruit, vegetables, whole grains and pulses. Cut down on salt, sugar, oil, and highly processed food. Get enough sleep: Seven to eight hours of sleep every day is essential. Try to reduce stress and maintain a regular routine. Get regular check-ups: Have your blood pressure, blood sugar, and cholesterol checked from time to time. Stay away from tobacco: Do not smoke cigarettes or bidis, consume gutka, or use tobacco in any form. Do not take supplements without medical advice: Steroids, fat burners, and some supplements can affect heart rate and blood pressure. Do not take them without a doctor's advice.

stories.title: ‘Haven’t seen my son’s face for 2 years’:Mother says Premanand Maharaj’s ashram turned her away 10 times; ‘Now they gave me his body'
stories.summary: I had not seen my son’s face for two years. Now they have given me his body. My family’s light has gone out. These were the words of Uma Patel, mother of 27-year-old Deepak alias Rasik Dulari Sharan from Parswada in Jabalpur, who died after falling from the fourth floor of an Ashram associated with Spiritual leader Premanand Maharaj in Vrindavan on Friday morning. The family has described the circumstances of his death as suspicious and has demanded a high-level and impartial investigation. According to his mother, the family visited Vrindavan more than 10 times over two years but was allegedly turned away from the Ashram gate each time. They were reportedly told on different occasions that Deepak did not live there or was busy with Sewa. The family also claims that after his death, they spent hours trying to find out which hospital he had been taken to and where his body had been kept. Deepak wanted to join Army, later became devoted to spirituality After completing his BA, Deepak had prepared to join the Army. He cleared the written examination and running test but could not clear the physical test. After this, his interest in spirituality increased. He became actively involved in bhajans and religious programmes in his village. In 2023, he joined a service group associated with Bhaiyyaji Sarkar Dada Guru’s Narmada Parikrama. He returned to Jabalpur after around eight months, and his family noticed changes in his behaviour. He began repeatedly expressing a desire to go to Vrindavan. Despite his family’s reservations, he left for Vrindavan without informing them in February 2024 and began staying at the ashram. Family says it respected his decision After some time, Deepak called his parents and told them that he wanted to receive guru diksha. He reportedly told them that he did not feel comfortable living in Jabalpur and wanted to serve at the ashram. The family said it respected his decision and agreed to his wish to receive spiritual initiation. Deepak later returned to Jabalpur for a short period, but his contact with the family gradually reduced. He did not usually have a mobile phone, and the family said they lost contact with him completely after around four months. In July 2024, his parents and younger brother travelled to Vrindavan, but the family claims they were not allowed to meet him. More than 17 family members visited, but could not meet him The family says it subsequently visited Vrindavan more than 10 times, but was turned away from the ashram gate on every occasion. In June 2026, more than 17 relatives travelled to Vrindavan together. Despite this, they were allegedly unable to meet Deepak. The family later learnt that Deepak was known at the ashram as ‘Rasik Dulari Sharan’. They said they do not know when or how his name was changed. Family says it struggled to locate hospital after death At around 3 pm on Friday, the family received a phone call informing them that Deepak had suffered an accident and had fallen from the roof. The relatives then left for Vrindavan. The family alleges that after reaching the city, they struggled to find out which hospital Deepak had been taken to and where his body had been kept. They said they spent several hours around the ashram trying to obtain information. They eventually found Deepak’s body at a hospital. According to the family, they were initially told only that an accident had occurred and that he was undergoing treatment. They allege that had they not travelled to Vrindavan themselves, they might not have received information about his death and body. Family raises questions over circumstances of death Deepak’s brother-in-law, Sonu Patel, questioned how Deepak was able to reach the fourth floor of an ashram where many people stay and why his fall was allegedly not noticed immediately. The family has also raised questions about an incident shortly before his death involving a grinder. They want investigators to establish what happened in the room before the incident and whether anyone else was present. The family also claims that a video shown to them by the ashram appeared to have been edited. They have demanded an independent examination of the footage. Family claims another woman died after falling from Ashram Deepak’s younger brother Manish claimed that a woman had died a few months earlier after falling from the ninth floor of the ashram. Manish said he had heard from people that the woman had been experiencing mental health problems. This claim has not been independently verified. Family seeks high-level investigation The family says Deepak had chosen a spiritual life and that they had respected his decision. They now want a high-level and impartial investigation into the circumstances of his death, the people present at the time and his activities at the ashram. Questions raised over events before death The family has also raised questions about Deepak’s condition in the days before his death. They said he had reportedly injured himself before the incident and was taken to a hospital for treatment before returning to the ashram. The family wants investigators to establish the circumstances surrounding the injuries, whether they were connected to his subsequent death and whether he received appropriate medical care. They have also questioned why the police were allegedly informed only later, if the hospital determined that Deepak had already died when he was brought there. Police say CCTV captured the fall Police have reportedly said that CCTV footage shows Deepak falling from the building. However, the footage has not been made public so far. The family is seeking an independent examination of the CCTV footage and other evidence to establish exactly what happened before Deepak’s death. Several questions therefore remain unanswered, including what led to the incident, who was present at the time and whether the available CCTV and other evidence can establish the sequence of events. An investigation is expected to determine the circumstances of his death.

stories.title: Hanuman Chalisa recitation announced outside Meerut mosque:100 cops deployed, PAC called in; police urge residents to stay indoors
stories.summary: Hindu groups announced a Hanuman Chalisa recitation outside a mosque in Meerut on Tuesday, following which police stepped up security in the area. More than 100 police personnel from five police stations have been deployed, and PAC has also been called in. Barricades have been put up on roads leading to Kesarganj Mosque. Police are allowing people to enter only after checking their IDs. Announcements are being made over loudspeakers asking people to stay indoors, while nearby shops have been closed. The mosque is located in Kesarganj Mandi under Sadar police station. The mosque committee was carrying out construction work on the upper floor. On 10 September, traders protested, alleging that the construction was illegal. Police reached the spot and stopped the work. The traders demanded an inquiry into the mosque and surrounding construction. The mosque committee, however, rejected the allegations and said the mosque is a historical heritage site. On 13 September, MP Arun Govil wrote to the district magistrate seeking an inquiry. On 28 September, Hindu Raksha Dal national president Pinky Chaudhary and Lalit Sharma from Ghaziabad announced that they would hold the Hanuman Chalisa recitation outside the mosque on Tuesday. See 3 pictures… SP City Vinayak Gopal Bhosle said- Additional police personnel have been deployed outside the mosque, and patrolling in the area has been intensified. The police are monitoring local activities as well as social media content. The police's priority is to maintain law and order, and no one will be allowed to take the law into their own hands. The police have appealed to local residents to maintain peace. They have also asked people not to pay heed to any unverified information or rumours and to co-operate in maintaining peace in the area. Meerut mosque dispute: What has happened so far The dispute began over construction on the upper floor of the Kesarganj mosque. Traders objected, alleging construction without permission. Police later stopped the work.

stories.title: Government school principal and wife murdered in Sultanpur:Bloodstained bodies found at school, crime carried out with spade and axe
stories.summary: A government school principal and his wife were murdered in Sultanpur. Their bloodstained bodies were found on the premises of their private school. They had been attacked with a spade and an axe. The incident came to light at 7 a.m. on Tuesday, when the school driver arrived to collect the vehicle keys. Principal Mukesh Singh (45) was also the president of the Block Teachers' Association. He was contesting the teachers' association election this time as well. Voting was scheduled for 30 September, but the election was postponed on 28 September, two days earlier. The incident took place in Kumbhi Dadiya village, under the Kadipur police station area, 55 km from the district headquarters. The principal's wife, Vinita (43), ran the private school. She had also contested the previous district panchayat election. Their house was 1 km from the school. The principal was posted at the composite school in Khanuhat. After receiving information about the incident, Superintendent of Police Vineet Jaiswal and Kadipur Circle Officer Vinay Gautam arrived with a police force. Bodies of the husband and wife were found 150 metres apart Mukesh Singh was living with his wife, Vinita Singh, in Kumbhi Dadiya village. Their only son, Abhyaduy (20), is studying at Delhi University. Vinita was running Manragi Inter College from her home, 1 km from the village. The school has around 18 teachers and staff members. Approximately 500 children study at the school. When the school van driver arrived on Tuesday morning, he saw Vinita's body in a room at the school. A bloodstained spade was lying nearby. The driver raised the alarm, prompting people to reach the spot. They found Mukesh's body lying 150 metres from Vinita's body. The SP and CO reached the spot after being informed of the incident. A spade, an axe and a knife were recovered from the scene. Father was a farmer, elder brother a government teacher, and younger brother a bank employee Mukesh's father, Ram Badan Singh, was a farmer. The family owns around 35 bighas of ancestral land. Mukesh was the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother, Awadhesh Singh, is a teacher at PG College, Ghazipur. His other brother, Akhilesh Singh, works at Lucknow Cooperative Bank. Mukesh was previously a Shikshamitra. He became an assistant teacher in 2009 and has been the teachers' union president in Motigarpur since 2013. His wife, Vinita Singh, opened the Manraji Shikshan Sansthan in the village in 2002. Police are also questioning the teachers and employees who work at the school. Police investigating these 2 angles Superintendent of Police Vineet Jaiswal said: "We received information this morning that the bodies of a husband and wife had been found. Our field unit team is also present at the spot. Several teams have been formed and are continuously working on the case. The family members have also been contacted. The incident will be solved soon."

stories.title: Former IAS Divya Mittal enters UP politics:Says, ‘I won’t be afraid, will seek answers; need your support, not any party’s’
stories.summary: Former UP IAS officer Divya Mittal to enter politics. She announced this in a video posted on Facebook at 8.30 am on Tuesday. She said, “I will stay in UP. I won’t be afraid; I will ask questions. I don’t want muscle power. Please support me.” A 2013-batch IAS officer, Divya resigned from the service on August 30. Her resignation was accepted on September 14. Since then, there has been speculation about her future plans. After completing a BTech from IIT Delhi and an MBA from IIM Bengaluru, Divya worked in London at a job with a salary package worth lakhs. Divya announces political entry: “Read exactly what she said” “Hello, I am Divya Mittal! A few days ago, I resigned from the IAS, leaving many questions in your minds. I did not answer for a few days because the task ahead was big and I was gathering the courage. But today, I have come to answer those questions. What next? With whom and from where? First question: What next? Politics! People told me, ‘You have already achieved everything; what more do you want to become?’ I want to become a voice, the voice of those whose voices cannot reach any government office, and even if they do, are not heard. On their behalf, I want accountability for the 80 years since our country’s Independence. Once, I was inspecting work to bring water to Lahuriyadah hill. A woman started walking towards me. I thought she might need something, perhaps a pension or a permanent house. She came up to me and said, ‘Madam, I want to ask you for something.’ What she asked made me bow my head in shame. She said, ‘Madam, our village has a school only up to Class 5. After that, our children’s education ends amid the forests and hills. I want a school in my village up to the next level of classes.’ At that time, the woman’s own house did not even have water, yet she asked for a school. I checked the rules and got the school approved. Even after three years, construction of that school has not begun. Now tell me, what was missing? Was it money, rules, or approval? There was simply no intent. If there had been intent, even the mountains would have made way. When there is no intent, even a file becomes a mountain. I want accountability for those missing schools.” “I was Special Secretary, Revenue, when a man came to me with his papers and hopes wrapped in a plastic bag. He told me, ‘Madam, I was landless. A few years ago, an SDM leased a small piece of government land to me. I got the papers, but I did not get possession of the land.’ I checked his papers and found that the report was completely false. So I spoke to the officer concerned in the district. He admitted that the report was wrong. The report was withdrawn, and action was also taken against the person who prepared it. Then came the issue of giving him possession. I called twice and had it followed up three times, but the response was, ‘We have been told not to do it from above.’ Who is this ‘above’? The Constitution says that the people are at the top. So why does a person have to run from pillar to post for justice? What is given from above may be a favour. Justice is a right. So I want accountability for the injustices wrapped in those plastic bags. There are thousands of villages that still have no roads. Where there is a river, there is no bridge. During the rains, villages become islands, and people have been waiting for generations. And where there is a road, there are so many potholes that the mud splashed onto the tiny feet of children walking to school does not even reach their white clothes. When a motorcyclist falls into the same pothole, even the splashes of blood do not reach their clothes. It is not that they do not have information. They know where the pothole is, what the file number is, and how many deaths have occurred. What is missing is concern. And when there is no concern, a death is not an accident, but a decision. I want accountability for those deaths. I was a girl from an ordinary family. This country had promised me that ‘if you study, you will progress’. I studied, and today I am standing before you. But what is the promise to children today? They study all night, only for the exam paper to be leaked. Prepare for five years, and then the decision ends up in court. And the question of the future is even bigger. A farmer is mortgaging his land to educate his son as an engineer, or a mother is selling her jewellery to teach her daughter coding. Do they know whether their future is secure?” AI is coming, and many jobs will be taken over by it. This worries every young person. I am a mother of two young daughters, and I worry about their future too. No one has all the answers, but at least we should be asking questions and thinking about the future our children are heading towards. Today, politics has everything: power, inaugurations, and noise, but no thought. I want accountability for this lack of thought. The aim is not just to replace one politician; politics itself needs to change, towards intent, justice, concern, and long-term thinking. Politics should not treat people as numbers or use them as stepping stones to power. It should listen to people, because people are the destination. If people are the destination, the path to them must go through the people, not through any political flag. That is why I will enter politics without joining any party, but with the people. The question is whether ordinary, honest people can enter politics. I got my answer within hours of resigning. While many ordinary people supported me, a state spokesperson of a major party claimed that I had secretly met a senior leader of another major party. The meeting never happened, and the person who made the claim knew that. The aim, she said, was to intimidate a woman who had stepped forward to ask questions by threatening people with FIRs or silencing them through trolling, so that ordinary and honest people stay away from politics. “This is what we need to change.” So, I will not be afraid; I will keep asking questions, so that every girl in the country can speak her mind without being made to fear the darkness. Together with those who supported me, we will build a platform that fears no one, but fears only for the country’s future. The question is: there is no fear, but there is no money, muscle power, or caste-religion equation either. That is true. But where does the money spent in elections come from? It comes from our roads, bridges, and schools. I don’t want to spend that money; I want the road itself. I don’t want muscle power over people; I want the power of people, for the people and belonging to the people. When I was an officer, I never asked anyone’s identity before delivering justice. I won’t do that in politics either. How this politics will begin, take shape, and move forward, we will decide together. The third question: Where from? I came here as an officer, but the people made me their daughter. The soil of Uttar Pradesh taught me who I am and whom I am here for. UP is my karmabhoomi, so this journey will begin here. People say nothing changes in this country, especially in UP. But I know a country that proved its doubters wrong. UP has always shown the way. I have seen people across districts come together for what is right and achieve what even officials could not. We have waited 80 years for a leader or messiah, but no one came. Because the person we were waiting for is us. So I say: Don’t trust me; trust yourself. I am calling teachers, doctors, farmers, workers, lawyers, students, and every parent worried about their children’s future. New politics cannot be built by one person; everyone will have to contribute. One day, a person will go to a government office with his papers wrapped in a plastic bag and get his case heard without a recommendation or phone call. He will return home and tell his son, “Today, I got justice.” And his son will ask, “What’s new about that?” That is the day we want to work towards. Let’s demand accountability. After resignation was accepted, she wrote: “Keep moving forward” After her resignation was accepted, Divya Mittal wrote, “My resignation from the IAS has been accepted.” She also quoted lines from poet Jaishankar Prasad’s play Chandragupta: “Prashast punya panth hai, badhe chalo, badhe chalo”. The lines mean that the path of protecting and securing the motherland and its freedom is broad, clear, and sacred. Through “badhe chalo, badhe chalo”, the poet calls upon the nation’s brave sons and soldiers to keep moving forward on this sacred path without stopping or being afraid. Divya left her London job to join civil services Divya is originally from Rewari, Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she worked in London, where she met Gagandeep Singh. The two got married after dating. A few years later, they left their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC exam. Without coaching, she cleared the IPS exam on her first attempt and was allotted the Gujarat cadre. She continued preparing for the IAS exam during her IPS training. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya’s husband is from Punjab, cleared UPSC on his first attempt Divya’s husband, Gagandeep Singh, belongs to Gidderbaha in Bathinda district, Punjab. He studied Chemical Engineering at IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002, followed by management at IIM Bengaluru from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC exam on his first attempt in 2010 and was selected for the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned as Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
