stories.title: Class 10 topper found dead in Gorakhpur’s Chiluataal:Missing for 5 days, suspected murder over love affair; family stages protest
stories.summary: The decomposed body of 15-year-old high school topper Prince Nishad was found floating in Chilua Taal, Gorakhpur, on 28 September. Prince left for Momentum Coaching in Betiyahata on 23 September and went missing. He was preparing for the IIT entrance examination. The discovery of his body after a five-day search left the family devastated. The family has expressed suspicion that the student was murdered and demanded that the police investigate the case and take strict action against those responsible. The police took custody of the body and sent it to BRD Medical College for a post-mortem. A commotion continued there late into the night. Police personnel from the station arrived with senior officers and pacified the family. The investigation has also revealed that the murder was committed over a love affair with a girl. The police have detained the girl, her parents and her brother for questioning. Student had been missing since 23 September Prince Nishad, who lived with his family in a rented house in Moharipur, Chiluatal, had been missing since 23 September. After he suddenly disappeared, his father, Nand Kishore, filed a missing-person complaint at Chiluatal police station. Family members continued searching for him, but no clue was found for five days. Help sought from SSP after no clues emerged Father Nandkishore said that when there was no trace of Prince despite the complaint filed at the police station, he also sought help from the senior superintendent of police. The family had been continuously demanding that the police intensify the search for the student. Meanwhile, news of a body being found in the river on 28 September shattered the family's hopes. Body found floating in river near Mohripur A body was seen floating in the river near the Mohripur area on 28 September. On receiving the information, police reached the spot. They had the body taken out of the river and took it into custody. After the identification process was completed, the body was identified as that of Prince Nishad. Prince Was His Elder Sister's Only Brother and the School Topper Prince was his elder sister's only brother in the family. According to his relatives, he was also academically gifted and had been the school topper. The family had high hopes for him. After receiving the news of their son's death, his relatives are inconsolable. Body sent to BRD Medical College for post-mortem examination Police have sent the body to BRD Medical College for a post-mortem examination. The cause of death is expected to become clear after the post-mortem report. Police are investigating the facts related to the case, and further action will be taken based on the report. Father inconsolable outside the mortuary Outside the mortuary at BRD Medical College, Prince's father Nandkishore Nishad and other family members appeared grief-stricken. The family said that the circumstances surrounding Prince's death did not appear normal. They said they would submit a detailed complaint to the police after the post-mortem report was released. Family members demand strict action against those responsible Prince's family members, expressing suspicion of murder, have demanded a thorough investigation into the case. They said they would submit their complaint to the police after the post-mortem report was released. The family demanded that authorities identify those responsible and take strict legal action against them. The Chiluatal police station in-charge said that the student's body had been sent to the mortuary. It has emerged that the case is linked to a romantic relationship. Some people have been taken into custody for questioning. The cause of death will be known after the post-mortem report is released. Further action will be taken on the basis of the evidence.

stories.title: January-like fog in UP, swollen rivers, flooded highways:350-year-old shrine in Barabanki submerged; 100m road washed away in Badaun
stories.summary: UP is seeing January-like fog in September. Dense mist was reported in Amethi, Rampur and Badaun on Tuesday morning, reducing visibility to around 25 metres. People also felt a slight chill. Meteorologists said clear, sunny days followed by cooler nights and slow winds are causing moisture in the air to condense into tiny water droplets that settle near the ground. Meanwhile, the monsoon has begun withdrawing from UP. It has already retreated from parts of western UP, including Muzaffarnagar and Aligarh, bringing an end to heavy rain across the state. However, rivers remain swollen after four consecutive days of rain. In Bijnor, Ganga water has flooded a state highway, with vehicles passing through 3–4 feet of water. In Barabanki, a 350-year-old shrine has been submerged in the Saryu River. In Badaun, 100 metres of road was washed away by the strong flood current. Roads are also waterlogged in Kanpur. Sunshine appeared across the state, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj and Varanasi, from Tuesday morning. However, light rain is forecast in 17 districts. The weather department expects only scattered rain from now on, with clearer weather from October. See pictures of the rain and flooding... The impact of the rain will reduce significantly in 24 hours Manoj Srivastava, a meteorologist in Varanasi, said that the cyclone that originated in the Bay of Bengal had weakened after passing through Uttar Pradesh. The rain, which continued for four days, has now begun to subside. The impact of the rain will reduce significantly over the next 24 hours. Only the Terai areas adjoining the Nepal border will receive light rain. The weather will remain clear across the state at the beginning of October. There will be bright sunshine. stories.title: ₹4,000 crore land scam:PCS officer dismissed for allotting Noida land to private firms; action underway since 2013
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has dismissed senior PCS officer Harish Chandra from service. He is a 1997-batch PCS officer. He has been accused of being involved in an approximately ₹4,000 crore leaseback scam during his posting at the Noida Development Authority. M. Devaraj, Principal Secretary, Appointment and Personnel, issued the order for his dismissal. Harish Chandra was currently posted in Kolkata, West Bengal, as the local representative of the Food and Logistics Department. Disciplinary proceedings against him had been under way since 2013. The government decided to dismiss him after a departmental inquiry and approval from the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission. Leaseback of land in violation of rules in 2011 Harish Chandra was the secretary of the Noida Authority in 2011-12. He is accused of arranging the leaseback, in violation of the rules, of around 3.81 lakh square metres of land in Shahdara village during that period. The land was located around Sectors 140A, 141, 142 and 143. Under the rules, the leaseback facility could be granted only to eligible villagers, and the maximum limit for a family was 450 square metres of land. The investigation alleged that large plots were also leased back to outsiders and private companies. According to the investigation, the market value of this land was around ₹3,800 crore. Departmental action had been underway since 2013 Departmental action was initiated in this case in September 2013. A chargesheet was also issued against Harish Chandra in 2014. The inquiry alleged violations of rules in the land survey and leaseback process during his tenure. His promotion to the IAS had also been stalled for a long time because of the departmental inquiry. After the inquiry was completed and the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission granted its approval, the government has now decided to terminate his services.

Death sentence or acquittal for ‘Blue Drum’ Muskan?:Verdict day in Saurabh murder case; testimonies of 22 witnesses form evidence
stories.summary: Date – March 3, 2025 Crime – Saurabh Murder Case Place – Meerut This case became famous across the country because of the ‘blue drum’. The body of Saurabh Rajput was found in a blue drum inside his own house. Now, the time for the verdict in this murder case has arrived. After 126 hearings and statements from more than 22 witnesses, Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra will deliver his verdict tomorrow, September 30. Saurabh’s accused wife, Muskan Rastogi, and her lover Sahil will also appear in court. Will both the accused face life imprisonment or the death penalty? Or will both be acquitted? All eyes are on the judge’s verdict. On March 19, 2025, police sent Muskan and Sahil to Meerut jail. The case reached the court on March 17, 2025. In July 2025, the case came up for trial before the District Judge’s court. The arguments continued for 13 months. Senior Advocate and DGC (Criminal) KK Chaubey said, All the witnesses in the Saurabh murder case have been examined. Our effort is to get the death penalty for Muskan and Sahil. A strong message should be sent against the way the relationship between husband and wife has been brought into disrepute in society. Now read the details… 22 witnesses appeared in court, said, ‘Muskan and Sahil are the killers’ All 22 witnesses who have testified in the case so far have identified Muskan and Sahil as the killers of Saurabh. The murder was carried out in a pre-planned manner. The accused had already purchased a knife, razor, cement, sand and a large blue drum. The testimony of the police and forensic team revealed the horrific condition of the crime scene, where blood stains were spread across the entire room. The body was brutally cut into pieces and hidden inside the drum in cement. The post-mortem report also confirmed the brutality of the murder and the use of sharp-edged weapons. All the testimonies are against Muskan and Sahil. In such a situation, it is being considered certain that they will be punished. Now read the testimony of 12 witnesses… 1. Muskan and Sahil killed my brother: Saurabh’s brother Bablu Rajput testified in court eight times. He said – I was unable to speak to my brother. On March 17, someone told me that my brother’s body was lying at his house. When I went there, there was a body, which was that of my younger brother Saurabh. My brother was murdered by his wife Muskan and her lover Sahil. 2. Body was hidden in a blue drum: Head Moharrir Brijesh Kumar said – I wrote the complaint in the case. A body was found inside a blue-coloured drum at a house in Brahmpuri. After this, the deceased Saurabh’s brother Rahul filed the complaint. It stated that Muskan had murdered her husband Saurabh along with her lover Sahil. 3. Muskan killed my son with her lover Saurabh’s mother Renu Rajput said – My younger son Saurabh fell in love with Muskan Rastogi. Despite our repeated objections, Saurabh married Muskan. After the marriage, Muskan lived at her in-laws’ house, but her behaviour was very bad. She did not take care of Saurabh at all. She fought with our entire family. Even before the marriage, Muskan used to meet Sahil frequently. When Saurabh went to London, Muskan and Sahil continued to meet frequently. Once, Muskan left the house secretly and went somewhere with her lover Sahil. Later, we had her traced with the help of the police. Even then, Saurabh told Muskan to stay away from Sahil. But she did not listen. Muskan killed my son along with her lover Sahil. 4. Friend Saurabh said – I saw Sahil Saurabh’s friend Saurabh said – I live in Brahmpuri. I know Saurabh Rajput. My house is also in the same lane. On the night of March 3, I saw Sahil, who lived in the lane ahead, going to Saurabh’s house at night. Saurabh and Muskan were at home that day. Sahil also went to Muskan’s house at night. On March 17, we came to know that Sahil and Muskan had murdered Saurabh. His dead body was found in a blue drum inside the same house. A large number of police personnel had also arrived there. 5. Muskan and Sahil took sand and cement: Building material trader Ashu said – I have a shop selling sand and cement on Sharda Road. A boy and a girl came to my shop in an e-rickshaw. They bought one sack of sand and two sacks of cement from me. They took them away in the rickshaw. I did not know why they were taking the cement and sand. I sold them the cement and sand like normal customers, and I also have the details of the transaction. 6. I prescribed only medicines for fever and headache: Dr Arvind said – Muskan came to me for a check-up. She told me that she had a fever and was not feeling well. I then prescribed medicines to her on my prescription. I prescribed medicines for fever and headache. I did not prescribe any sedative medicine, Midazolam, anywhere on my prescription. The medicines Muskan purchased from the medical shop were not prescribed by me. 7. The headless body was inside the drum: Ashok, who cut open the drum, told the court that Brahmpuri police station had called him after informing him about the matter. Police personnel took him to the mortuary of Medical Hospital, where a blue drum was kept. The police asked him to cut open the drum. Ashok said that he first tried to open the lid of the drum, but it was stuck. He then started cutting the drum lengthwise. When the drum was cut in the presence of the police, cement accumulated inside it was found. He said that two pillow covers and remains of the body were found inside the cement. A razor and a knife were also found. 8. Saurabh’s body was found in three pieces: Sub-Inspector Dharmendra Gaur, who prepared the panchnama, said – A young man’s body, embedded in cement, was found inside a blue plastic drum. The drum was cut open by labourers. Saurabh’s body was found inside it in three pieces. As the body had remained buried in cement for a long time, it had turned white at several places. 9. Murder was carried out very brutally: The doctor who conducted the post-mortem said – The body of a boy named Saurabh was taken out of the blue drum. His hand, wrist and head had been severed. There was a torso on one side. There were three knife wounds on Saurabh’s body. The marks were present. A sedative substance (some food) was found in his body, which he had consumed before his death. He was murdered very brutally. 10. Both said they wanted to go out again Cab driver Ajab Singh said- Both of them also drank alcohol during the journey. I did not know that the two had travelled with me after murdering Saurabh. I dropped them back in Meerut. Later, on March 19, I read the news of the Saurabh murder case in the newspaper. When I saw Muskan and Sahil’s pictures, I realised that they were the same two people who had travelled in my cab for the previous 10 days. 11. I provided the call detail records: Lokesh Kumar, Alternate Nodal Officer of Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, said – Police had asked us for the call details of some numbers. We provided the call detail report and mobile location data. The conversations were between Muskan and Sahil. Saurabh’s call details were also included. 12. They introduced themselves as husband and wife: Devendra, manager of Hotel Lords Gray in Shimla, said – Muskan and Sahil came and stayed at our hotel. Both introduced each other as husband and wife. They also submitted their Aadhaar cards. They told us that they were husband and wife. They then stayed at the hotel.

stories.title: Pharma businessman’s daughter-in-law accused of his murder, released from jail:Kanpur's Shalu says, ‘Suffered for 21 days; proved I am innocent’
stories.summary: I had been saying from the beginning that I had done nothing wrong. I am innocent. The truth is now before everyone. It has been proved today. I don't know why Subrat made allegations against me. I spent 21 days in jail and suffered a lot. Only I know how I spent each day. I missed my son terribly. These were the words of Shalu, the daughter-in-law of millionaire businessman Vineet Minocha, after she was released from jail in the case of his murder. Shalu was given a clean chit by the police after 21 days in custody. A court ordered her release on Monday, observing that she had no role in her father-in-law's murder. While ordering her release, the court said she would have to appear whenever summoned by the court or investigating officer. Pictures of bail Shalu spoke exclusively to Dainik Bhaskar after her release. Here are excerpts from the conversation... Q: What happened when you saw your father-in-law's body? Shalu: At that time, I could not understand what to do. Q: What is the truth about this murder case, according to you? Shalu: The truth is before everyone. I had been saying from the beginning that I had done nothing. I am innocent. That has been proved today. Q: What do you have to say about the allegations made by Subrat? Shalu: I have no information about that. I do not want to talk about it right now. All the allegations against me are false. I did nothing like that. Q: Subrat is your husband. Why do you think he did this to you? Shalu: I don't know myself why he did this to me. I cannot understand what happened and what did not. I have come out of jail after so many days and I have no idea about all these things yet. Q: You were confronted with Subrat during police remand. Did you ask him about the murder? Shalu: I did. He denied it. Subrat told me, “I am sure you did not do this.” That is why I am saying that I only know one side of the story right now. I don't know the details. Q: You spent 21 days in jail away from your five-year-old son. How did you cope? Shalu: It was extremely difficult. I spent every moment missing my son. I had never been away from him for so long. That period was very difficult for me. Q: Did you ask to speak to your son during remand? Shalu: I was missing my son terribly. I just wanted to see his face. I requested the police officers, and they allowed me to speak to him. But I could not talk to him for very long. Q: What are your plans now? Shalu: I have not thought about that yet. I just want to go to my parents and my son. Q: What was your relationship with Subrat like? Shalu: Every husband and wife have disagreements. We also had arguments, like any other couple, but there was no major dispute between us. Q: What do you have to say about the allegations Subrat made against your father-in-law Vineet Minocha? Shalu: I do not want to answer that. Q: Who did you initially suspect had committed the murder? Shalu: I had no idea about any of this. It was shocking for all of us. We suddenly wondered what had happened. We called our kitty party members and family members. Q: After the murder, did you tell your husband that Shubham could be behind it? Shalu: Yes, because he (Vishal) used to come to the shop several times. Papa had insulted him several times and humiliated him. He had told me that Papa had humiliated him badly at the shop and thrown him out. Q: Your father-in-law had a very large business. Would you like to take it forward? Shalu: No. Vineet Minocha was murdered on September 5 Businessman Vineet Minocha was murdered on September 5 at flat C-104 in Ratan Orbit, Indira Nagar. The medicine businessman had been stabbed 17 times. On September 24, police arrested his son Subrat and sent him to jail on charges of murdering his father. Speaking to the media, Subrat had alleged that his father had relationships with several women, which was why his mother Punita did not live with him. According to Subrat, he feared that a woman might come to his house and claim that she was pregnant with Vineet's child. He therefore allegedly got his father murdered through his former employee Vishal Gautam and Vishal's associate Rajkishore. During the initial investigation, police treated daughter-in-law Shalu as an accused in the murder and sent her to jail. However, the subsequent investigation found her innocent. The court released Shalu on Monday. How did Subrat allegedly frame his wife in his father's murder? DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said Subrat had been harbouring resentment against his father, Vineet Minocha, for a long time. However, he allegedly began planning the murder around one to two months before the incident. Subrat knew that after his father was killed, his brother, or Subrat's uncle Puneet, would come after him. He would try to find out the truth behind his brother's death, and there could also be a property dispute, according to the DCP. Subrat therefore wanted to achieve two objectives with one plan: make his uncle the accused in his father's murder. He allegedly shared this plan with Vishal, who worked at Subrat's shop and had been fired by Vineet seven months earlier. While planning the murder, the two also knew that Puneet had considerable influence in the city and would make every effort to prove his innocence. Therefore, around 25 days before the murder, the plan was changed. Subrat allegedly decided to portray his wife Shalu as the mastermind behind the conspiracy. He also allegedly told the employee to name Shalu if he was caught.

stories.title: State Minister says, ‘IAS Medha Roopam didn't answer my calls’:Called several times; I had her removed from Hapur three years ago
stories.summary: I was sitting at the house of a senior officer in Noida. There was a very serious matter involving his wife. I called DM Medha Rupam from his residence. She has my number, office number and even the numbers of my Lucknow office saved. I called the DM twice and waited, hoping she would call back. But she did not. This was stated by Minister of State-ranked Captain Vikas Gupta, who is also chairman of the Uttar Pradesh Council of Agricultural Research. He has complained to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath about Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida) DM Medha Rupam. Gupta alleged that the DM does not answer calls and claimed that she had been transferred from Hapur three years ago over a similar issue. Read the full conversation... Captain Vikas says he does not call people frequently Captain Vikas Gupta said, I hold an important position in the UP government and remain connected with the public. People approach me with various issues. I stay in touch with all district magistrates and SPs in the state. For any problem, I either write to them or speak to them. Sometimes, I also visit them personally.“I regularly speak to DMs of different districts. I am also in touch with everyone from departmental principal secretaries to the Chief Minister’s Office.I do not call people unnecessarily. There is a protocol I follow. My residence is in Noida, so if there is an issue, speaking to the DM becomes necessary. People from the area approach me with their problems. I called DM Medha Rupam in one such case. Medha Rupam did not answer calls in August either Gupta said, 'I received feedback from BJP workers that DM Medha Rupam answers calls only from select people. I tried several times in April and May to contact her in Noida, but she did not answer. After this, I wrote to her and sent a copy of the letter to Sanjay Prasad, Principal Secretary to the Chief Minister. I thought there might be some improvement. But things did not turn out the way I expected. I tried again in August and September. I then raised the issue with the Chief Minister.' What did Captain Vikas Gupta write in his letter? In his letter, Captain Vikas Gupta wrote, 'I have been continuously receiving complaints from citizens of the district about the DM being unavailable. I also personally tried to contact the DM regarding public grievances and administrative matters, but could not get through.' The minister asked the Chief Minister to order an inquiry into the matter. He also sought directions to ensure that all DMs remain accountable to the public, social workers and elected representatives. Medha Rupam was removed from Hapur Captain Vikas Gupta also referred to his previous experience in his letter. He said he was appointed in-charge of the Dhaulana Assembly constituency in Hapur in January 2022. During that period, while interacting with party workers and the public, he claimed to have received complaints expressing dissatisfaction with Medha Rupam, who was then the Hapur DM. stories.title: Akhilesh seeks to defeat BJP using its own formula:Adopts ‘Panna Pramukh’ model; targets double 2022 vote share
stories.summary: To defeat CM Yogi in the 2027 Assembly elections, Akhilesh is adopting the BJP’s own formula. He has asked all his booth-level agents (BLAs) to closely reach out to families in which half or some members voted for the Samajwadi Party (SP) in the 2022 Assembly elections, while the remaining members did not turn up to vote. The BLAs will be responsible for ensuring that the other members of these families also come out to vote for the SP in the 2027 elections. Guidelines have also been set to ensure that the strategy is implemented properly. The BJP’s ‘Panna Pramukh’ has a similar responsibility. In addition, the party has set a target of enrolling 400 new members at every booth. Uttar Pradesh has a total of 1.77 lakh booths. Based on this, the SP’s target is to add 7 crore new voters. Looking at the 2022 election results, the SP received 2.95 crore (32.06%) votes. This means the party is targeting an increase of nearly two-and-a-half times in its votes this time. ‘Cut BJP’s 27,000 votes, add 27,000 votes to SP’ Akhilesh Yadav has given workers a target of reducing the BJP’s votes by 27,000 and increasing the SP’s votes by 27,000 in every Assembly constituency. He said that if the party achieves this target, nothing can stop the SP from forming the government in 2027. To achieve the target, state-level leaders have been asked to devote four days a week to organisational work. Responsibilities have also been assigned to office-bearers at the block and booth levels. In addition, the SP’s high-tech ‘Digital Membership Drive’ has been underway since July 1. Instead of paper forms, the party is focusing on strengthening its organisation at the booth level through a mobile app, digital database and voter-list matching. ‘PDA Swabhiman App’ for membership and verification The party’s technical team has developed a special app for the membership drive. It is not available on the Google Play Store. It is being installed only on the mobile phones of office-bearers at the party headquarters. The app works as follows: Fee and receipt: Membership can be obtained by paying an online fee of ₹20 through the app. An online receipt is generated along with the transaction ID. This will help raise funds while also creating verified data. Mapping with voter list: Details of members are digitally verified against the electoral roll. Data maintained for every booth: Booth agents will be able to view and enter data only for their respective booths. Assembly-level office-bearers will verify the data for the entire constituency. The party has also launched the pdaswabhiman.com portal. BJP’s ‘Panna Pramukhs’ activated to counter SP strategy The BJP’s Panna Pramukhs have become active in response to the SP’s strategy of adding new voters. They are assigned responsibility for one page of the electoral roll. They personally contact voters listed on that page, collect their information and try to bring them to polling stations on election day. In other words, while the SP is focusing on apps, digital databases and voter mapping, the BJP’s model relies on grassroots contact, personal relationships and continuous follow-up. ‘Panna Pramukhs’ are a key link in the BJP’s booth management strategy. Digital push for the PDA factor The campaign is primarily based on the PDA (Backward Classes, Dalits and minorities) social equation. The party is working on a strategy to expand its core voter base by bringing young people, women, farmers, labourers and traders into the fold. Through digital data and grassroots efforts at the booth level, the SP is seeking to lay the groundwork for a return to power in 2027.

stories.title: UP Muslim activist threatened, ‘Will send you to hell soon’:Received headless body photo; caller claimed to be Pakistani gangster’s aide
stories.summary: Nazia Ilahi Khan, Bharatiya Janata Party Minority Morchaa leader, Supreme Court lawyer and Muslim activist from Uttar Pradesh, was threatened again on Thursday evening. A man named Rana Hunain, alias Rana Bhai, called her on WhatsApp and said, "Listen carefully by opening your ear hole wide. We have found your location. We also know where you live. We will soon send you to hell." After this, Nazia called senior police officers in Ghaziabad and Lucknow and informed them about the entire matter. Nazia Ilahi said, "I have also safely preserved the audio of the threat. My life is in danger." Sent a photo of a severed head Nazia Ilahi said that she was threatened during a call lasting around 30 seconds. A photo of a severed head was sent afterwards. The caller used abusive language and claimed to be a member of the Shahzad Bhatti gang. Two Uttar Pradesh Police gunmen are deployed for Nazia's security. She is living in the Indirapuram area of Ghaziabad. No one from outside can meet her. A jammer has also been installed at her residence, which means normal mobile calls can neither be received nor made there. Threat received a month ago as well Earlier, on 25 August, Nazia Ilahi filed an FIR at Indirapuram police station, alleging that a man named Shahil Ahmad had abused her on his Instagram account. She also alleged that Shahil had made children urinate on a poster featuring her. He had also threatened to behead her. The accused made remarks about harassing her through minor children and inciting violence against her. He also shared an objectionable video on his Instagram account showing a poster featuring her photograph. Nazia commented on Prophet Muhammad three months ago Nazia Khan commented on issues related to the Muslim community, the rights of Muslim women, Prophet Hazrat Muhammad and Hazrat Aisha during a podcast in June 2026. After a video of her remarks appeared on social media, several Muslim organisations and people expressed their anger. The complainants alleged that Nazia had deliberately made comments that hurt the religious sentiments of the Muslim community. An FIR was also registered against Nazia in the case on 25 August. Who is Nazia Elahi Khan? From law to politics: Triple talaq case brought her recognition Nazia Elahi Khan has been in the spotlight for her legal practice in the Supreme Court and for cases related to women's rights. She also played an active role in politics. She was earlier a spokesperson for the Trinamool Congress and later joined the BJP.

stories.title: Husband slits wife’s throat with razor, kills her:Cut his own throat too in Saharanpur; quarrel followed sister-in-law’s wedding
stories.summary: In Saharanpur, a man who had arrived for his sister-in-law's wedding slit his wife's throat with a razor and killed her. He then used the same razor to cut his own neck. Hearing their screams, family members rushed to the room. They found the husband and wife writhing in a pool of blood. The family took both of them to hospital, where doctors declared the woman dead. The husband is undergoing treatment in serious condition at the district hospital. The incident took place on Thursday evening in the Chahanjli locality of the Nanauta area. A police investigation found that the husband and wife had quarrelled over an issue. The husband had been staying at his in-laws' house since his sister-in-law's wedding. See 2 pictures... They had been married for 14 years and had no children Ghazala, the daughter of Islam, who lived in Mohalla Chahmanjli, married Irfan, the son of Umar Daraz of Kairana, in 2012. Even after 14 years of marriage, the couple had no children. Family members told the police that the husband and wife often quarrelled over not having a child. Sister-in-law's wedding took place on 21 September Ghazala's (30) sister Nilofar was married on 21 September. Irfan (33) had also come to his wife's parental home to attend the wedding. On Thursday, Ghazala's brother Suhail was due to leave for Punjab. She was packing his clothes in a bag. Meanwhile, Irfan went upstairs to the room. According to the family, the husband and wife began arguing over something in the room. As the dispute escalated, Irfan attacked Ghazala's throat with a razor. Ghazala began screaming as soon as she was injured. Hearing her screams, family members rushed upstairs. Irfan then cut his own throat with the same razor. Mourning descends on wedding house Gazala's family immediately took the daughter and son-in-law to the Nanuata CHC. Doctors there declared Gazala dead. After providing initial treatment to Irfan, doctors referred him to the district hospital. Since the death of their daughter Gazala, her mother Sanjeeda, father Islam and brothers Suhail and Shoaib have been inconsolable. The house that was filled with wedding celebrations a few days ago is now steeped in mourning. Gangoh CO Shailendra Gautam said: The husband attacked his wife with a sharp weapon. stories.title: 'Would shoot Gyanesh Kumar if one murder were forgiven':Mukesh Sahani targets Chief Election Commissioner, praises UP Police
stories.summary: Former Bihar minister and Vikasheel Insaan Party (VIP) founder Mukesh Sahni, who is seeking a political foothold in Uttar Pradesh, attacked Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, saying, “If we were forgiven for one murder, we would first shoot Gyanesh Kumar. But we are people who believe in the Constitution.” Sahni, who praised Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, said he was travelling across the state and observing how the government and administration were functioning, adding, “Yogi ji’s police are doing a very good job.” Sahni made the statement after a media report mentioned differences among Election Commission officials over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR). According to the report, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had repeatedly raised concerns within the poll panel over the SIR process. All three officials oversaw the SIR process, but Sandhu and Joshi formally lodged objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months. Four of these objections were lodged on the same day. The report also stated that the objections concerned decisions and orders that had been issued without Sandhu and Joshi's knowledge. Mukesh Sahani said, ‘Election Commission is working for the BJP’ Mukesh Sahni said democracy is being crushed. The Election Commission has become the BJP's commission. I want to tell Gyanesh Kumar to have some shame. You are playing with the Constitution of the country. Sahni said he was hurt by the way democracy was being murdered in the country. He said, "If one murder were forgiven, we would shoot Gyanesh Kumar first." However, he then said that they were people who respected the Constitution. Mukesh Sahni steps up activity in UP ahead of 2027 Mukesh Sahni has increased his activity in UP ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. He has made several visits to UP since April. His main issue is reservation for the Nishad community. He is also trying to politically unite the Nishad community. Mukesh Sahani joined the protest outside the mortuary at Lucknow's KGMU (King George's Medical University) in connection with the recent death of Vinod Nishad in Gonda. Cabinet minister and Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad and Samajwadi Party leader Rajpal Kashyap were present at the protest. The leaders demanded action against the accused and justice for the victim's family. Sanjay Nishad had called him a 'seasonal politician' After this, Sanjay Nishad launched an indirect attack on Mukesh Sahani. He said, "Some 'seasonal leaders' have still not decided whether they will do business in Mumbai, keep moving around laying carpets for others or continue brokering the votes of the fishing community. That is what he has done in his own state." Sanjay Nishad said that the fishing community was not a people who could be bought with money. Before trying to teach the fishermen of Uttar Pradesh politics, it must be understood that politics is in their blood. A fisherman may be poor, but he is not the son of a traitor. Because of some people, the community's reservation benefits were looted and continue to be looted even today. The community is not being allowed to unite. Divisions are being created within it in the name of Kevat, Mallah, Bind and Kashyap. Focus on the Nishad community for 2027 Political analysts say Mukesh Sahani's frequent visits to Uttar Pradesh indicate his growing political activity. Before the 2027 election, he is trying to strengthen the VIP's base in Uttar Pradesh. Nishad reservation is the major issue in his campaign. Alongside this, he is appealing to the Nishad community to unite politically. Talks also underway over Mukesh Sahni's alliance with the SP Mukesh Sahni's activism before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections is also considered significant because talks are underway over an alliance with the SP. Sahni's party has been trying to establish its political identity among the fisherfolk and Extremely Backward Class vote banks in Bihar. Besides this, the Nishad, Mallah, Bind, Kevat and Kashyap communities have a significant presence in a large number of Assembly seats in Purvanchal, Uttar Pradesh. In such a situation, Sahni's activism could pose a direct political challenge to the Nishad Party.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar says he will support Mayawati, calls Akhilesh confused:‘His PDA keeps changing’; CEC should be removed
stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad targeted Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav in Lucknow on Thursday, accusing him of being confused about PDA and saying, “Akhilesh Yadav is confused about PDA. At times, he says P stands for Pandit and at other times for backward classes. His P keeps changing, but ours will not. Our P stands for the oppressed and will always stand for the oppressed.” Chandrashekhar also commented on Akhilesh Yadav's 'chariot'. He said, "Akhilesh Yadav comes in a Yadav chariot. Other leaders come from the ground. I come from 10 feet below the ground. If I had a chariot, it would start from Lucknow and definitely reach its destination." Chandrashekhar said that if Behenji (Mayawati) gained strength in 2027 and came to power with his participation, he would support her. Chandrashekhar Azad held the Sampoorna Bhagidari movement at Eco Garden in the capital on Thursday. People from several districts of Uttar Pradesh had arrived to support him. All parties tried to bury us Chandrashekhar said, "Other leaders come from the grassroots, but we come from 10 feet below the ground. All parties tried to bury us. Our parents were not ministers. No one in our family was an MLA or an MP. We have reached this point through our own efforts and the love of society. We were born in the Azad Samaj Party and will die in it." Reacting to Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar's statement about making him Chief Minister, Chandrashekhar said, "We want Rajbhar's son to become Chief Minister. But who will make him – the public? And will the public be with him? Will this Rajbhar's son become Chief Minister? The people will also decide which Rajbhar's son will become Chief Minister now." The Chief Election Commissioner should be removed from office Chandrashekhar Azad also called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to be removed from office. He said that none of the elections held while Gyanesh Kumar was in office should be considered fair elections. "If the elections had been conducted properly, we would not have guarded the EVMs for one and a half months. Elections should now be held using ballot papers, not EVMs." "Once questions have been raised about the Election Commissioner, how can the Election Commission's impartiality remain? People will be satisfied only after he is removed from office." A report published on 23 September claimed that, over the past 10 months, two election commissioners had raised objections with Gyanesh Kumar over the functioning of the office 14 times. Since then, opposition leaders have been gaining the upper hand over the Chief Election Commissioner.

stories.title: Mining department clerk took ₹1.35 lakh bribe:₹71 lakh cash found at officer’s house in Shamli, counted using two machines at the police station
stories.summary: Meerut Vigilance team carried out a major operation at the Mining Department office in Shamli on Thursday. The team caught department clerk Saddam and Mining Officer Sudhakar red-handed while allegedly accepting a bribe of ₹1.35 lakh. The Vigilance team then took both men to Adarsh Mandi police station, where they were questioned. What was the bribe allegedly sought for, and who else is involved in the case? According to reports, a person had lodged a complaint with the Vigilance Department. The team conducted an inquiry before taking action. During the operation, the Vigilance team also recovered ₹71 lakh in cash from Mining Officer Sudhakar’s house. He had kept the money in a black bag inside a cupboard. Another ₹8 lakh was found in a rack at his office. The Vigilance team brought the cash recovered from Sudhakar to Adarsh Mandi police station. Two machines were used to count the cash in the SHO’s room. ASP Sumit Shukla and Sadar Circle Officer Jitendra Kumar were present at the spot. Here is the full story... According to the complainant, Parmal, he had submitted a file at the mineral department office to get a file related to sand mining in Sahalapur village approved. He was asked for a bribe in the name of getting the file approved. Parmal said, "Instead of taking the money directly, the mining officer asked me to speak to clerk Saddam. After that, Saddam was the one negotiating the amount with me. ₹50,000 was demanded a week ago. I deposited ₹50,000 into Saddam's account on 21 September. I also have the receipt." Complaint filed with anti-corruption team 20 days earlier Paramal then paid ₹85,000 in cash on Thursday, taking the total amount paid to ₹1.35 lakh. Paramal had complained to the anti-corruption team about the bribe demand 20 days earlier. Since then, the anti-corruption team had been laying a trap to catch the clerk and the mining officer. Both caught accepting ₹85,000 Parmal said it had been agreed that ₹85,000 in cash would be handed over on Thursday. The Anti-Corruption team was already present at the Mining Department office. At 3 p.m., as soon as I handed ₹80,000 to clerk Saddam, the Anti-Corruption team arrested him. During questioning, Saddam said he had negotiated the deal at the behest of mining officer Sudhakar. The Anti-Corruption team then arrested clerk Saddam and mining officer Sudhakar.

stories.summary: A 23-year-old seafarer identified as Suraj Yadav from UP's Deoria district was killed in a missile attack on a commercial ship near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's eastern coast. Suraj Yadav, son of Om Prakash Yadav and a resident of Karmanjipur Ahirwati Tola village, had travelled to Oman on August 19 through a Mumbai-based company to work aboard a commercial vessel, his uncle Awadhesh Yadav was cited in a PTI report on Thursday. According to the same report, the ship was travelling from Oman to Bahrain when Suraj, a wiper, last spoke to his family. He had told them that the vessel would return to Oman after loading cargo. India condemns the attack The Indian Embassy in Oman on X said the merchant vessel, MV Cape Dao, came under attack while transiting towards India on Wednesday. Union Ports, Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all surviving crew members, including the 19 Indian nationals, have been safely evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman and are currently ashore. The government will ensure that the mortal remains of Suraj Yadav are brought home with full dignity, and every possible support is extended to his next of kin, Sonowal said on X. Suraj was eldest among 4 brothers Suraj was the eldest of four brothers and was unmarried. His three younger brothers -- Sunny, a Class 10 student, Sahil, a Class 9 student, and Sameer, a Class 6 student -- live with their mother and grandfather in the village. On Thursday, relatives, neighbours, and villagers gathered at the family home to mourn Suraj's death. Previous deaths of Indian sailors during West Asia war The latest death comes months after another seafarer from Deoria, Shivanand Chaurasia, was killed in an attack on the Palau-flagged tanker Settebello off the Oman coast in June. Twenty-four Indian crew members were aboard that vessel, of whom 21 were rescued. Chaurasia and two others were later confirmed dead. Following attacks on merchant vessels in the Strait of Hormuz in July, the Centre reviewed the safety of Indian seafarers working in conflict-sensitive regions. A high-level review chaired by Sonowal launched the Seafarer-First initiative to protect Indian sailors in conflict zones like the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.title: Noida bus fire:Bodies kept burning for 2 hours; skin stuck to seats, granddaughter identified woman by anklet
stories.summary: A sleeper AC bus travelling to Mahoba caught fire around midnight on Wednesday in Noida. Nine passengers were burnt alive, including eight men and a woman, Usha Devi. Usha was identified by her anklet. At the mortuary, Ayushi broke down after seeing her grandmother’s anklet. According to eyewitnesses, passengers were trapped inside the bus, screaming for help. However, the flames were so intense that no one could move closer to rescue them. Gradually, the screams fell silent. The bodies continued to burn for nearly two hours. After the fire was extinguished, the rescue team cut open the rear section of the bus using a cutter. When police and forensic teams entered, they found that the bodies had been reduced to skeletons. The skin of three passengers was found stuck to the seats. Some bodies were lying in the aisle and were also found stuck to the floor of the bus. Mobile phones were found burnt and stuck to the legs or chests of some victims. Open food tiffins were lying on the seats. The team took around 45 minutes to collect the bodies from inside the bus. A large quantity of nail polish and a cylinder were also found in the bus’s luggage compartment. Police suspect that the cylinder and nail polish may have contributed to the rapid spread of the fire. When and how did police learn about the incident? When did they reach the spot? How many bodies have been identified? What will happen to those that remain unidentified? Read the full details… See 3 pictures… Police and fire brigade arrived within 10 minutes, bus kept burning for 2 hours People likely suffocated as smoke filled the bus and were unable to escape The rescue team said a total of 35 people were travelling on the bus. The bodies of nine people were recovered from the bus. Identifying the bodies is extremely difficult. They had been completely burnt in the fire. The bus was also completely gutted. It appears that the fire started in the bus's air conditioner because of a short circuit. The flames then spread from the bus cabin to the inside. The bus seats, the plastic fittings, seat covers, curtains and fibre fuelled the fire. Passengers' belongings also caught fire. The bus seats had been burnt to ashes. Only the metal frame remained. When the fire broke out, most of the passengers were in their sleeper cabins. They were asleep, so they could not get out of the bus in time. Some became trapped in the aisle, while others remained seated. By then, the bus had filled with smoke. This led to the formation of gases such as carbon monoxide and carbon dioxide, causing the passengers to suffocate. Those who managed to get out survived. The others suffocated inside the bus. The families of the passengers who are missing have reached the mortuary. SDM says, 'People who travelled on the bus are being called by phone" Jewar SDM Durgesh Singh and Jewar police station in-charge Ajay Kumar also reached the spot. SDM Durgesh Singh said the bus had departed from Kashmiri Gate. Several people had boarded at Kashmiri Gate. The driver also picked up some passengers at Sector 37 in Noida and the Zero Point of the Yamuna Expressway. Since the bus driver picked up passengers at several locations, the complete details of the passengers are not available. I have a list of more than 25 people who were travelling on the bus. They are now being called by phone so that they can identify the bodies. They are being asked, "Who was travelling with you? Who was sitting in the seat next to you?" People who have reached the post-mortem house will be asked to identify the bodies. The bodies that are identified will be handed over to their families. Those that cannot be identified will undergo DNA testing. The bodies were completely burnt after the fire. Bus parked 2 km from accident site, 2 drivers and helper sent to jail After the accident, police removed the bus from the expressway. It was parked under the expressway near the Jewar toll plaza, 2 km from the accident site. Police said the bus belongs to Raj Kalpana Travels of Madhya Pradesh, but operates from the Kashmiri Gate bus depot in New Delhi. The bus is registered in Bihar's Madhubani district. Its fitness certificate was issued in Rajasthan and its pollution certificate in Haryana. The bus has received 19 challans and a fine of ₹1.75 lakh has been imposed. Meanwhile, police have arrested the bus drivers, Pawan and Vinod. They have also apprehended the helper, Yogesh. Police have sent all three to jail. Sanjay Kumar Gupta, the MVI at the Gautam Buddha Nagar RTO office, said the bus was also found to be slightly taller than the prescribed limit. According to the standards, its height should be 3.8 metres, whereas the bus was 4.1 metres tall. Transport minister says, 'Driver's licence cancelled' Uttar Pradesh Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh expressed grief over the bus accident. He said that, according to preliminary information, the bus, registered in Bihar, was travelling from Delhi to Mahoba. The bus owner is said to be from Kanpur. According to the minister, passengers had complained of a strange smell in the bus. Despite this, the driver did not open the emergency exit. Nine people have died in the accident. The driver's licence has been cancelled. He said strict action would be taken based on the investigation.

stories.title: Kanpur millionaire businessman’s murder was allegedly orchestrated by son:Daughter-in-law cleared, son says father had affairs with several women
stories.summary: Shocking revelation has emerged in the murder case of millionaire pharma trader Vineet Minocha (63) in Kanpur. His son, Subrat (35), allegedly orchestrated the murder, while his daughter-in-law, Shalu (32), has been cleared of involvement. On Thursday, Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said Subrat was the mastermind behind the murder. Police will file an application in court seeking Shalu’s release. Subrat said: My only regret about having my father killed is that he should not have been stabbed to death like this. I did not want him to be killed in this manner, but I wanted him dead. My mother was also troubled by my father’s extramarital relationships. He would openly talk about his relationships after coming home. My mother would also tell us to do something about it. I regret that Shalu, my wife, had to go through this. Subrat also told police during questioning: “My father had affairs with several women. I feared that he might marry one of them and bring her home, making her a shareholder in the family property. I was struggling for every rupee, while my father would show me photographs of himself partying with women in Goa. I had a debt of ₹40 lakh. I had to pay an instalment of ₹55,000 every month, while my father gave me only ₹40,000 as pocket money. Frustrated by this, I planned the murder.” Police caught businessman’s son 19 days after the murder Police reached the alleged mastermind, Subrat, 19 days after the pharma trader’s murder. Earlier, on 6 September, police had arrested domestic worker Vishal and his associate Raj Kishore after shooting them in the leg. During questioning, both had said they carried out the murder at the behest of daughter-in-law Shalu. Police later arrested Shalu and sent her to jail. However, the case took a U-turn on Wednesday (23 September), when police took Shalu, Vishal and Raj Kishore into 24-hour custody for questioning. Shalu and Vishal were confronted with Subrat at Kalyanpur police station. During questioning, Vishal said he had killed Vineet at Subrat’s instruction. Subrat had allegedly told him, “If you are caught, name Shalu.” He had promised to pay ₹6 lakh for the murder. Following Vishal’s statement, police questioned Subrat intensively at around 2.30am. He then allegedly admitted to having his father killed. ‘I framed my wife because she used to speak to the domestic worker’ Police asked Subrat why he had framed his wife, Shalu. He said Shalu regularly spoke to Vishal. He had also met Vishal several times with Shalu, and Vishal used to visit their home. So, he thought suspicion during the murder investigation could easily fall on Shalu. For this reason, he had told Vishal to name Shalu if police caught him after the murder. Subrat said his relationship with Shalu was good and they only argued over some family matters, which he described as normal between a husband and wife. Shalu had also asked her father, Naresh Arora, to give him ₹14 lakh to help repay his debt. Debt piled up over expensive habits and status symbols Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal said at a press conference at 1pm on Thursday that Subrat was addicted to alcohol, gambling and betting. He kept falling deeper into debt to fund his expensive habits and maintain his social status. He had taken loans of ₹75,000 from ICICI Bank, ₹25,000 from RBL Bank, ₹5 lakh from Moneyview and ₹3 lakh from PNB. He had also borrowed money from other banks and through credit cards. His total debt gradually reached around ₹40 lakh. ‘Vishal killed my father at my instruction’ “Vishal killed my father at my instruction. Shalu is innocent. I initially wanted to frame my uncle for the murder, but that did not work out. I then plotted to implicate Shalu in the case. I had access to the CCTV cameras installed at my house and switched them off myself on the day of the murder.” ‘I was the one who gave Shalu Vishal’s new number’ After the murder plot was planned, Vishal bought a new SIM card on 3 September under the name Shubham. Between 6.29pm and 6.49pm that evening, Vishal and I spoke four times. He then stopped using his old number. To make the suspicion fall on Shalu, I sent her Vishal’s new number on WhatsApp. On 4 September (Janmashtami), Vishal and Shalu spoke at 12.44pm. Shalu had asked Vishal to bring new glasses and other items for Janmashtami. On the day of the murder, I spoke to Vishal six times and Shalu seven times. That day, I also told Shalu to tell security guard Madan Singh that Vishal’s name was Shubham. She did as I told her. ‘I had a duplicate key made for ₹100’ I was the one who asked Vishal to get a duplicate key made for the flat. Vishal got the key made for ₹100 from Gumti No. 5. I kept the key with me. During the murder, the flat door was opened using the original key. After Shalu’s arrest, I also started fearing that I would be arrested. I remained in constant contact with my family and lawyers. My legal adviser told me to stick to my statement and not get disturbed during police questioning. ‘I was taking sleeping pills after Shalu’s arrest’ As the police investigation closed in on me, I realised that I could be arrested. After Shalu’s arrest, I felt guilty that my wife was in jail because of me. To cope with the shock, I started taking sleeping pills. If I had not been arrested, I would have taken sleeping pills and died by suicide. ‘My father was a womaniser, so my mother lived separately’ Subrat said, “Our family had a high social status, so ₹40,000 in pocket money was not enough. My father was a womaniser. Because of his behaviour, my mother lived separately from him in Ghaziabad. Once, my father, my wife Shalu and I were travelling in a car. While driving, my father’s hand touched Shalu. I suspected that he had touched my wife inappropriately. I became angry with my father. However, when police questioned Shalu about the incident, she denied that any inappropriate touching had taken place.” ‘I had medicines stolen from my father’s shop nine times to repay my debt’ According to police, Subrat started stealing medicines from his father’s shop on Birhana Road with the help of domestic worker Vishal to repay his debt. Vishal would stand outside the shop while Subrat handed him cartons of medicines worth lakhs of rupees. Vishal would later sell them. Subrat allegedly got Vishal to steal from the shop eight to nine times. Later, Subrat’s father caught Vishal stealing. The two had an argument, following which Vineet fired Vishal from his job. ‘I had been planning my father’s murder for three months’ During questioning, Subrat said he had been planning his father’s murder for three months. He first asked Vishal to arrange an accident, but Vishal refused. They then planned to suffocate him with a pillow. Vishal also involved his associate Raj Kishore. The plan was for one person to hold his father’s hands and legs while the other suffocated him with a pillow. After the murder, Subrat planned to return home, claim that his father had suffered a heart attack and arrange his funeral. As planned, he went to a party with his wife and son. Vishal and Raj Kishore had already hidden inside the flat. After some time, his father returned home and suddenly switched on the light in the room where the two men were hiding. On seeing them, he started shouting. Vishal panicked and attacked him with a knife, killing him. The plan to suffocate him with a pillow therefore failed. Shalu kept crying, while husband Subrat did not even look at her During questioning, Shalu kept looking at Subrat, but he did not look at her. When Subrat accused her of arranging his father’s murder, she broke down in tears. She said, “He framed me to save himself. I trusted Subrat, but I have now lost that trust. I was shocked to know who had told Vishal to name me.” Repeating her earlier statement, Shalu said, “I did not arrange the murder of my father-in-law, Vineet Minocha. I had a good relationship with him. He had diabetes, so I took care of him. Subrat knows me well, yet he did not even come to meet me in jail.” As part of the murder investigation, police officers asked the accused more than 40 questions. Their facial expressions, faltering speech while allegedly lying and every admission were recorded on camera.

stories.title: 68,500 teacher recruitment candidates enter BJP office in Lucknow:Lie on floor, raise slogans; allege scuffle with cops, clothes torn and misbehaviour
stories.summary: Candidates seeking jobs under the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers entered the BJP office in Lucknow on Thursday and staged a protest. The candidates lay on the floor and raised slogans while wearing caps carrying the words ‘reservation scam’ and blowing whistles. The protest continued for around 30 minutes, during which a scuffle and heated exchange took place between the candidates and police personnel. The protesters alleged that police forcibly removed them, tore their clothes and misbehaved with them. The candidates are demanding that the reservation benefits promised under the 2018 recruitment process be implemented and that a revised selection list be issued after providing a 5% relaxation in the qualifying marks. During the protest, the candidates raised slogans including, “What is the compulsion? It is reservation theft” and “The Backward Classes Commission has accepted it — it is a reservation scam.” Police tried to remove the protesters from the BJP office, following which a scuffle broke out between the two sides. Police detained all the protesters and took them to Eco Garden. A large number of candidates with disabilities also took part in the protest. See 3 pictures of the protest... ‘We have been waiting for jobs for eight years’ Ashutosh Verma, who came from Sitapur, said the candidates had been struggling to get jobs for the past eight years. He alleged that there had been large-scale irregularities in the recruitment of 68,500 assistant teachers. According to him, the State and National Backwards Classes Commissions had also acknowledged irregularities in the implementation of reservation and directed the authorities to follow the rules. “Our demand is that the orders of the commissions should be implemented. The recruitment was announced in 2018 and we had applied then. Since then, we have spent eight years waiting for a job and running from one office to another,” Ashutosh said. According to the protesters, the recruitment process for 68,500 assistant teachers was announced in 2018. A provision allowed a 5% relaxation for candidates from four categories — persons with disabilities, ex-servicemen, Scheduled Castes and Other Backwards Classes. The candidates alleged that applicants from these four categories did not receive the benefit and that the results were declared along with those of candidates from the general category. They are demanding a 5% relaxation in the qualifying marks for the recruitment examination. They said that for the 150-mark examination, the result should be revised by setting the qualifying score at 60 marks, or 40%, and a fresh selection list should be issued. ‘Meetings are held, but no solution’ Adarsh, who came from Ayodhya, said he had been a BJP supporter and member for the past eight years but was still struggling to find a job. “We have been protesting at Eco Garden for a long time. We visit the Education Minister’s residence, and meetings are held after we are called, but no solution comes out,” he said. He questioned whether the government did not want to create employment opportunities for the protesters and alleged that their concerns were being ignored. ‘We have been struggling for jobs for years’ Utkarsh, who travelled from Basti to join the protest, accused police personnel of misbehaving with the protesters and tearing their clothes. “We have been struggling for jobs for years. There is a BJP government in the state, so if we do not come to their office, where else should we go? The police tore our clothes and assaulted us today. We are job candidates — why are we being treated like this?” he said.

stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav will launch the campaign for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. He will take out the PDA Rath from Raebareli, considered Rahul Gandhi’s stronghold, and address a public meeting at the GIC ground. The PDA Rath is being launched for the first time. According to party sources, the Rath will travel across the state during the 2027 elections. The Samajwadi Party’s PDA Rath reached Raebareli on Thursday. Party workers gave the Rath a grand welcome at the Bachhrawan toll plaza. A large number of SP workers were present at the toll plaza and raised slogans in support of the party. Meanwhile, posters targeting Akhilesh Yadav have been put up in Raebareli ahead of the Rath Yatra. The posters feature pictures of Akhilesh along with Azam Khan, Atiq Ahmed and Mukhtar Ansari. They carry slogans including ‘Akhilesh Yadav, go back’, ‘Akhilesh’s mafia, mafia’s Akhilesh’ and ‘Azam Khan, Atiq Ahmed, Mukhtar Ansari — they were the ones running the government’. Public meeting at GIC ground, Akhilesh to visit SP MLA’s home Akhilesh Yadav will address a public meeting at Raebareli’s GIC ground. After this, he will visit the residence of Harचandpur SP MLA Rahul Lodhi and have tea there. He will also meet Samajwadi Chhatrasabha workers who clashed with ABVP members and police officials on September 17.

stories.title: Ram Mandir donation theft case:Chargesheet filed in anti-corruption court; Champat Rai, Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao turn approvers
stories.summary: Police on Wednesday (23 Sept) filed a 36,039-page chargesheet in the Ram Temple donation funds case before the Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court in Ayodhya. The chargesheet was brought to the court in four large boxes and two cartons. Former Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr Anil Mishra and construction in-charge Gopal Rao have not been named as accused. Police have instead listed all three as witnesses in the case. The chargesheet mentions 133 witnesses. It includes a 59-page charge report and 101 case diary sheets. The chargesheet was filed after the 90-day deadline of the second SIT, constituted on the orders of the Supreme Court, ended. Chargesheet brought to court in four boxes Barabanki ASP Ritesh Kumar Singh and investigating officer and CO Ayodhya Ashutosh Tiwari reached the court premises on Wednesday morning with a police team. Around five inspectors and 12 sub-inspectors were among the police personnel present. The chargesheet was brought in four large boxes and two cartons. After it was filed, the court began matching and examining the documents. The development led to increased activity in the court premises. Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao made witnesses Police have not made Champat Rai, Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao accused in the case and have instead included them as witnesses. A total of 133 witnesses have been named in the chargesheet. Some lawyers raised objections over the investigation and questioned why certain people had not been named as accused. Slogans were also raised against the police outside the Special Judge, Anti-Corruption Court. Security arrangements had already been made at the court complex in view of the chargesheet filing. Two trucks of the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC) were also deployed. Next hearing on remand scheduled for October 7 The court disposed of an application filed by the Bar Association in the case. According to the court, no evidence was found in connection with the affidavits submitted by lawyers seeking their inclusion in the investigation. The application was therefore disposed of. The next hearing on the remand proceedings is scheduled for October 7. Case came to light on June 4 The Ram Temple donation funds case came to light on June 4 after an incident involving alleged concealment of cash in the counting room was reported. A probe was subsequently sought and a report was called for. The first SIT was formed on June 13 and began questioning Trust officials and employees from June 15. Between June 16 and 19, the SIT also examined Trust documents and sought information from bank officials and representatives of the agency responsible for counting the cash. On June 23, the first SIT submitted a preliminary report of around 20 pages to the Additional Chief Secretary of the Home Department. The report mentioned CCTV evidence related to around 70 suspected theft incidents over a 42-day period between April 27 and June 5.

stories.title: From Bundelkhandi folk songs to ‘Hanuman Ansh’:Director’s Instagram message gives Sunil Lodhi a chance to sing in film
stories.summary: Sunil Lodhi, a folk singer from Agra village in Madhya Pradesh, is now gaining recognition for his song Maine Tere Hi Bharose, Hanuman, Sagar Mein Naiya Daal Dai from the film Hanuman Ansh. His journey from singing Bundelkhandi folk songs in his village to recording a song for a film began with a video that went viral on social media. In 2019, his maternal uncle Rohit Sahu recorded a video of Sunil, who is visually impaired, singing a Bundelkhandi folk song and shared it on social media. The video went viral, after which Sunil began receiving more opportunities to perform folk songs and gradually gained recognition across the Bundelkhand region. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Rohit, who had recorded and shared Sunil’s first video. He said Sunil had been interested in music since childhood and started learning to play the tambura at around nine after watching elderly people in the village play it. Here is the story of Sunil Lodhi’s journey from folk songs to the film industry. ‘I recognised the talent hidden in Sunil’ Rohit Sahu lives in Talchir village, around 6 km from Sunil’s home in Agra village. Sunil had called him “mama” since childhood. Rohit said he noticed Sunil’s talent and began recording his performances and uploading them on social media. In 2019, he recorded Sunil singing a Bundelkhandi folk song and shared the video online. The video brought Sunil more opportunities to perform folk songs. The 2019 folk song that went viral Rohit said he had asked Sunil to sing a Bundelkhandi song that included lines about a wedding and vehicles arriving for the celebration. The video of the song went viral, after which Sunil began receiving regular opportunities to perform folk songs. Rohit said the response boosted Sunil’s confidence and made him believe that he could pursue singing. Since 2019, he has continued to receive opportunities to perform folk music. More Raiyan Ne Bhora... Dulha Ban Ke Aa GayeThela Hai Motor Ko ByaahMore Raiyan Ne Bhora, Sabre Vahan Jor Mein Le AayePatpatiya Nyote LagwaayeTractor Mama Ji Kat Le Aaye An Instagram message brought a film opportunity Rohit said he took Sunil to Mumbai on February 6, 2026, to record a folk song. Later that evening, the two went to Versova beach. While they were there, Sunil received a message on Instagram from a person who introduced himself as a film director and said he wanted to meet him. The person later sent a mobile number through Instagram. Rohit said they initially did not believe that the message was genuine. However, when they called the number, the person on the other end identified himself as Vishal Chaturvedi, director of Hanuman Ansh, and invited them to meet. Director invited Sunil to sing for the film Rohit said Chaturvedi told them that he had heard Sunil’s songs on Instagram and had contacted him after listening to his performances. The director then asked whether Sunil would be willing to sing a song for the film. Rohit and Sunil were surprised by the unexpected opportunity and were happy to accept it. Sunil subsequently recorded the song Sagar Mein Naiya Daal Dai for the film. They waited for the film’s release After recording the song, Sunil and Rohit waited for the film to be released. Hanuman Ansh hit theatres on August 7. Rohit said they were curious to know whether Sunil’s song had made it into the final film. Some people whom they had told about the song later said they had watched the film but had not heard it. On the third day after the release, Rohit and Sunil went to a theatre to watch the film themselves. When Sunil’s voice was heard in the film, both were delighted. The song Maine Tere Liye Hi, Hanuman, Sagar Mein Naiya Daal Dai, sung by Sunil, subsequently received a positive response from listeners. Rohit said people began discussing the song not only across India but also in other countries. Thousands of students listened to Sunil’s songs in Kanpur Sunil visited Kanpur University on September 18, where he performed for thousands of students in the auditorium. University Vice-Chancellor Vinay Pathak was also seen listening to Sunil’s bhajans and applauding with his eyes closed during the programme. Sunil and Rohit stayed in Kanpur for around four hours during the visit.

stories.title: Rain in 10 cities including Lucknow and Maharajganj:Schools up to Class 8 shut in Gonda; alert in 58 UP districts today
stories.summary: The monsoon has become active again in Uttar Pradesh, with rain reported in 10 cities, including Lucknow, Gonda and Jaunpur, on Thursday (24 Sept) morning. In Lucknow, rain in the early hours was followed by cool winds, while dark clouds continued to cover the sky. Rain alert issued for 58 districts, heavy showers likely in 17 The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 58 districts for Thursday. Heavy rain is likely in 17 districts, including Varanasi and Prayagraj. The state is expected to receive monsoon rain for another three days. Gonda records 10 mm rain in two hours, schools closed for Classes 1 to 8 Apart from Lucknow, rain was reported in Gonda, Maharajganj, Unnao, Prayagraj and Fatehpur. Gonda received heavy rain, recording 10 mm in two hours in the morning. The district administration declared a holiday for students from Classes 1 to 8. Jaunpur records 4.2 mm rain as heavy showers expected till September 27 Jaunpur received intermittent heavy rain, recording 4.2 mm in three hours in the morning. According to weather scientists, a deep depression over the Bay of Bengal may bring heavy rain and winds of up to 50 kmph between September 24 and 27. Maximum temperatures could fall by 6°C to 9°C. UP records 6% rainfall deficit this monsoon season Uttar Pradesh has recorded 6% less rainfall than normal so far this monsoon season. In 14 districts, rainfall has not even reached half of the seasonal quota. Deoria, Kushinagar, Shamli, Ghaziabad and Kanpur Dehat have recorded the lowest rainfall, with deficits of up to 75%. See pictures of the rain Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, “The southwest monsoon has started withdrawing. This is, in a way, the final round of monsoon rainfall. Light to moderate rain may continue at different places across the state until September 27–28.” Where is rain expected today?

Chamber president Sanjay Singhania has urged Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to order a high-level investigation into the matter. He said, “The truth would come out if the allegations were investigated fairly.” Traders allege names made public before final reports Chamber president Sanjay Singhania said food samples were being collected during the festive season. He alleged that in several cases, reports about the sampling were published in newspapers before the final test results were received, damaging the reputation of the traders concerned. He said traders have the right to get the samples retested. They can also present their case before the lower court and, if required, approach the High Court and Supreme Court. In such circumstances, Singhania said, making a trader’s name public before a final decision can affect their reputation. Traders allege threats at Vyapari Bandhu meeting The chamber president alleged that traders were not treated properly at a Vyapari Bandhu meeting held in March under the chairmanship of the district magistrate. He said traders were told, “We will set you right in two minutes.” Singhania said such actions have created an atmosphere of fear among traders. He alleged that official action was affecting the social and professional reputation of businesspeople. Chamber claims complaints filed since August 2025 According to Singhania, the chamber has been submitting complaints against the officials, along with evidence, since August 2025. He claimed that no effective action had been taken even after around 13 months. He also alleged that complaints submitted through the Chief Minister’s public grievance portal were shown as resolved after allegedly attaching misleading and incorrect reports. Singhania further claimed that officials told traders, “File your complaint wherever you want; we have access to people at the highest levels.” Chamber seeks probe by senior officer from outside Gorakhpur The Chamber of Commerce has demanded an investigation by a senior officer from outside Gorakhpur to ensure an impartial probe. It has also sought the transfer of the officials concerned outside the district until the investigation is completed. The chamber has further demanded that in food-sampling cases, the names of traders should not be made public in the media before the investigation report and until the court issues its final order. ‘Order a high-level inquiry and the truth will emerge’ Sanjay Singhania has appealed to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath to order a high-level inquiry into the matter. He said traders consider the Chief Minister their protector and are confident that the allegations will be investigated impartially. “Order a high-level inquiry and the truth will become clear. It will emerge who is exploiting traders and how,” he said. The chamber president said traders hoped that action would be taken against officials found guilty following the inquiry and that businesspeople would be able to operate without fear.
