stories.title: Woman allegedly pushed from moving vehicle by live-in partner:Father accuses police of treating incident as accident; video shows her pleading for help
stories.summary: A young woman was seriously injured in a road incident in Lucknow's Sushant Golf City area on September 1. Her family alleges that her live-in partner, who was with her at the time, pushed her from a moving vehicle. The woman's father, Atul Kumar, has accused the police of treating the incident as an accident and not acting on his complaint. The woman remains in a serious condition and is reportedly in a coma. The incident reportedly took place at around 11 pm on August 31. However, according to her family, the man informed them about it at around 4am on September 1. When the family reached Lucknow, they alleged that the man continued to mislead them before leaving the scene. The family initially treated the incident as a road accident. Later, they found a video on the woman's phone in which she can allegedly be seen folding her hands and pleading with the man. Family initially filed accident complaint According to the FIR, Atul Kumar, a resident of Roshan Ganj near Kali Temple in Shahjahanpur, reported that an unidentified vehicle had hit his daughter Malishka Sonwani's two-wheeler at around 11.30 pm on August 31. She suffered serious injuries and was taken to Medanta Hospital. The family said they received information about the incident through her friend at around 4 am on September 1. As they were busy arranging her treatment, the family approached the Sushant Golf City police station on September 4 and registered a complaint. Father questions five-hour delay in informing family Atul Kumar said his daughter had come to Lucknow for a hotel-management internship. He alleged that a man identified as Priyanshu Gupta was with her when the incident occurred. According to the father, Priyanshu claimed that he had taken her to Tinder Palm and other private hospitals after the incident, but the family found no record of her admission there. The father questioned why Priyanshu informed the family only around five hours after the incident. Video found on woman's phone raises family's suspicions When the family reached the hospital, they found Priyanshu there. According to Atul, he had Malishka's mobile phone and initially refused to hand it over. The family later found a video on the phone that allegedly shows Malishka folding her hands and pleading with Priyanshu to let her go. She appears frightened and can be heard crying, according to her father. The video is around one minute long. When questioned about it, Priyanshu allegedly gave different explanations. He initially said the video had been made casually, and later claimed that Malishka had been drinking and wanted to leave the house. The family said the video was recorded around two to three hours before the reported accident. Priyanshu claimed she jumped from moving vehicle According to the family, Priyanshu told them that Malishka had insisted on leaving home and that she had tried several times to jump from the vehicle. He allegedly said that she eventually jumped from the two-wheeler at one location, sustaining serious injuries, after which she was taken to Medanta Hospital. However, the family said Priyanshu has not been able to identify the exact location of the incident to police. Police also checked CCTV footage along the route with him. The footage reportedly shows the two travelling together, but the location where Priyanshu claims the incident happened does not have CCTV cameras nearby. Father alleges complaint was changed Atul Kumar alleged that when he initially approached the police outpost and explained the matter, the outpost in-charge conducted an inquiry and recorded that the incident appeared genuine. He said that after he submitted a written complaint at the police station, he was asked to return in the evening. When he went back after receiving a call from the police, he alleged that the complaint was changed. The family had named Priyanshu in their complaint, he said. Father also alleges changes to Aadhaar details According to Atul, Malishka's Aadhaar card was found in Priyanshu's possession. He alleged that her surname had been changed from Sonwani to Gupta and that her father's name had also been replaced with Priyanshu's father's name. The father has alleged that these changes indicate a deliberate attempt to conceal facts. Police are investigating the allegations. Police say accident case registered, probe ordered The Sushant Golf City police station inspector said an accident case had been registered and that Priyanshu had been questioned. Police are also waiting for Malishka to regain consciousness so that her statement can be recorded. DCP South Mohammad Mustafa said the woman's father had approached the police and that the investigation had established that Malishka and Priyanshu had been living together. He said the incident currently appeared to be an accident based on the available information. However, he added that an investigation into the father's allegations had been ordered and that action would be taken if the allegations were found to be true.

stories.title: Haryana woman alleges gang rape at Uttarakhand MLA’s Amroha farmhouse:UP sub-inspector, constable and 2 CRPF personnel arrested
stories.summary: A 23-year-old woman from Haryana has alleged that she was gang-raped at a farmhouse in Amroha, Uttar Pradesh, by two UP Police personnel and two CRPF personnel. The farmhouse in Hasanpur is reportedly owned by independent Uttarakhand MLA Umesh Sharma, who represents the Khanpur Assembly constituency. The four accused — a sub-inspector, a police constable, a CRPF inspector and a CRPF head constable — have been arrested in connection with the case. According to the woman's complaint, she was taken from Sonipat to Amroha by CRPF head constable Mohit. CRPF inspector Lalaram Yadav was also travelling with them. The woman alleged that they later reached a farmhouse in Jhulpuri village, where UP Police sub-inspector Sanjay Tomar and constable Pramod also joined them. The group allegedly consumed alcohol before the incident. Woman alleges three men entered her room According to the complaint, two rooms were booked at the farmhouse. The woman said Mohit, Lalaram and Sanjay later entered her room and allegedly sexually assaulted her. She alleged that when the fourth accused, Pramod, entered the room, she pushed him out and locked herself inside. She then searched for Amroha police officials' phone numbers on Google and informed the police about the incident. The account of the incident is based on the woman's complaint and remains subject to investigation. Police register case, arrest all four accused Amroha Superintendent of Police Lakhan Singh Yadav said police received information about the incident late on September 22 and reached the location. A case was registered based on the woman's complaint, and all four accused were arrested for questioning. Police said the woman was already acquainted with Mohit and Lalaram. The two UP Police personnel, Sanjay Tomar and Pramod, have also been suspended pending the investigation. MLA did not respond to calls The farmhouse is located near Jhulpuri village in the Hasanpur Kotwali area, on a link road towards Gajraula. Reports identify it as the DD Brothers Farmhouse, associated with MLA Umesh Sharma. When contacted for his response to the allegations, Sharma reportedly did not answer the call. His personal assistant said the MLA was undergoing therapy and was in Khanpur for a rally. The story of Khanpur MLA, owner of the farmhouse... Who is Umesh Sharma? Umesh Sharma won the Khanpur Assembly seat as an independent candidate in the 2022 Uttarakhand Assembly election. Before entering politics, he worked as an investigative journalist and was associated with a news channel. In June 2026, he announced the formation of the Jan Nirman Party at a public meeting in Roorkee and appointed his wife, Sonia Sharma, as its national president. He also made headlines in June 2026 after allegedly losing ₹4.5 lakh in a fraud involving the proposed sale of a vintage Morris car. In December 2025, he organised a mass wedding ceremony for 151 women from economically weaker families in Khanpur. UP Congress said-how long will daughters continue to be offered as sacrifices? 20 dogs at farmhouse, hi-tech cameras installed Khanpur MLA Umesh Sharma's farmhouse is spread across several acres. It has more than 20 ferocious dogs. The farmhouse is fully equipped with high-tech technology. HD cameras have also been installed. Entry is allowed only at the MLA's signal. Several cricketers, including Suresh Raina and Mohammed Shami, have visited the farmhouse. IAS and IPS officers also stay there.

stories.title: Contractor killed after being hit by bus in Varanasi:Family blocks road in protest; worked with father
stories.summary: A young contractor from Suddhipur in Varanasi's Shivpur area was killed after a bus hit his motorcycle on Wednesday evening. The deceased, Anuj Singh Patel, was returning home from the city when the accident occurred. He had crossed Sant Atulanand Tiraha when the bus hit his motorcycle, causing him to fall on the road. The bus's rear wheel ran over his head, killing him on the spot. Police reached the spot amid rain and began diverting vehicles from the road. Meanwhile, after learning about the accident, Anuj's family members and villagers gathered at the spot and blocked the road. The protest continued for around 2.5 hours and was called off after ACP Cantt Pragya Pathak assured them of action. The bus driver has been arrested. Anuj worked with his father According to his family, Anuj had gone to the city for work and was returning home when the accident occurred. After completing his MTech, he had joined his father, Amarnath Singh, in the contracting business. His father was involved in house construction work. Anuj's mother Chandrawati Devi, wife Priyanka and their two young children were left devastated after learning about his death. Driver arrested, family assured of action ACP Cantt Pragya Pathak spoke to the villagers who had blocked the road and assured them of justice and compensation. Police acted immediately following her instructions and arrested the bus driver. The roadblock was then removed, although traffic remained disrupted for a considerable time.

stories.title: Kanpur millionaire businessman murder case:Son arrested, servant says son, not daughter-in-law, orders killing; Shalu cries seeing husband
stories.summary: Police arrested Subrat, the son of millionaire Kanpur medicine businessman , late on Wednesday night in the murder case. During police questioning, the servant Vishal said, "I killed Vineet at Subrat's behest." Subrat had promised to pay him ₹6 lakh and told him to name Shalu if he was caught. At Subrat's behest, he had stolen medicines from the shop. When he was caught, Vineet scolded Subrat, leading to an argument between the two. Vishal was subsequently dismissed from his job. On Wednesday, the police confronted the accused daughter-in-law Shalu, servant Vishal and son Subrat with one another. According to the police, Shalu began crying when she saw her husband Subrat during questioning and said, "I have been framed." Commissioner Raghubir Lal questioned all three in several rounds at the police lines. The police team asked around 40 questions. The police investigation found that Subrat was in debt to the tune of ₹15 lakh. Kalyanpur police station in-charge Keshav Kumar Tiwari said the custody remand of the three accused was obtained only after they underwent medical examinations at the jail. After their medical examinations on Thursday, all three will be sent back to jail at noon. On the night of 5 September, medicine trader Vineet Minocha was murdered in his apartment. His domestic help, Vishal, stabbed Vineet 26 times with the help of an associate, Rajkumar. When the police arrested the two, Vishal named his daughter-in-law, Shalu. All three accused are in jail. The police are also questioning Shalu's husband, Subrat. Read what came to light during the police custody remand... "Brother had said-kill him in such a way that it looks like a natural death" During police questioning, domestic help Vishal claimed that before the murder, Subrat had called him and said the incident should be carried out in such a way that it appeared to be a natural death rather than murder. According to Vishal, Subrat called him six times on the day of the murder and spoke hurriedly throughout. Vishal said that Vineet Minocha saw the two of them in the room and began raising the alarm. Out of fear, he attacked him with a knife. When the police questioned Subrat, he craftily denied the allegations made by his servant, Vishal. Subrat said, "I do not know why Vishal is making such statements. I never asked Vishal to steal." Shalu Broke Down on Seeing Her Husband The police then questioned Subrat and his wife, Shalu, after seating them face to face at Kalyanpur police station. Shalu became emotional and began crying as soon as she saw Subrat. However, there was neither anguish nor love in Subrat's eyes. Subrat's face showed indifference towards his own wife. He looked at Shalu for a moment and then turned his face away. Shalu continued crying for around 20 minutes. Shalu kept crying, while her husband Subrat did not even look at her During questioning, Shalu told the officers through tears that Subrat knew her well, yet he had not even come to meet her in jail. The police officers calmed her down, after which the questioning began. Shalu stood by her earlier statements. She said she had not had her father-in-law, Vineet Minocha, killed. According to her, she shared a good relationship with her father-in-law and took full care of his diet because he had diabetes. When police asked why Vishal had named her, Shalu said she was herself surprised about who had told Vishal to name her. When police told her that Vishal had said in his statement that he had named her at Subrat's behest, Shalu looked at Subrat and Vishal for some time. Throughout this, Shalu kept her eyes on Subrat, but Subrat did not look at her. On seeing Subrat, Shalu said: "You framed me" Shalu came face to face with her husband, Subrat, after 18 days in police custody remand. During the hour-long questioning, Shalu kept looking at Subrat. She had questions about why her husband had not come to meet her in jail and why, based on Vishal's statement, she had been accused of conspiring to murder. Subrat, meanwhile, kept avoiding her gaze. When Subrat accused Shalu of murdering his father, she broke down. She said, "You framed me to save yourself." Shalu cried three to four times during the questioning. She told the officials that she had placed great trust in Subrat, but that trust had now been shattered. More than 40 questions and video recording of every second Police officials had prepared a list of more than 40 questions to investigate the murder case. The investigation is being led directly by a joint team comprising Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal, DCP West S.M. Qasim Abidi, an inspector and three sub-inspectors. The entire investigation was videotaped. The accused's facial expressions, their faltering speech while lying and each of their confessions were being recorded on camera, so that none of them could retract their statements before the court in the future. Key found on the boundary wall of Ratan Orbit On Wednesday, the police took Vishal to Ratan Orbit in Keshavpuram, Kalyanpur. Vishal had thrown the key there while fleeing after jumping over Ratan Orbit's boundary wall. According to the police, a key was found in a vacant plot adjoining the boundary wall. Meanwhile, the second accused, Rajkishore, was taken to Central Station. Acting on his information, the police recovered his bloodstained trousers and black gamcha from behind a public toilet. Subrat and Shalu did not recognise Rajkishore According to the police, when Rajkishore was also brought face to face with Subrat and Shalu, both denied recognising him, while he denied recognising them. During questioning, Rajkishore told the police that he had committed the crime at Vishal's behest. He carried out the crime because he needed money. He had never met Shalu or Subrat before. On Wednesday, Shalu Minocha, Vishal Gautam and Rajkishore were taken into 24-hour custody remand. They were brought out of jail at 12:13 p.m. The police team took all three to Z Square Mall, Kalyanpur police station and the IIT outpost. The questioning began at the IIT police outpost late in the evening. After the servant's claim, the police arrested Subrat from his home late at night. Key questions asked to Subrat and his answers Police: What was your relationship with your father like? Subrat: My father was good and caring. He handled all the responsibilities of the family. Police: What was the relationship between your parents like? Subrat: They had a good relationship. My mother, Punita, stayed in Kanpur for a few months and in Delhi for a few months. We also have a flat in Delhi. Police: What was your relationship with your wife like? Subrat: We had a good relationship. There were disputes over some family matters, which is normal. Police: What happened when goods went missing from the shop on Birhana Road? Subrat: A carton of Electral went missing from the shop. I made it disappear with Vishal's help. My father scolded me in front of everyone at the shop. There was an argument at home as well. Police: You went to Dehradun after being called by a pharmaceutical company. What happened there? Subrat: A bag went missing from the hotel. It contained several important documents. My father scolded me severely over it. Police: Do you have a friend from Canada in Dehradun? Subrat: Yes, I have a friend. But there is only friendship between us. Police: Vishal is now naming you. Did you have your father killed? Subrat: Vishal was naming Shalu earlier. He is now trying to frame me. Police: Your father had dismissed Vishal from his job on charges of theft. He did not like him, so why did you still maintain a relationship with him? Subrat: He helped me with various tasks. In return, I helped him financially. Police: You were always in need of money. Did your father give you too little money? Subrat: It is true that my father gave me a limited amount of money. Our status was high, so that money was always insufficient. Police: Even after receiving ₹40,000 a month, did you attend expensive parties and kitty parties? Subrat: I used credit cards and sought help from friends. That is why I have also fallen into debt. Police: Did you plan your father's murder because of the debt and frame Shalu? Subrat: No, that is absolutely not true. I could not have my father killed for money. Police: Why did you fail to recognise Vishal even after seeing him in the CCTV footage on the day of the murder? Subrat: I had consumed too much alcohol at the party, so I could not recognise him. Subrat owes ₹15 lakh Police questioning has revealed that Subrat owes around ₹15 lakh. During questioning, he said his debt had increased because of credit card expenses, partying and his fondness for travelling. Police have also learnt that he lost money through gaming and betting. Round-wise questioning after blood sugar rose According to sources, Subrat has diabetes. His blood sugar rose considerably during questioning on Wednesday. Sources claim that at one point, his sugar level went above 700. Keeping his health in mind, police are questioning him in rounds.

stories.title: 9 burnt alive in moving sleeper bus in Noida:Passengers say driver, cleaner smoked; bus wasn’t stopped as fire spread
stories.summary: Nine passengers were killed when a moving sleeper AC bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Noida on Wednesday night. The victims included eight men and one woman. There were 35 passengers on the bus. Twenty were rescued, while some managed to escape by breaking the windows. Those trapped inside were badly burnt, and their bodies could not be identified. The bus left Delhi’s Kashmiri Gate at 9.30pm for Mahoba. It caught fire around 11.30pm, about 500 metres beyond Jewar Airport. Passengers say driver and cleaner were smoking Sunil Kumar, who was travelling on the bus, told police that the driver and cleaner were smoking cigarettes. When passengers objected, the two reportedly laughed. There was also a smell of burning inside the bus. It caught fire shortly afterwards. Despite the fire, the driver did not stop the bus immediately. It was only stopped after passengers broke the windows. | Several burnt alive in Noida bus fire:Why do luxury sleeper coaches become death traps in India? Some pictures related to the incident… See the accident location on the map Bus belongs to Madhya Pradesh firm; 19 challans, ₹1.75 lakh fine Police said the bus belongs to Raj Kalpana Travels in Madhya Pradesh. It has received 19 challans and has been fined ₹1.75 lakh. Police have arrested two drivers, Pawan and Vinod, and conductor Yogesh. Firefighters cut open rear of bus to reach inside A fire officer said five fire engines took 45 minutes to douse the blaze. Firefighters cut open the rear section of the bus to enter, after which the bodies were brought out one by one. The rescue operation continued for around two hours. Initial probe suggests fire may have started after AC spark or blast Noida Chief Fire Officer (CFO) Pradeep Kumar said the initial investigation suggests that a spark or blast in the AC may have triggered a fire in the engine.

stories.title: Father asks, ‘How did she die on wedding night?’:Daughter allegedly killed, then hanged; bride and groom found dead in Siddharthnagar
stories.summary: Anita's father, Panchram, said the family had been planning to get her married in Vaishakh. About 15 days earlier, the groom had called and said he was unwell and had no one to look after him, asking the family to send Anita to his house. Panchram said he was worried about what the villagers would say, but he did not know what the groom told his daughter. She went to his house the following day. Panchram said the couple got married happily during the day, raising questions about how they could have died by suicide that night. He alleged that his daughter was murdered and demanded justice. In Siddharthnagar, the bodies of the bride and groom were found inside a room on Monday night (September 21), shortly after their wedding. The bride's family has alleged that the groom and his family members murdered Anita. The incident took place in the Bansi police station area. The Dainik Bhaskar team visited the spot, located 30 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to the family members and relatives. Read the full report... Families of two brothers live in the same house Mukesh owns a two-storey house in Janiyajot village, where he lives with his wife, Mamta, sons Deshraj (24) and Arun (22), and younger daughter Kuchchi (18). Mukesh's younger brother and his family also live on the first floor of the same house. Mukesh sells vegetables in Ludhiana, while Deshraj used to work at a pani puri stall in Delhi. Anita and Deshraj got engaged in July Panchram, a resident of Karjhawaha village located 15 km away, works at a chole-bhature shop in Delhi. He lives with his wife, Kislawati, and two daughters. His elder daughter is married, while his younger daughter, 22-year-old Anita, was engaged to Deshraj in July. Their wedding was scheduled for May 2027. Deshraj returned to Delhi after the engagement. After their engagement, Anita and Deshraj started talking to each other over the phone. Deshraj returned to the village from Delhi around 15 days ago. Anita went to Deshraj's house the next day Anita and Deshraj spoke over the phone, after which Anita went to Deshraj's house the following day. The families of both sides felt it was inappropriate for the couple to live together without getting married. However, neither Anita nor Deshraj was willing to stay apart. Both families then decided to arrange their wedding at a temple. Couple married at temple in Bansi The wedding was held at 2 pm on Monday (September 21) at Tekdhar Baba Temple in Bansi. The couple took seven rounds around the sacred fire, and all the wedding rituals were performed with family members present. Relatives blessed the newlyweds after the ceremony. After the wedding, Deshraj took Anita to his home. In the evening, a feast was organised for relatives and villagers. Groom prepared wedding meal with his father Deshraj and his father had prepared the wedding meal together. The celebrations continued until 11 pm, with the bride and groom also dancing to DJ music. As there was limited space downstairs, the family members went upstairs to sleep. The room downstairs was given to Deshraj and Anita. Bride found dead, groom found hanging the next morning On Tuesday morning (September 22), Deshraj's maternal aunt, Meenakshi, went to wake Anita but received no response from inside the room. When the family pushed the door open, Anita was found lying on the floor, while Deshraj was hanging from a noose. Meenakshi raised an alarm, following which other family members reached the spot. Anita's family and the police were informed about the incident. Police arrived, brought both bodies down and sent them for post-mortem examination. Girl's father alleges groom's family demanded ₹50,000 and a vehicle Anita's father, Panchram, said, “The room's door was found open. In such a situation, who else could have committed the murder apart from the family members? I was preparing to give dowry for the wedding, but the marriage was suddenly solemnised at a temple.” He added, “During the tilak ceremony, the groom's family had demanded ₹50,000 and a vehicle. I told them that we would give them sooner or later.” ‘How could both of them have died at the same time?’ Anita's father said, “After all the wedding programmes were over at night, we returned home. The next morning, I suddenly received a call asking me to come urgently. I said, 'We have only just arrived home. What happened so suddenly?' A woman then told me that both of them had died.” He said he could not understand how both of them could have died at the same time. When the family reached the spot, he alleged that they were abused and chased away, with threats of being beaten. He also said they were not allowed to see Anita's body. “I only want justice,” he said. Sister alleges family members and neighbours killed the couple Anita's sister alleged that family members and neighbours together murdered her sister. She said, “When I reached the house to see my sister, the door was open from outside. If the two had died by suicide, the door would have been locked from inside.” ‘Food was untouched inside the room’ She said the food kept inside the room had not been touched. The plate contained puris, vegetables, dal and rice, but not a single grain had been eaten. Items and flowers were scattered around the room, where only a mat had been spread on the floor. She further alleged that when they reached the spot, villagers collectively assaulted and abused them. “The boy was educated and sensible. His father must have killed him,” she said. Groom's aunt: ‘We went to the roof to sleep after dinner’ Deshraj's aunt, Pramila, said, “We had all come for the wedding. After eating and drinking at home, the power went out in the evening, so we all went to the roof to sleep between 10 and 11 pm.” He added, “Since it was a wedding, utensils and other items had been kept downstairs, leaving little space. We also thought that as they had just got married, the two of them would stay downstairs.” He further said, “When we went to sleep, they had locked the door. Deshraj neither left the house nor came up to the roof during the night. We have no idea what happened between them that night. We are also deeply troubled. How did such an incident suddenly occur after such a major event?” ‘Anita suddenly came home, so we arranged their marriage’ Deshraj's aunt said, “The door was not bolted from inside; it was simply shut. When my maternal aunt opened the door, she saw the girl lying on the floor, while Deshraj was hanging from a noose.” She added, “Only Deshraj's mobile phone was in the room. Anita did not have a phone of her own and used to speak to her family members on their phones. She had not brought a mobile phone with her when she came here.” Deshraj's uncle said Anita had suddenly come to their home. “We said, how could we keep her at home without getting married? We also sought the opinion of some people, who suggested that the two should have a court marriage.” He added, “Everyone was living happily together. We spoke to Anita's father, Panchram, who was in Delhi, and told him everything. After this, it was decided that they would get married at a temple on September 21.” ‘Neither was willing to live without the other’ Anita's father, Panchram, came from Delhi, while Deshraj's father, who was in Ludhiana, was also called to the village. “The boy and girl were unwilling to live without each other. So, they were married happily. Everything was fine, and the atmosphere was also normal.” He added, “I cannot understand what happened during the night that led both of them to end their lives,” the family member said. Post-mortem report adds another dimension to the case The case has become more complicated after the post-mortem report was released. Initially, it was suspected that the husband had killed his wife and then hanged himself, as Anita's body was found lying on the floor. However, the post-mortem report found that both had died by hanging. No signs of struggle or assault were found on either body. The report also stated that the couple had not had sexual relations during the night. Villagers have claimed that a video was sent to Deshraj's phone during the night. According to them, the video was allegedly sent by Anita's lover and led to an argument between the couple. It is suspected that Deshraj went outside after the argument, following which Anita died by suicide. When Deshraj returned, he allegedly removed Anita from the noose and then hanged himself from the same noose. Mahendra Pratap Chaturvedi, Station House Officer of Kotwali Bansi, said both died by hanging. Deshraj's phone has been sent to the forensic team for examination. So far, neither side has filed a complaint, and the matter is being investigated.

Will Mohammed Shami help NDA woo Muslim voters?:RLD entry buzz after meeting Jayant; out of international cricket for 1.5 years
stories.summary: Away from international cricket, Mohammed Shami could be preparing to begin a new innings on the political pitch. Speculation about his possible entry into politics has intensified after his recent meeting with RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary. It is being discussed that the fast bowler could have two options ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The question now is whether his possible political entry is simply because of his popularity or whether it is part of a broader RLD-BJP strategy to reach Muslim voters in western Uttar Pradesh. Three reasons behind speculation over Shami’s political entry Shami has not yet retired from Indian cricket. This has raised questions over the timing of his possible entry into politics. According to political analysts, there are three reasons behind the speculation. 1. RLD could be a political bridge towards the BJP The RLD is currently part of the BJP-led NDA alliance. Directly joining the BJP could have raised several questions about Shami’s image among the Muslim community. In such a situation, the RLD, which has traditionally been associated with farmers, Jats and communal harmony, could serve as a more comfortable political bridge for Shami to enter the NDA camp. 2. Could he seek political backing amid legal issues? Shami’s younger brother, Mohammed Kaif, has been accused of rape by a woman from Lucknow. His family is facing legal complications in connection with the allegations. The source suggests that Shami could be looking to move closer to those in power to deal with possible pressure from the police and administration. 3. At 36, a long fast-bowling career may not be ahead Shami is a fast bowler and is now 36. The chances of a fast bowler being selected for the Indian cricket team tend to decline after the age of 35. Does the RLD want to make inroads into the SP’s Muslim vote base? Jayant Chaudhary’s party has largely remained centred around Jat and farmer politics. After joining hands with the BJP in the 2024 election, the RLD’s traditional “Jat-Muslim” equation is believed to have weakened to some extent. To counter the SP-Congress alliance led by Akhilesh Yadav, the RLD needs a prominent Muslim face, according to the source. Shami is not merely a Muslim face. He is a World Cup hero and a national icon, with a strong following among Muslim youth. Through Shami, the RLD could seek to send a message that despite being part of the NDA, it also speaks for the interests of the Muslim community. Shami could influence the Turk Muslim community Mohammed Shami is originally from Sahaspur Alinagar tehsil in Amroha district. Amroha, Moradabad, Sambhal, Bijnor, Meerut and Bulandshahr are identified in the source as his main areas of influence in western Uttar Pradesh. The Amroha seat has more than 3.25 lakh voters, of whom around 2 lakh are Muslim. More than 70,000 belong to the Turk community, which Shami’s family also comes from. SP heavyweight leader Mehboob Ali has held the Amroha seat since 2002. He also defeated BJP’s Ram Singh in 2022. If Shami or a member of his family becomes the face of the NDA, it could potentially challenge the SP’s hold over the seat. ‘Celebrity image’ could benefit Shami in politics The entry of cricket and Bollywood stars into Indian politics is not new. Mohammed Shami could benefit directly from his image as a sports star. His performances for India, particularly during the 2023 World Cup, made him popular among people across religious and social groups. Young voters who think beyond party lines or caste-based politics could be attracted by a popular sportsperson such as Shami, according to the source. The BJP-RLD alliance could also use his presence to project the message that it is not limited to any one community and is willing to include Muslim personalities who have brought recognition to the country. Expert says Shami’s entry may have limited impact on Muslim votes Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is likely to be more bipolar than the 2022 and 2024 elections. According to him, the possibility of making significant inroads into Muslim votes through Mohammed Shami is very low. Kalhans says Shami is not a political face and that his popularity is also not what it once was. He believes contesting from Amroha would not automatically make it easy to secure votes with the support of the RLD-BJP alliance. According to him, Shami’s presence could certainly generate media attention and add glamour to the campaign, but its impact on votes is likely to be limited.

stories.title: Did DJ sound really cause girl’s death?:How sound waves can affect heartbeat; what is silent blockage?
stories.summary: A girl sitting in a classroom in Balrampur suddenly collapsed unconscious at her desk. She was taken to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. School authorities said a Ganesh immersion procession was passing by when she collapsed, and the DJ was playing so loudly that the classroom windows were shaking. It was suspected that the loud noise triggered a heart attack, leading to her death. The question is, What effect can extremely loud noise have on the body that it could potentially lead to death? And why would the sound affect only one girl in the classroom? Read today’s UP Explainer to find out… Question 1: Can loud DJ or sound-system music affect the heart and cause a heart attack? Answer: In simple terms, extremely loud sound can trigger a stress response, temporarily increasing heart rate and blood pressure. In vulnerable people, severe stress can contribute to cardiovascular complications. A. Sudden rise in stress hormones A sudden, very loud noise, such as a DJ bass or explosion-like sound, can be perceived by the brain as a threat. This can trigger the release of stress hormones such as adrenaline and cortisol, causing blood vessels to constrict and heart rate and blood pressure to rise. B. Abnormal heart rhythms The copy states that low-frequency waves from heavy DJ bass can cause strong vibrations in the body and chest and may interfere with the heart’s electrical system. This can lead to an abnormal heart rhythm, or arrhythmia, which in severe cases can result in sudden cardiac arrest. C. Silent heart blockage The copy explains that some people may have undetected narrowing or blockage in the arteries supplying blood to the heart. A sudden rise in blood pressure and stress may contribute to plaque rupture and clot formation, potentially blocking blood flow to the heart and causing a heart attack. D. Greater risk for people with heart conditions People with existing high blood pressure or heart disease may be more vulnerable to the effects of intense noise, especially when combined with factors such as heat, crowds and physical stress. Question 2: Did loud noise cause the girl’s death in Balrampur? Answer: The exact cause has not been established. According to the copy, the incident occurred on September 21 and the police were informed only after a video surfaced on September 22. The girl had already been cremated, so no post-mortem was conducted. Doctors cited in the copy have suggested that the extremely loud DJ sound could have triggered a severe cardiovascular response. However, this remains an inference rather than a confirmed cause of death. The copy also notes that children can have previously undiagnosed congenital heart conditions, which could make an individual more vulnerable to a sudden cardiac event. Question 3: What are the rules for DJs and sound systems in Uttar Pradesh? The copy says that loudspeakers and DJs are regulated under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000 and the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986. It states that: Written administrative permission is required for using DJs or loudspeakers at public or religious places. Use of loudspeakers, DJs and amplifiers in the open is prohibited between 10pm and 6am, subject to the stated exceptions. The Balrampur police are investigating whether the rules were followed during the procession and are also examining the DJ equipment used. Question 4: How can you measure the noise level at a location? Noise intensity can be measured using a decibel meter. The copy mentions mobile apps such as Decibel X, SPL Meter and Sound Meter Noise Detector for approximate measurements.

stories.title: ‘Food is so bad even dogs won’t eat it’:PAC jawan shares pain; venomous snakes enter beds, they clean toilets themselves; where does budget go?
stories.summary: PAC personnel posted in Barabanki have alleged that poor barracks, bad food, lack of leave, inadequate drinking water and power cuts during extreme heat are among the common problems they face, with constable Devendra Gupta saying they are sometimes made to stay in places “where even animals would not stay”. Gupta, posted with a PAC battalion in Barabanki, said, “We are given food that even a dog would not eat. We even have to clean the toilets ourselves,” and claimed that PAC personnel cannot speak openly about these conditions. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Devendra to understand the alleged lack of basic facilities in the PAC. Constable claims: ‘We are being kept in places like cattle sheds’ There are nine PAC companies in Barabanki, with around 1,100 personnel posted there. Devendra Gupta is also posted there. Devendra says PAC personnel remain posted at police headquarters for only one or two months a year. For the remaining nine to 10 months, they are sent to different districts for duty. “There are no proper arrangements for accommodation at the places where we are sent. If you go and see these places, you will be shocked and wonder how any human being can stay there. The conditions are like a buffalo shed,” he says. He claims PAC personnel are housed in some of the city’s most dilapidated and poorly maintained buildings. “Mosquitoes bite us during the day. Poisonous snakes come onto our beds, while rats, cats and monkeys enter the rooms. There is no security for our lives or our belongings. What are we? Machines or animals?” he asks. ‘Not a single constable is happy, everyone is silent for fear of suspension’ We asked Devendra whether he was afraid of disciplinary action after making videos about his problems. “It is true that anyone who raises their voice will either be suspended by the officers or asked to give an explanation. Because of this fear, no constable speaks up. But the reality is that not a single constable in the department is happy,” he says. He alleges that when officers come for inspections, they check the constables’ uniforms and belts. “If they find even a minor deficiency, disciplinary action is immediately taken. But no officer checks the hell in which the constable is living. This is affecting the mental well-being of the personnel,” he says. Devendra also questioned the sanitation arrangements. “There must be a budget for phenyl and cleaning materials to clean the toilets and barracks. Then where does that money go?” he asks. ‘I was not given paternity leave after becoming a father’ Devendra had not mentioned leave in his video, but after controversy grew around his post, the PAC Barabanki issued an official response. The department said Devendra had already taken 25 days of earned leave (EL) and 19 days of casual leave (CL) this year. Devendra says his wife was pregnant and gave birth this month, which is why he had to take 25 days of earned leave. “Under the rules, the department provides 15 days of paternity leave when a personnel becomes a father. I applied for it on September 15, but the officers rejected my application. “If my leave appears excessive this year, the officers should look at my service record for the past three years. I have taken only a nominal amount of leave during that period,” he says. ‘Everything is fine in paperwork, but constables are suffering on the ground’ PAC Barabanki, in its response, said welfare meetings are held every month to resolve the problems faced by personnel. It said issues are discussed with officers and resolved. Devendra disputes this. “A meeting is held every month, but only the battalion in-charge, such as the subedar or in-charge officer, attends it. They simply tell the senior officers that everything is fine. They can see the problems on the ground, but they do not have the courage to speak about them in front of senior officers,” he says. PAC constable makes VIDEO and seeks justice from Chief Minister On September 22, Devendra Gupta shared a 6-minute-42-second video. For the first 5 minutes and 48 seconds, he spoke about his own difficulties and those of his colleagues. In the final 1 minute and 8 seconds, he included an episode from the Mahabharata in which Lord Krishna appears before Dhritarashtra’s court seeking justice. Devendra, who is from the Gorakhpur region, appealed to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, saying: Chief Minister, I come from your own parliamentary constituency. You have listened to the grievances of lakhs of helpless and poor people in the state and worked for their welfare. Now we hope that you will also listen to the pain of us constables. PAC personnel perform duty round the clock in scorching heat, severe cold and torrential rain. Please bring reforms to this corrupt and dilapidated system and impose strict rules against officers who harass constables over every little issue. Hundreds of comments have appeared on Devendra Gupta’s video from UP Police and PAC personnel, who are describing the poor conditions in their own barracks and alleging problems with the attitude of officers.

stories.title: Azamgarh case:5-year-old searches for parents, brother, asks crying, ‘I want to play with Shaurya’; all three cremated on one pyre
stories.summary: The accused who allegedly killed his wife, son and two priests in Uttar Pradesh’s Azamgarh was shot dead in an encounter, leaving the family’s two young daughters searching for their mother, father and brother. The five-year-old girl still does not understand that her parents and brother will never return; her maternal uncle is looking after her, but she repeatedly breaks down while remembering them. She asks, “Where is brother Shaurya? I want to play with him.” There is no one to answer her questions. The seven-month-old girl, meanwhile, is still too young to understand that her parents and brother have been separated from her forever. The two daughters from the same family are experiencing the tragedy in their own ways. One is searching for her loved ones, while the other is not yet old enough to understand what she has lost. This is the story of a family torn apart… First, know the full case At around 6 pm on Tuesday, Arvind Singh (42), from Shambhupur village under Ahiraula police station, around 50 km from the Azamgarh district headquarters, allegedly shot dead his wife Babita, son Shaurya (9), and priests Mahendra Pathak (60) and Akhilesh Mishra (55). The family is now left with Arvind’s mother Kamla Devi (70) and his two daughters, Pari (5) and Shambhavi (7 months). Fearing arrest, Arvind Singh held his three children hostage inside a room. Seven hours later, he fired at his son. ATS and SOG teams subsequently killed Arvind Singh. According to police, the family suspected that Arvind was being troubled by the spirit of his brother Sunil. His wife and mother had therefore arranged a Mahamrityunjaya chant. Arvind was angry about this. At around 6 pm on Tuesday, he argued with his wife over the issue. He allegedly said, “Your brother was killed because of you. Now you are creating a drama here.” He then asked the priests for their Aadhaar cards and got into an argument with them. In the middle of this, he brought a licensed revolver from the room and allegedly shot his wife and the two priests. At around 7 pm on Wednesday, Arvind Singh, his wife Babita and son Shaurya Singh were cremated together on a single pyre. Arvind’s niece Varsha lit the funeral pyre. Husband, wife and son cremated on the same pyre Arvind Singh, his wife Babita and son Shaurya were cremated together at Rajghat in Azamgarh at around 7 pm on Wednesday. Priest Mahendra Pathak was cremated near Durvasa Dham in Phulpur, while priest Akhilesh Mishra was cremated at Kamariya Ghat in Ambedkar Nagar district. Arvind Singh’s firing also injured his five-year-old daughter Pari. The bullet grazed her hand, causing minor injuries. She is undergoing treatment at the district hospital and remains shaken after the incident. Nine-hour postmortem: eight bullets hit five people The postmortem examinations of all five bodies took around nine hours on Wednesday. A team comprising Additional CMO Dr Alendra Kumar, Dr HL Saroj and Dr Sanjay Gaur conducted the postmortems under video recording. The bullet injuries caused severe damage to the victims’ heads. Priest Akhilesh Mishra’s postmortem was conducted at around 10.30 am on Wednesday. He had been hit by two bullets in the head. Priest Mahendra Pathak’s postmortem was conducted at around 11.15 am. One bullet was lodged in his head. The postmortems of Babita and Shaurya were completed at around 1.30 pm. One bullet passed through Shaurya’s head, while one bullet was lodged in Babita’s head. Arvind Singh’s postmortem was completed last, at around 7 pm. He was killed during the commando operation. He had been hit by three bullets, two in the chest and one on the lower right side of his abdomen. No one came forward to prepare the accused’s panchnama The bodies of the husband, wife and son were lying at the postmortem house, but no one from the village came forward to prepare the panchnama for Arvind Singh until afternoon. Women from Babita’s maternal family arrived and helped prepare the panchnamas for Babita and Shaurya. Their postmortems were conducted afterwards. Babita’s maternal family, however, refused to help prepare the panchnama for Arvind Singh. The police then brought Arvind Singh’s mother, sister and niece from the village. The postmortem proceedings began at around 4 pm, after which his body was examined. Brother was killed eight years ago, had been Balasaheb Thackeray’s gunman In 2018, Arvind’s brother Sunil Singh was allegedly shot dead by his cousins. Sunil lived in Maharashtra and had worked as Balasaheb Thackeray’s gunman. Suraj Singh, the brother of Sunil’s wife, said, “My brother-in-law had gone to the village with Arvind to attend a bhandara. At that point, his cousins Manish Singh and Avnish surrounded them. They chased Sunil and shot him. They also assaulted Arvind.” Suraj said, “After the incident, my sister Mamta, Sunil’s wife, lodged a named complaint against Manish and Avnish. The police arrested both of them and sent them to jail. They were released from jail only about one-and-a-half months ago.” He further alleged, “Babita was having an affair with Manish. My brother-in-law Sunil had found out about it. He had lodged complaints against Manish in several cases, including theft, snatching and molestation. Manish killed Sunil because of this rivalry.” Eyewitness priest says: ‘First the wife, then both priests were shot’ Pandit Himanshu told police that Arvind was believed to be troubled by the spirit of his elder brother Sunil Singh. Arvind’s mother Kamla Devi and wife Babita had therefore called the priests to conduct a puja. Himanshu said, “The puja had been going on for four days. The Purnahuti was scheduled for Tuesday. Four of us, including me, my father Akhilesh Mishra and Pandit Mahendra Pathak, were conducting the puja." “On Monday, Arvind had warned us not to come the next day. He was opposed to the puja.“ At around 6 pm on Tuesday, he returned from the market and started arguing with his wife. When we went to intervene, he began abusing us. He asked us for our Aadhaar cards. “We told him, ‘We are priests. Why would we carry Aadhaar cards around? We are neither hawkers nor have we come from Nepal or Bangladesh.’ But he remained adamant." Meanwhile, Babita said, ‘Do not insult the priests.’ Arvind then said, ‘Your brother was killed because of you. Now you are creating a drama here.’ After this, he shot his wife Babita. “When we tried to run away, he shot my father. The other priest, Mahendra, had reached the doorway when Arvind shot him as well. I jumped over a wall to save my life. His mother also ran outside. People gathered after hearing the sound of gunfire. Seeing this, Arvind locked himself inside a room with his three children. The police arrived after neighbours informed them.”

stories.title: Millionaire businessman murder:Servant says son, not daughter-in-law, ordered killing; Shalu cried seeing husband, Kanpur cops asked 40 questions
stories.summary: Police on Wednesday confronted accused daughter-in-law Shalu, domestic help Vishal and son Subrat in the murder case of Kanpur millionaire drug trader Vineet Minocha. Police Commissioner Raghuveer Lal questioned the three accused in several rounds at the Police Lines. During questioning, domestic help Vishal alleged that he killed Vineet on Subrat’s instructions. He claimed Subrat had promised to pay him Rs 6 lakh and told him to name Shalu if he was caught. Vishal also said that he had stolen medicines from the shop on Subrat’s instructions. According to him, Vineet had scolded Subrat after the theft was discovered, leading to an argument between the two. Vishal was subsequently dismissed from his job. According to police, Shalu broke down after seeing her husband Subrat during questioning and said, “You have framed me.” Vineet Minocha was murdered inside his apartment on the night of September 5. Domestic help Vishal and his associate Rajkishore allegedly stabbed him 26 times. When police arrested the two, Vishal named Vineet’s daughter-in-law Shalu. All three accused are currently in jail, while police are also questioning Shalu’s husband Subrat. What emerged during police custody remand ‘Brother had said: Kill him in a way that makes it look like a natural death’ During questioning, domestic help Vishal claimed that before the murder, Subrat had called him and told him that the incident should be carried out in such a way that it looked like a natural death rather than murder. According to Vishal, Subrat called him six times on the day of the murder and repeatedly spoke in a hurry. Vishal said Vineet Minocha saw the two men inside the room and began raising an alarm. He claimed that he attacked Vineet with a knife out of fear. Police then questioned Subrat, who rejected Vishal’s allegations. Subrat said, “I do not know why Vishal is making such statements. I never asked Vishal to steal.” Shalu broke down after seeing her husband Police then questioned Subrat and his wife Shalu face-to-face. According to police, Shalu became emotional and started crying as soon as she saw Subrat. The questioning continued, while Subrat did not respond emotionally to her. Shalu kept crying, Subrat did not even look at her During questioning, Shalu cried in front of the officers and said that Subrat knew her well, yet he had not even come to meet her in jail. Police officers calmed her down before continuing the questioning. Shalu maintained her earlier statements and denied having arranged the murder of her father-in-law, Vineet Minocha. According to her, she had a good relationship with Vineet and also took full care of his diet because he was diabetic. When police asked why Vishal had named her, Shalu said she herself was shocked and did not know at whose behest Vishal had taken her name. When police told her that Vishal had said in his statement that Subrat had instructed him to name her, Shalu looked at both Subrat and Vishal for some time. Throughout this, Shalu kept looking towards Subrat, while he did not look at her. Shalu told Subrat: ‘You framed me’ Shalu confronted her husband Subrat after 18 days during police custody remand. During around an hour of questioning, Shalu repeatedly looked at Subrat. She had questions about why her husband had not come to meet her in jail and why Vishal had accused her of being involved in the murder conspiracy. Meanwhile, Subrat continued to avoid looking at her. When Subrat accused Shalu of being involved in his father’s murder, she broke down and said, “You framed me to save yourself.” Shalu cried three to four times during the questioning. She told officers that she had trusted Subrat deeply but that her trust in him had now been broken. More than 40 questions, with every second recorded on video Police officers prepared a list of more than 40 questions as part of the murder investigation. The investigation is being led by a joint team comprising Police Commissioner Raghuveer Lal, DCP West SM Qasim Abidi, an inspector and three sub-inspectors. The entire investigation was videographed. The accused’ facial expressions, changes in their speech while allegedly lying and every admission made during questioning were recorded on camera so that they could not later retract their statements before the court. Key found near Ratan Orbit boundary On Wednesday, police took Vishal to Ratan Orbit in Kalyanpur’s Keshavpuram. According to police, Vishal had thrown a key there while fleeing after jumping over the boundary wall of Ratan Orbit. Police said the key was recovered from an empty plot adjoining the boundary wall. Meanwhile, another accused, Rajkishore, was taken to Central Station. On his identification, police recovered his blood-stained trousers and a black scarf from behind a public toilet. Subrat and Shalu did not recognise Rajkishore According to police, Rajkishore was also confronted with Subrat and Shalu, but both sides denied recognising each other. During questioning, Rajkishore told police that he had committed the crime at Vishal’s request. He said he carried out the crime because he needed money and had never met Shalu or Subrat before. Main questions asked to Subrat and his answers Police: What was your relationship with your father? Subrat: My father was good and caring. He handled all the responsibilities of the family. Police: What was the relationship between your parents? Subrat: They had a good relationship. My mother Punita stayed in Kanpur for a few months and in Delhi for a few months. We also have a flat in Delhi. Police: What was your relationship with your wife? Subrat: Our relationship was good. There were disagreements over some family matters, which is normal. Police: What happened when goods went missing from the shop on Birhana Road? Subrat: A carton of Electral went missing from the shop. I had it removed with Vishal’s help. My father scolded me in front of everyone at the shop. There was also an argument at home. Police: You had gone to Dehradun after being called by a medicine company. What happened there? Subrat: A bag went missing from the hotel. It contained several important documents. My father scolded me severely over it. Police: Do you have a female friend in Canada whom you met in Dehradun? Subrat: Yes, I have a friend. But we are only friends. Police: Vishal is now naming you. Did you have your father killed? Subrat: Vishal initially named Shalu. Now he is trying to frame me. Police: Your father had dismissed Vishal over allegations of theft and did not like him. Why did you remain in contact with him? Subrat: He helped me with various small and big tasks. In return, I helped him financially. Police: You always needed money. Did your father give you less money? Subrat: It is true that my father gave me limited money. Our lifestyle was high, so the money always fell short. Police: Even after receiving Rs 40,000 a month, you attended expensive parties and kitty parties? Subrat: I used credit cards and took help from friends. This is why I also got into debt. Police: Did you plan your father’s murder because of your debt and frame Shalu? Subrat: No, absolutely not. I could not have my father killed for money. Police: Why did you not recognise Vishal even after seeing him in the CCTV footage on the day of the murder? Subrat: I had drunk a lot of alcohol at the party, so I could not recognise him. Subrat has a debt of around Rs 15 lakh Police questioning has revealed that Subrat has debts of around Rs 15 lakh. During questioning, he said his debt had increased because of credit card expenses, parties and his interest in travelling. Police have also received information about him losing money through gaming and betting. Round-wise questioning after blood sugar rose According to sources, Subrat is diabetic. His blood sugar reportedly rose significantly during questioning on Wednesday. Sources claimed that at one point his blood sugar level went above 700. Considering his health, police are questioning him in multiple rounds.

She hugged her son’s body and repeatedly said, “My dear son, get up. O God, what has happened?” Ankit, a resident of Daulatpur Eksara (Mathia) village in Ambedkar Nagar, was killed in firing at a CISF camp at the Sewa Hydroelectric Project in Kathua, Jammu and Kashmir. His body, wrapped in the Tricolour, reached his village at around 12 noon on Thursday. Ankit's wife, Priyanka, also wept uncontrollably and repeatedly banged her head against the coffin. She also continued to support her elderly mother-in-law. His sisters Yogeshwari, Lalita, Niteshwari, Sudha, Seema and Antima were also seen sobbing. His last rites were performed at around 1:30 pm. At around 7:30 pm on Tuesday, a dispute broke out among personnel at the CISF camp over something. During the dispute, a head constable opened fire with his service rifle. CISF Commandant Ankit Pandey, Sub-Inspector Laxman Singh and four other personnel were killed. Watch the disturbing visuals below : Ankit was selected for CISF in 2016 Daultpur Eksara Mathia is a village in the Ibrahimapur police station area, around 28 km from the district headquarters. Ankit, who lived there, was the only son of retired teacher Shiv Prasad Pandey. He had six sisters and was the youngest in the family. All his sisters are married. Ankit was selected as a sub-inspector in the CISF in 2016. After passing the departmental examination in 2021, he was promoted to the rank of commandant. For around a year, he had been responsible for the security of a hydroelectric project in the Basoli area of Kathua. Before that, he was posted at Bharat Mandapam in Delhi. He married Priyanka in 2019. Ankit has a two-and-a-half-year-old son, Agastya. Patriotic slogans raised as mortal remains reached village When the family was informed of Ankit's sacrifice, the house was filled with cries of anguish. At 6 am on Thursday, his mortal remains were first brought to Lucknow airport. From there, the body was taken to Ambedkar Nagar in an Army vehicle decorated with flowers. Thousands of people were waiting there to pay their last respects. The body was wrapped in the tricolour. Seeing this, people began raising patriotic slogans. CISF battalion pays tribute Personnel from the CISF battalion based at NTPC saluted the mortal remains of martyr Ankit Kumar Pandey. His final procession then began. A large number of villagers, along with public representatives, officials and local residents, joined it. Slogans of "Long live Ankit Kumar" continued to be raised.

stories.title: Alok Kumar Pushpendra Pasi become SC Morcha general secretaries:BJP forms state team, also appoints regional presidents
stories.summary: The BJP has appointed Pushpendra Pasi, Alok Kumar, Kamlesh Jatav and Pardesi Ravidas as state general secretaries of its Scheduled Caste (SC) Morcha in Uttar Pradesh on Thursday. The party has announced the new state team while maintaining organisational balance, with the appointments also carrying several political implications. The most surprising and widely discussed name on the list is Vikas Kishore, who has been appointed state vice-president. Vikas Kishore is the son of Kaushal Kishore, the BJP's former MP from Mohanlalganj and former Union minister of state. Interestingly, Kaushal Kishore had recently raised questions about the functioning of the government and the organisation, shortly after which his son was given this major responsibility in the organisation. Besides Vikas Kishore, the BJP has appointed 11 other leaders as state vice-presidents. They include Anup Valmiki, Ashok Sonkar, Babulal Bhanwara, Charan Singh Lisadi, Bhagwati Prasad, Nand Kishore Kanaujia, Abhishek Sagar, Narendra Mahandha, Hariram Rawat, Adesh Kori and Anita Siddharth. Read the list below : The BJP has appointed Nayan Dohre, Anmol Kumar Verma, Chandrika Prasad, Manoj Jajoora, Usha Paswan, Jaiprakash Gautam, Dr Harsh Jatav, Vikas Paswan, Ravi Prakash, Ramveer Katheria, Sudhir Bhuihar and Purushottam Jatav as state ministers. Dheeraj Pradhan Valmiki has been appointed treasurer, while Rahul Sonkar and Rohit Chaudhary have been appointed deputy treasurers. Shubham Sonkar has been appointed media coordinator; Jitendra Sonkar and Rajenshwar Kumar Shrivas, deputy media coordinators; Aparajita Singh, social media coordinator; and Anuj Nag and Suraj Sonkar, deputy social media coordinators. Dr Vinod Kumar Kanaujia has been appointed head of the state research department, while Sanjay Singh and Ashwini Valmiki have been appointed deputy coordinators of the research department. The regional presidents Regional presidents of the BJP Scheduled Caste Morcha have also been appointed. Akhil Kumar has been appointed regional president for West, Vishal Valmiki for Braj, Salil Shrivas for Kanpur, Arun Rawat for Awadh, Shailesh Ram for Kashi and Vijay Sonkar for Gorakhpur.

stories.summary: A massive fire broke out after cylinders explode at a Blinkit grocery store in Indirapuram, Ghaziabad on Thursday. Several nearby shops were engulfed as fire spread rapidly. Loud explosions were heard during the incident. The flames and thick smoke were visible from a long distance. According to information, the incident took place in Neeti Khand-1 on Kala Patthar Road. Fearing that the fire could spread, police evacuated nearby shops and moved people to a safe location. Seven fire engines from the Ghaziabad Kotwali, Vaishali and Sahibabad fire stations reached the scene. Firefighters are working to extinguish the blaze. According to the local residents, cylinders kept inside the store exploded, although this has not been officially confirmed. No casualties have been reported so far. Watch fire visuals below : An eyewitness at the scene said, “The fire started at the Blinkit grocery shop. I was at my shop when I saw smoke rising from there. I went closer and saw that the shop was on fire. This shop belongs to my brother, and furniture work is carried out here. The exact cause of the fire will be known later.” Story being updated...

stories.title: Brij Bhushan Singh says he won’t contest elections:Has personal ties with Akhilesh, says he doesn’t speak against him; ‘I’m in BJP, he’s SP leader’
stories.summary: Amid the Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, former BJP MP Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh on Thursday spoke about his relationship with Akhilesh Yadav and said he will not contest the 2027 Assembly elections. Speaking in Ayodhya about his growing leniency towards Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, Brij Bhushan said that he had personal relations with Akhilesh. "We have been MPs from his party. Akhilesh is a good person," he said. Brij Bhushan went on to say, “When he praises us, we praise him too. I do not speak against him, and he does not speak against me. This should not be viewed through a political lens. I am in the BJP, and he is a leader of the SP.” He also ruled out contesting the elections and said, "I do not want to contest the Assembly elections." Brij Bhushan arrived in Ayodhya from Delhi at 2 pm and received a rousing welcome from party workers at Maharishi Valmiki International Airport. There, he gave clear indications about his political role. However, he did not say that he would stay away from politics. Dig at Keshav Maurya and the Samajwadi Party through hints Brij Bhushan Singh took a dig at Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Maurya and the Samajwadi Party without naming them. He said, "Some people say that 25 Samajwadi Party MLAs are in contact with me. Others say that BJP MLAs are in contact with me. I have nothing to say about any of this." In fact, referring to cross-voting in the Rajya Sabha election, Akhilesh Yadav claimed on Wednesday, "Several BJP MLAs are in contact with us. But the question is, how will we accommodate all of them? We do not want to make false promises to anyone and then fail to honour them." After this, Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya had said that 25 Samajwadi Party MLAs were in contact with them. Had said a day earlier: Everything is desolate without Akhilesh Congress had said that in Uttar Pradesh, it would not contest fewer than 150 seats in an alliance with the Samajwadi Party. Brij Bhushan Singh was asked about this in Delhi on Wednesday morning. In response, he had said that everything was desolate without Akhilesh. Congress had no existence in Uttar Pradesh without Akhilesh. When asked about Congress's refusal to contest fewer than 150 seats in Uttar Pradesh and Akhilesh's absence from the INDI alliance meeting, the BJP leader said, "We cannot say yet whether Akhilesh will attend. It is possible that a representative of his party may be attending the meeting, but Congress has no existence in Uttar Pradesh without Akhilesh." When asked about speculation over his going to the Rajya Sabha, Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh did not respond. In the afternoon, when asked about Brij Bhushan, the Samajwadi Party chief had said, My relations with him are very good. We are all united on the issue of Uttar Pradesh's development. Supported Baba Ramdev's statement Brij Bhushan supported yoga guru Baba Ramdev's statement that "all Muslims in Hindustan are converted". He said, "As far as Baba Ramdev's statement about the Muslim community is concerned, I have been saying this from the beginning. Seventy to 80 per cent of people in the Muslim community come from Hindu society. I had said what Baba Ramdev has said before he did."

stories.title: Akhilesh announces ₹51,000 pension for ‘democracy fighters’ if govt formed:Asked about becoming PM; says, ‘Don’t make us fight’
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has made a major announcement for the defenders of democracy. He said that if his government comes to power in the state, the honorarium for these fighters will be increased to ₹51,000 per month. They will also receive free medical treatment. Just like freedom fighters, democracy fighters will also receive other facilities. Targeting the BJP government, Akhilesh said, “At present, social justice across the country is going through the BJP’s Emergency era. Any period in which the PDA is oppressed will be an Emergency.” He said that even if the BJP manages things under a microscope, it will still lose. Asked about becoming the prime minister, Akhilesh said, “Let me stay in Uttar Pradesh for now; do not make us fight among ourselves.” He was referring to Rahul Gandhi. The Samajwadi Party and the Congress are part of the INDIA alliance, with Rahul Gandhi leading the alliance. Former Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav was addressing a press conference at the Samajwadi Party office on Thursday. During the event, he honoured Mohammad Naseem by draping a shawl around him. Naseem had carved an image of the Legislative Assembly on a tiny grain of rice. Key points from Akhilesh Yadav's press conference : Yadav said, "The police cannot be trusted; they are working as BJP workers. In this government, genuine saints have been deeply insulted and have not received justice." Taking a dig at Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak for saying that young people should drive e-rickshaws instead of seeking jobs, Yadav said, "The Deputy Chief Minister should book an e-rickshaw. This is the Deputy Chief Minister who has made hospitals sick." The former chief minister said, "The BJP will lose even if it manages the election with a microscope. Whether the BJP fields nine candidates or 10, it is going to lose this election. Anyone who wants to join hands to defeat the BJP is welcome. Even today, we are living through the same period, with inflation, unemployment and corruption at their peak." Yadav alleged that a young man in Gorakhpur who made a video showing waterlogging and corruption was booked under the Goonda Act. Taking a jibe at the Uttar Pradesh government for approaching the Supreme Court in the Noida district magistrate case, he said that lakhs of rupees were being spent to avoid a ₹5 lakh fine. He said, "As soon as this government is removed from the state, this bulldozer-style situation will also end." Asked about Minister Rajbhar's continued attacks, Yadav said, "How will those who won on the Samajwadi Party's votes win again on their own?" Smiling in response to a question, he said, "You bring Rajbhar to us and we will take him... Go and bring him, we are waiting." Yadav said that Gen Z and the PDA would wipe out the BJP in the coming days. He gave the slogan, "Ek kachori, do samosas, BJP me na koi bharosa." A major Gen Z programme will be organised soon.

stories.title: UP Shikshamitras cannot take special TET:HC rejects plea, saying their status differs from govt teachers
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh's shiksha mitras will not be able to appear for the Special TET-2026. The Allahabad High Court dismissed a petition seeking their inclusion in the exam on Thursday. Justice Manju Rani Chauhan said that the petitioners cannot claim the right to appear for the Special TET merely because they are eligible to take the regular TET. The court said the legal status of shiksha mitras is different from that of teachers employed in government service. The court further said that the Constitution does not require the state to remove a distinction if it is based on a legitimate legal objective. The petition was filed in September last year by 220 shiksha mitras, including Wasim Ahmed. They had sought an opportunity to appear for the Special TET-2026. The court reserved its judgment after the hearing was completed on September 24. About special TET examination : Special TET is a special teacher eligibility test for teachers and shikshamitra working in Uttar Pradesh. The State Education Service Selection Commission has introduced it for teachers who have not yet passed TET or CTET. Examination on 3 November Passing the TET by 2028 is mandatory In an order issued on 1 September last year, the Supreme Court made it mandatory for all serving teachers to pass the TET by 31 August 2028. Following this, teachers' organisations launched a protest demanding special relief. The government had announced that a separate special TET would be conducted for serving teachers. The plan for conducting it has now been approved. News is being updated...

stories.title: Prayagraj court summons Rambhadracharya over 'casteist' remark:He said Brahmins don’t marry into Upadhyay, Chaubey, Dixit families
stories.summary: The ACJM court in Prayagraj issued a notice to Tulsi Peethadhishwar Jagadguru Rambhadracharya over his remarks about sub-castes in the Brahmin community on Thursday. He has been asked to appear in court on October 12. A case against him will be heard in the court. The controversy began after a video of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya went viral. In the viral video, he made remarks about some sub-castes in the Brahmin community, such as Upadhyay, Chaubey, Trigunayat, Dixit and Pathak. He had said, "The Brahmin community does not marry its daughters into these sub-castes." On 14 September, Ramesh Upadhyay, a resident of Varanasi, filed an application in the ACJM court seeking to lodge a complaint. He said, "The Jagadguru's remarks have hurt the sentiments of the community, so he should be summoned and action should be taken against him." Ramesh is the national president of the Bharatiya Kisan Sena Loktantrik Party. Read what Jagadguru said in the video below : "The discussion about lowly Brahmins... inferior Brahmins was started. Some Brahmins are not considered good in our community. Families from higher lineages do not give their daughters in marriage to them. Upadhyay, Chaubey, Trigunayat, Dixit and Pathak are considered inferior because they taught students after taking money from them. "We neither give our daughters in marriage to their families nor take daughters from them. We consider taking even a single penny from a student equivalent to eating beef. I am a Saryuparin Brahmin. First, I am a Brahmin-specifically, a Brahmin of the Vashishtha gotra. Then I am a sadhu, then a sannyasi, and then Jagadguru Ramanandacharya. I am proud of my Brahmin identity." Petitioner said-Statement has begun creating obstacles to children's marriages Ramesh Upadhyay filed an application to lodge a complaint at ACJM Court No. 8 on 14 September, accompanied by his lawyer, Kamla Prasad. The application stated that Jagadguru Rambhadracharya is a saint whom people worship. It said that after his remarks during a Bhagwat Katha in Vrindavan on 3 February 2024, people had begun looking down upon the Upadhyay community. According to the petitioner, boys and girls from the community had begun facing difficulties in getting married. He said he had met the Prayagraj Police Commissioner and filed a complaint in the matter on 22 May 2025. He had also sent a complaint by post, but no action was taken. "After this, I am filing a complaint case in court. It is necessary to take action against him in the interest of justice."

stories.title: ‘Blue drum’ Muskaan-Sahil break down after verdict:Restless in jail, ate little; judge calls crime ‘frightening’
stories.summary: The blue drum case took an emotional turn as Muskan and her lover Sahil started crying as the judge announced the verdict on Thursday. When Meerut District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra asked them what sentence should be given to them, both remained silent before breaking down. The court later deferred the decision on their sentence until October 14. The judge made the remarks while delivering the verdict in the high-profile case. They both were convicted of killing Muskan's husband, Saurabh Rajput, and hiding his body in a blue drum. The judge said such crimes create fear and insecurity in society and affect the way people think. He said a rise in crime is a matter of concern and that the justice system must assure people of their safety and maintain their faith in the law. He also said the court's responsibility is not limited to punishing the crime and the accused. It must also take into account the rights of the accused and the interests of society. According to jail sources, following the verdict, Muskan and Sahil remained restless in their barrack. They kept crying and ate little at night. In view of their condition, jail authorities increased surveillance on them. Judge says dismembering hiding a body is a heinous crime The final arguments in the case were heard on 19 September. The court set 30 September for pronouncing the verdict. District Judge Arvind Kumar Mishra entered the courtroom at 4:30 pm on Wednesday. Muskan and Sahil were connected from Meerut jail via video conference. The judge saw both of them on the screen. He first named Sahil Shukla, followed by Muskan Rastogi. The judge said, "the statements of the witnesses and the evidence have proved that both of them murdered Saurabh Rajput. To destroy the evidence, they cut the body into pieces and packed them in a blue drum. This is a heinous crime. The court declares both of them guilty." Deceased's mother and brother began crying as soon as the verdict was pronounced After hearing the verdict, Saurabh's brother Rahul and mother Renu Devi became emotional and began to cry. After the verdict, Saurabh's lawyers KK Chaubey and Vijay Bahadur folded their hands and thanked the court, urging it to sentence both of them to death. After the verdict, Muskan and Sahil will not be transferred to another prison. Both will remain in Meerut Jail. The prison administration has increased surveillance of both of them. Senior Jail Superintendent Dr Veeresh Raj Sharma said: Muskaan has been performing prayers for more than three days. Sahil also remains quiet. Jail staff are keeping a constant watch on both their behaviour. A counsellor's help will be sought if necessary. No one has come to meet Muskaan in jail in the past 17 months.
