stories.title: Yogi says ACS called former DGP without doing homework:Says such formalities put system in dock
stories.summary: Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh Yogi Adityanath criticised the practice of unnecessary formalities while addressing a programme in Lucknow on Thursday. He reprimanded Additional Chief Secretary (Home) Sanjay Prasad over the formal phone call made to former DGP Prakash Singh. The CM said, “It is because of such formalities that you people end up in the dock. Put an end to these formalities and hold programmes with full preparation.” Yogi Adityanath awarded medals to 26 brave police personnel at the programme. Ten of them received the Chief Minister’s Gallantry Medal, while 16 received the Gallantry Medal. The CM also released former DGP Prakash Singh’s book, Sangharsh, and flagged off 87 high-tech police vehicles. The CM said, “Whenever a person tries to take a shortcut, it leads not to progress but to decline. It creates a crisis of identity for the person. That is exactly what Uttar Pradesh was facing. What was the situation before 2017? People would immediately exclude someone simply by saying he was from Uttar Pradesh.” This story is being updated...

stories.title: Passenger falls asleep in Varanasi airport parking:Misses Dubai flight; people say Gorakhpur man was drunk
stories.summary: A drunk passenger missed his flight to Dubai after falling asleep at the parking area of Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport on Wednesday evening. He lay down in the car park after drinking alcohol and remained there for a long time, during which his flight took off. Local residents later informed the police. The police reached the spot and sent the passenger to hospital in an ambulance. His family members were also informed about the incident. After he sobered up on Thursday morning, the passenger returned home. He had come from Gorakhpur to travel to Dubai Bhabhishan Kumar, a resident of Barhalganj in Gorakhpur, was scheduled to travel to Dubai on Air India Express flight IX-183. He reached Varanasi Airport at around 5:30 pm on Wednesday. The flight was scheduled to depart for Dubai at 9 pm. After reaching the airport, he drank alcohol and later lay down in the parking area in an intoxicated state. He remained there until his flight departed. Drunk man abuses taxi drivers when they tried to wake him up Taxi drivers and passengers passing through the parking area noticed the man lying there and tried to wake him. However, they moved away after noticing the smell of alcohol and hearing him abuse them. The passenger remained in the parking area for a long time, during which his Dubai-bound flight also departed. Police sent him to hospital in an ambulance Upon receiving information, a team from Phulpur police station reached the spot and found the passenger in an unconscious state. The police called an ambulance and sent him to the Primary Health Centre in Baragaon, where he was given treatment. Babhatpur outpost in-charge Vijay Kushwaha said the passenger's family was informed about the incident through his mobile phone. He said the passenger could not board the flight because he was heavily intoxicated. By the time he regained consciousness at night, the flight had already departed. After regaining consciousness, the passenger realised his mistake and left for home on Thursday morning.

stories.title: FIR against 20, including SP councillor, on court order:Accused of grabbing temple land in Gorakhpur; councillor says, ‘Will present my side in court’
stories.summary: Police have registered a case against 20 people, including Samajwadi Party councillor Vijendra Agrahari, following a court order over allegations of attempting to encroach on land belonging to Shri Thakurji Hanuman Temple in Hanumanchak, under Gorakhpur’s Rajghat police station. The case was filed on a complaint by Ramprakash Das, the temple’s caretaker. Allegation of forged documents and illegal construction records Ramprakash Das alleged that forged documents related to the temple land were prepared with the intention of selling and encroaching on it. He said the land is recorded in the temple’s name and that he is its successor and sarvarakar on the basis of a registered will dated December 15, 1998. According to the complaint, some people allegedly obtained house tax and building/plot numbers from the municipal corporation for the temple land even though no houses had been constructed there. Sale deeds and other documents were subsequently prepared for the land on different dates. Soil allegedly dumped on temple land using JCB in January According to the complaint, councillor Vijendra Agrahari allegedly began filling the temple land with soil using a JCB on January 5. Temple priest Kamaldas reportedly reached the spot after learning about the work and stopped it. The complainant alleged that the priest was abused and threatened with death when he objected. ‘Returned with tractor-trolley to dump soil in August’ Ramprakash Das alleged that on August 20, Agrahari returned to the disputed land with his associates in a tractor-trolley and began dumping soil again. He claimed that those who objected were threatened with death if they did not vacate the land. Das maintained that the temple land is recorded in government documents and that he had never sold it. He subsequently sought legal action against those named in the complaint. Following the court’s order, Rajghat police registered the case and began an investigation. Case registered against 20 people The accused named in the case are Vijendra Agrahari, Ramavatar, Digvijaynath, Ashok Kumar Agrahari, Chandragupta, Sushila Lohia, Satya Prakash, Shalini Gupta, Ranjeet, Arvind Jaiswal, Vimla, Krishna Prakash, Jyoti Prakash, Piyush Gupta, Imran Khan, Krishna Murari, Krishnakant Sharma, Vinay Kumar, Pankaj Kumar and Surendra Kumar. Councillor denies allegations, says he executed sale deed in 2018 Vijendra Agrahari denied the allegations. He said he had executed a sale deed for the land in 2018 and would present his case before the court, adding that the allegations against him were baseless.

stories.title: Ganga water reaches Namo Ghat platform in Varanasi:Connectivity cut off to 84 ghats; boatmen pray, ‘Mother Ganga, please calm down’
stories.summary: The weather has begun to change once again in Varanasi. The city recorded a temperature of 30°C on Thursday morning. Wind speed was around 8 kilometres per hour, while humidity remained at 69 per cent. The city's air quality index (AQI) was recorded at 99. According to meteorologist Prof. Manoj Srivastava, there is no possibility of rain or cloudy conditions over the next week. During this period, temperatures may rise by one to two degrees Celsius. However, the weather will remain slightly cool in the mornings. Ganga water level rising Meanwhile, the rising water level of the Ganga has once again begun changing the condition of the ghats. Water has returned to the ghats where it had receded in recent days, and cleaning of the steps and platforms has begun. The Ganga has reached the platform at Namo Ghat. Water has also reached the steps at Assi Ghat. In addition, 84 ghats remain cut off from the mainland. As the Ganga's water level rises, problems have increased at the ghats where cleaning had been carried out after the floodwaters receded. With the water returning, the silt and rubbish accumulated there will have to be cleared again. The shortage of space at the ghats is also causing difficulties for people arriving to perform pind daan and other religious rituals. With devotees moving in and out during Pitru Paksha, the limited space has made arrangements at the ghats challenging. Boats have not operated for two months, increasing boatmen's concern The Ganga's constantly changing water level and the condition of the ghats have also affected the boatmen's livelihoods. The boatmen said boat operations have been affected for around two months. This has made it difficult to support their families. They said they were praying to Mother Ganga for the water level to settle and the condition of the ghats to return to normal so that boat operations could resume.

stories.title: 20,000 people affected in Gomti river floods:Water enters several Lucknow villages and submerges crops; locals wait for relief
stories.summary: The rising water level of the Gomti River has worsened the situation in the low-lying areas of Itaunja in Lucknow. Several villages, including Sultanpur, Bahadurpur, Lasa, Akadariya Khurd, Akadariya Kala, Hirapurwa, Jamkhanwa and Dughra, are affected by flooding. Around 20,000 people are reportedly affected. Roads connecting several villages have been submerged, disrupting movement in the area. With floodwater reaching homes, some families have been forced to move to safer locations. Schoolchildren, women and elderly residents are also relying on boats to travel. Villagers said several boats do not have adequate safety equipment, including life jackets, raising concerns about their safety. What are the villagers demanding? Which areas are at risk? Read about it in this ground report by Dainik Bhaskar... First, take a look at six photographs... Roads submerged, children using boats to reach school The rising Gomti has disrupted road connectivity between villages. Water has made several routes difficult to cross on foot or by vehicle, forcing residents to use boats. Children are also using boats to reach school, while women and elderly residents have limited options for travelling. Villagers said the lack of adequate safety equipment on boats could lead to accidents. Floodwater enters homes, families move to safer places After floodwater entered homes, some families moved to safer locations. Those who remain in the villages are facing difficulties in arranging food and other daily essentials. Arranging fodder for livestock has also become difficult. Villagers have demanded that relief materials be provided to affected families and fodder be arranged for their animals. Paddy, okra and 'sebi' crops destroyed Ram Devi of Bahadurpur village said she had planted paddy, but the entire crop was submerged in floodwater. Her okra and 'sebi' crops were also damaged. She said the income from the 'sebi' crop helped support her family. She had used money earned from selling wheat to grow paddy, but that investment has now been lost. Ram Devi said, “I invested the money from selling wheat in paddy farming. Now the paddy has also been submerged. The okra and sebi crops have also been damaged. The District Magistrate visited, but we did not receive any help.” Ramu: Entire village flooded, no relief received Ramu, a resident of Bahadurpur, said the entire village was flooded and people were facing major difficulties in travelling. He said the District Magistrate had visited the village for an inspection, but residents had still not received relief. Villagers have demanded that essential facilities be provided in the affected areas at the earliest. The DM had conducted an inspection On Monday, District Magistrate Vishakh G. Iyer had inspected flood-affected areas, including Lasa and Akdariya Kala. He spoke to the villagers to assess the situation and directed officials to provide relief as needed. The administration had also instructed officials to arrange additional boats and provide health services. Meanwhile, according to the villagers, ADM Supply Jyoti Gautam had also visited the flood-affected area. The villagers allege that she had photographs taken during her inspection at the site and then left. They still did not receive any relief. Residents seek relief and safety measures Villagers have urged the administration to provide relief materials, fodder for livestock and safe transport arrangements for affected families. They have also sought life jackets and other safety equipment for boats. Farmers whose crops have been damaged by the floods have also sought financial assistance. Villagers said that even after the water recedes, they will face the challenge of restarting farming.

stories.title: 2 sadhus killed and bodies burnt in Shahjahanpur:Bodies set on fire on a wooden pyre inside Shiva temple; smoke alerted people
stories.summary: Two sadhus were allegedly murdered at a temple in Shahjahanpur district, and their bodies were later set on fire. According to the information, villagers reached the temple at around 7 am on Thursday after noticing smoke rising from the premises. They found one sadhu’s body still burning, while the other’s body had been reduced to a skeleton. Bodies found 10 metres apart The two bodies were found around 10 metres apart. The incident took place in Khudaganj, around 70 km from the district headquarters. The deceased have been identified as Baba Gopal Das and Baba Bihari Das. Both lived at a temple in Sutha village under Khudaganj police station limits. Know the full details Villagers said sadhu Gopal Das (70), a resident of Azizganj locality, was a storyteller who had been living at the temple for around 20 years. Bihar Das (60) was from the same village. He had earlier lived at the Thakur Ji temple in Sutha village and became Gopal Das’s disciple a month ago. The two then began living at the Shiva temple. Pradeep Singh, nephew of Baba Bihar Das, alleged that a local youth, Sumit, carried out the killings. He claimed Sumit had attacked the two sadhus several times in the past. Dragpal, who cleaned the temple, said he reached the temple at around 7 am and found the bodies burning. He said he had not met the sadhus at night and had last seen them at around 3 pm on Wednesday before returning home.

stories.title: Where will former IAS Divya Mittal contest from?:Mirzapur or join Raja Bhaiya; will she form new party?
stories.summary: Former IAS officer Divya Mittal is set to enter politics. A viral photograph with Raja Bhaiya and her past disputes with Anupriya Patel in Mirzapur have fuelled speculation in political circles. She has also received offers to join the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress. Despite this, she does not want to join any political party. This has raised three major questions: Here are the answers, one by one… 1. Where could Divya Mittal contest an election? Three possible options are being discussed for Divya Mittal’s political debut. First, she could begin her political career by contesting the Mirzapur Sadar Assembly seat. When she was transferred in 2023, people in Mirzapur gave her a flower-filled farewell. Second, she could contest from Chunar. People in the region still remember the grand Chunar Mahotsav organised during her tenure. The constituency has a sizeable Kurmi and Dalit population, and the BJP is considered strong there. Third, instead of contesting the Assembly election herself, Divya Mittal could field some of her supporters from Mirzapur. She could then directly challenge Anupriya Patel in the 2029 Lok Sabha election. However, political experts believe that this is the right time for a non-political person to enter politics. The Lok Sabha election is still some time away. Rather than waiting until then, they suggest she could build her political profile by contesting an Assembly election. How strong is Divya’s public connect in Mirzapur? Divya Mittal’s biggest political asset is considered to be her administrative record and direct engagement with the public. After her transfer in 2023, local leaders and villagers publicly praised her work. Her efforts to bring water to Lahuriyadih, in particular, earned her recognition in rural areas. Following her resignation, she also raised questions about why a secondary school approved during her tenure in Lahuriyadih had still not been built. Her remarks prompted officials to move quickly to begin construction. This is why her supporters argue that Mirzapur could be her natural political base if she contests an election. Divya Mittal also has considerable support among the Mirzapur Gram Pradhan Association. Several village heads even have her tie a rakhi on their wrists. Despite no longer being posted in Mirzapur, she continued to help secure development projects in several villages through her administrative contacts. Support from the village heads’ association could prove to be a major political asset during an election. 2. Could she also take on Anupriya Patel? First dispute: Divya Mittal served in Mirzapur from September 2022 to September 2023. During this period, her most widely discussed achievement was bringing water to Lahuriyadih village. A water-worship ceremony was held after the water supply reached the village, but a controversy arose because local elected representatives were not invited. The incident was linked to differences between her and Union Minister and Mirzapur MP Anupriya Patel. Lahuriyadih falls within both the Mirzapur Lok Sabha constituency and the Chhanbey Assembly constituency. At the time, Anupriya Patel was the MP from Mirzapur, while the Chhanbey seat was held by Apna Dal (S). Second dispute: This concerned Acharya Ramchandra Shukla Park and the Kajri Memorial. As District Magistrate, Divya Mittal had the memorial built in the park in Mirzapur city with public contributions. The inauguration was scheduled for 2 September 2023, with Union Minister Anupriya Patel set to attend. Anupriya Patel’s husband, Ashish Patel, reportedly became upset over the name of the park. Third dispute: This arose over the Chunar Mahotsav. Divya Mittal repeatedly sought dates from Anupriya Patel for the festival but could not secure a suitable date. She subsequently organised a grand Chunar Mahotsav without Anupriya Patel. This further deepened their differences. Following these incidents, Divya Mittal was transferred and kept on a waiting list for around 10 months. Local residents still call her ‘DM Beti’. Speculation has now emerged that she could challenge Anupriya Patel in the Lok Sabha election after establishing herself through an Assembly contest. 3. How likely is she to join Raja Bhaiya? Dr Brijesh Singh Rajawat, a leader of the Jansatta Dal Loktantrik, shared a photograph on social media on 29 September. The caption read: “IAS experience + Raja Bhaiya’s grassroots influence = a new direction?” The post went viral. Raja Bhaiya’s party has a regional political base. Speculation began that an association with the party could give Divya organisational strength. However, she has repeatedly made it clear that she will not join any political party. For now, this remains speculation. Why the BJP, SP and Congress may not be options for Divya Mittal After Divya Mittal’s resignation, speculation emerged that she was receiving behind-the-scenes support from the BJP. However, she has herself dismissed any such possibility. Following her resignation, she raised concerns about the poor condition of schools and other problems in the state, directly questioning the state government. BJP leader Prashant Umrao questioned her resignation on social media, linking it to an alleged meeting with Rahul Gandhi. Divya later rejected these allegations, saying that such accusations were intended to intimidate a woman and discourage her from entering politics. Now, regarding the possibility of her joining the SP or Congress, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav made an open offer to Divya Mittal while speaking to the media on 30 September. He said that the former IAS officer should now wear a green and red scarf, the colours associated with the SP. Following Divya Mittal’s resignation, Akhilesh Yadav was among the first to link it to the functioning of the government. He said that honest officers were being troubled under the BJP government and that corruption was preventing officials from doing their jobs. Similarly, Congress state president Ajay Rai was asked whether the party would offer Divya a ticket if she decided to contest an election. Rai said the party could consider anyone who wanted to work for society and contest an election. However, Divya clarified her position on 29 September. She said, “I cannot stand under the flags under which no one has been held accountable for 80 years and demand accountability.” Rather than joining a particular party, she is talking about changing the system. This stance points towards an independent political experiment outside the BJP, SP and Congress. Statements made by Divya Mittal after her resignation Why did Divya Mittal choose Uttar Pradesh for her political career? Divya Mittal, who studied at IIT Delhi and IIM Bengaluru, has served as District Magistrate of districts such as Sant Kabir Nagar, Mirzapur and Deoria. She originally belongs to Haryana. This means Haryana was also an option for her political career, apart from Uttar Pradesh. People who know Divya Mittal closely say that her administrative career was spent in Uttar Pradesh, where she built relationships that remain strong even after her resignation. Her statements since resigning can be divided into three broad categories. ‘It remains to be seen how far she can go alone in an election’ Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says her statements are anti-establishment and focused on public concerns. She is presenting herself as a ‘voice’ distinct from traditional politicians. While this approach has emotional appeal, her organisational weaknesses are also evident. By choosing the independent route, she has distanced herself from major parties. This may give her an independent image, but it remains to be seen how far she can go alone in the current electoral environment.

stories.title: 15-ft potholes on Gorakhpur Link Expressway:Road broken up to 5 ft, patchwork washed away in rain; hard to drive at 100 kmph
stories.summary: The Link Expressway connecting the Purvanchal Expressway to Gorakhpur has deteriorated. There are potholes at 74 places on a 45-km stretch of the 91-km-long Link Expressway. Some are 10 to 15 feet long, while others are half a foot deep. At several places, the road has cracked in the middle. The company that built the expressway has filled these potholes with gravel, but the gravel can also be seen spread far across the road. Wherever the patchwork has come off, deep potholes have appeared again. This ruins the experience of a ‘comfortable journey’. It also becomes difficult to maintain a speed of 100 kmph. It is not that the expressway was built in a hurry. It took five years to complete. It has only four lanes. A total of Rs 7,283 crore was spent on its construction, which means an average of Rs 80 crore was spent to build each kilometre. This includes the cost of land acquisition. Know the condition of the expressway step by step… While travelling from Lucknow on the Purvanchal Expressway, we reached the Gorakhpur Link Expressway. Around 3 km ahead, after crossing the toll booth, fresh patchwork was visible on the road. At several places, the patchwork was 50 to 100 metres long. When the car was driven at speed, it was bouncing over the potholes. Our car travelled around 10 km through Jogipur, Banwaripatti and Chandrabhanpur. During this stretch, we found the road damaged at 20 more places. Attempts had been made to repair these spots, but the gravel had spread far across the road with the tyres of vehicles. Several vehicles passing in front of us were travelling while avoiding these potholes. Near Katoi and Sheikhpura, the expressway had broken right in the middle. A little further ahead, in Barhalganj, we found the road broken at several places over a long stretch. We got down and counted the potholes; there were around 20. The road had cracked in the middle. A pothole more than half a foot deep had formed here. It was more than 10 feet wide. This was not limited to one spot; there were four such potholes within a 100-metre stretch. It appeared that these had been filled only a few days earlier, but the gravel and asphalt had now come out of the potholes and accumulated on the road, forming bumps. In other words, there is a pothole on one side of the road and a 1-foot-high bump right next to it on the other side. The road has also sunk at this spot. A drain-like depression has formed in the middle. During rainfall, instead of flowing towards the side, water collects at the same spot. This further damages the road. However, after this, the road remained in good condition for around 25 km. Travellers said, ‘This is not even like Lucknow’s Kisan Path’ While travelling on the expressway, we met Barabanki resident Pankaj Verma at the toll plaza. Pankaj said- This is not like the Purvanchal Expressway or the Agra Expressway. In fact, I would say that it is not even like Lucknow’s Kisan Path; there are too many potholes on it. Some other people, like Pankaj, also said that travelling on this expressway is not easy. You are driving a car at 100 kmph, and then suddenly potholes appear, causing the vehicle to go out of control several times. 22 damaged spots found while returning to Lucknow After travelling 91 km from the Purvanchal Expressway to Gorakhpur, we started our return journey towards Lucknow. Now, we had to inspect the other stretch of the road. The first around 30 km of the road looked good. We reached the 50-km mark. Potholes started appearing on the expressway again. The road near Kukripur, Borajpur and Dahiya Buzurg villages was damaged. During the return journey, we found 22 potholes in all. DBL company’s construction found to be worse During our journey on the Link Expressway, we found the road damaged at a total of 74 places. At several places, the patchwork had already come off. At many places, patchwork had not been done at all. We did not include the smaller potholes. As the expressway has started deteriorating, the company that built it has also come under discussion. It was built in two phases by two different companies. First stretch- From Jaitpur in Gorakhpur to Phulwaria was built by APCO Infratech. Second stretch- The stretch from Phulwaria to Salarpur was built by Dilip Buildcon Limited (DBL). On the ground, the work by APCO Infratech appeared better than that of DBL. In other words, the road built by DBL has deteriorated faster. You cannot drive at a speed of 80-90 kmph. Potholes at several places make the journey difficult. The possibility of accidents remains. Gorakhpur Link Expressway built to reduce travel time by 3 hours This expressway directly connects Gorakhpur to the Purvanchal Expressway near Azamgarh (Salarpur), making travel from Gorakhpur to Lucknow, Agra and Delhi easier. With its construction, the time taken to travel from Gorakhpur to Lucknow has been reduced by around 2 to 3 hours. When construction began in February 2020, its budget was Rs 5,876 crore. But by the time it was completed in 2025, the final budget had reached Rs 7,283 crore. The Gorakhpur Link Expressway has a total of 7 flyovers, 8 major bridges, 14 minor bridges and more than 100 underpasses. In 2023, when the expressway was under construction, the Ghaghra River changed its course near Kamahariaghat. This created difficulties in construction. The work was halted. The alignment was then changed and the bridge was made longer. On June 20, 2025, CM Yogi Adityanath inaugurated this four-lane expressway. Two-year agreement for toll collection At present, Highway Infrastructure Limited collects toll on this expressway. It has a two-year agreement, worth Rs 220 crore 66 lakh. Rs 105 crore has been fixed for the first year and Rs 115 crore for the second year, with a 10% increase. This means the company will have to pay around Rs 30 lakh per day to UPEIDA. The company will also have to deploy four vehicles for patrolling. Their job is to reduce road damage and the possibility of accidents. Who is responsible for filling potholes on the expressway? According to the official UPEIDA website, if any kind of damage occurs on the Gorakhpur Link Expressway during the five years after its inauguration (June 20, 2025), the responsibility lies with the two companies that built it. Both companies have appointed employees who repair the road from time to time. UPEIDA does not have to bear any expense for the repairs. So far, both companies have made public how much they have spent on repairs. If a complaint about potholes is received, repairs are carried out within 24 hours. Where there is major damage, it can take 2 to 10 days.

stories.title: Ghaziabad lawyer beaten with sticks 17 times on road:Attackers pushed wife too, threatened to kill them if they complained
stories.summary: Attackers beat a lawyer with sticks in Ghaziabad on Sunday afternoon. He was buying household items at a general store when five or six attackers dragged him away. They threw him onto the road, kicked and punched him, and hit him with around 17 sticks. They also pushed and manhandled the lawyer's wife when she came to save him. Nearby shopkeepers somehow rescued the lawyer and his wife. CCTV footage of the incident has surfaced. When Sahibabad police arrived after receiving the information, the lawyer told them, I had complained to government officials in Lucknow about the construction taking place next to my house. The youths took revenge for this. See 3 pictures.... Lawyer-neighbour dispute over construction work Ashish Pannu, a resident of Rajendra Nagar in the Sahibabad police station area, is a senior advocate at Delhi's Tis Hazari Court. Ashish said, "A basement has been built in a building adjoining my house. This has caused cracks to appear in my house." According to the lawyer, he had complained to police and government officials in Lucknow, which angered the accused. At around 1:40 p.m. today, I went with my wife, Preshika, and children by car to a grocery shop about 1 km from our home to buy provisions. After parking the car by the roadside, I went inside the shop. Meanwhile, five or six youths arrived there carrying sticks and clubs. One of them dragged me out of the shop and onto the road. After knocking me to the ground, they began beating me with kicks, punches and sticks. Hit with around 17 sticks, wife also pushed and beaten Ashish said that he was hit with around 17 sticks. His wife got out of the car and ran to save him. The accused also pushed and assaulted her. A grocery shopkeeper and people in the area somehow rescued both of them. The accused then left the spot. While abusing them, the attackers asked why they were complaining about Sushil Gupta's house. They also threatened to kill them if they filed another complaint. I have lodged a complaint against the attackers at Sahibabad police station. ACP Sahibabad Amit Saxena said: The case involving the assault of the lawyer is being investigated. A report will be registered on the basis of the complaint and action will be taken against the accused. The CCTV footage from the scene is also being examined.

stories.title: Sub-inspector beaten with shoes in Gorakhpur:Incident found to be fake, 2 youths held for staging it for likes and views
stories.summary: A video emerged in Gorakhpur on Sunday showing a sub-inspector being hit with a shoe on the road. In the video, a young man dressed as a lawyer stops the sub-inspector, who is riding a motorcycle. After an argument, he starts assaulting him. The sub-inspector then also starts beating the young man. The incident was said to have taken place in the Shahpur area. When the police had the video investigated, the incident turned out to be fake. It emerged that the video had been shot to gain likes and views. Both the sub-inspector and the lawyer were found to be fake. The police detained both young men by the evening. See 2 pictures... Now read what is shown in the video The video of the fake sub-inspector and lawyer is 2 minutes and 55 seconds long. It shows a youth wearing a black waistcoat and white shirt approaching the fake sub-inspector standing by the roadside. Two other boys are with him. The three surround the sub-inspector, who is sitting on a motorcycle. The youth asks, "Why did you take my father to the police station and keep him there?" The sub-inspector replies, "When you were not found at home, I had to take your father instead." The youth and the sub-inspector then begin fighting on the road. The youth hits the uniformed man with his shoe and abuses him. Some people also arrive and intervene. At this point, one of the youths says, "Call the MP and have him transferred." During this, the youth says, "The video has been recorded. Do whatever you can." SP City Nimish Patil said: A video from the Shahpur police station area is going viral. It shows a police personnel and an advocate appearing to argue. The video was examined and found to be fake. The policeman shown in the video is not from the police department. The person shown as the advocate is also fake.

stories.title: Auto catches fire after car collision in Jhansi:4 passengers suffer burns; woman says, ‘My legs were burnt, I crawled to safety’
stories.summary: Luxury car rammed an autorickshaw in Jhansi on Sunday morning. On impact, the autorickshaw burst into flames, with flames rising 20 feet into the air. Four people, including the driver, suffered burns. The injured were admitted to a medical college. The injured woman said, "I was thrown out of the autorickshaw after the collision. It was engulfed in flames. People were shouting, 'Run... run.' But my legs had already been burned and I could not run. So I crawled for 20 metres. Two boys then picked me up, took me away from the spot and saved my life." Meanwhile, after being informed about the fire, a fire brigade vehicle reached the spot and brought it under control by spraying water. The autorickshaw was completely gutted in the fire. The car driver fled after abandoning the vehicle at the spot. Police are investigating the matter. The accident took place near the Hansari railway crossing in the Sadar Bazar police station area. See 4 pictures of the accident... Savita was returning from hospital Savita Nagar, who lives in the ITI Colony under the jurisdiction of Sipri Bazar police station, works as a ward attendant at Babina MH Hospital. She was returning home by auto-rickshaw in the morning after completing her night duty. On the way, a car hit the auto-rickshaw with great force, causing it to suddenly burst into flames. "I somehow managed to survive." Meanwhile, Phooladevi said she was coming to Talpura to meet her nephew Kamlesh. She somehow survived the accident. Auto-rickshaw was travelling from Babina to Jhansi Kumer Yadav (50), a resident of Rasoi village in Babina, said, "I drive a CNG auto-rickshaw. On Sunday morning, I was travelling from Babina to Jhansi with five passengers in the auto-rickshaw. When I reached near the Hansari railway crossing, a Hyundai Verna car coming from the opposite direction came on the wrong side of the road and hit the auto-rickshaw forcefully." The car dragged the auto-rickshaw for around 10 metres after hitting it. The collision was so powerful that the auto-rickshaw immediately caught fire. Two young men were thrown out. The remaining passengers somehow got out of the auto-rickshaw. Kumer Yadav, Rajiv (31), a resident of Khailar, Fula Devi (70), a resident of Raja Ka Talab in Babina, and Savita Nagar (44), a resident of the ITI Colony, were injured after suffering injuries and burns in the accident. All four have been admitted to the Medical College. Police reached the spot after receiving information about the accident. The fire brigade was then called to the scene. After about half an hour of efforts, fire service personnel brought the blaze under control. By then, however, the auto-rickshaw had been completely gutted. Sadar Bazaar police station in-charge Shailendra Singh said all the injured were out of danger. They have been admitted to the Medical College. The cause of the accident is being investigated.

stories.title: 12-year-old girl dies of heart attack:Collapsed while sitting in school; body exhumed for post-mortem, report reveals cause
stories.summary: A 12-year-old student in Kushinagar died of a heart attack. She had suddenly fallen to the floor while sitting at school. This was revealed in the post-mortem report. Two days later, on Friday, the girl's body was exhumed and sent for a post-mortem on the district magistrate's instructions. Everyone was shocked when the cause of death emerged in the report on Saturday. The girl was cremated on Saturday. The entire incident took place in the Ramkola police station area, around 20 kilometres from the district headquarters. See the pictures... Read the full story Rajaram alias Bablu, a resident of Rampur Bhath village, works at a savoury snacks factory in Mumbai. Besides his wife, his family includes four children: Sonu Kumar (15), Neha (12), Vicky (9) and Gudiya (6). Neha was studying in Class 7 at the primary school in Mahuawa, near the village. Neha went to school on Wednesday morning. At around 10 a.m., she was sitting on a bench at the school when she suddenly collapsed on the floor. The incident caused panic at the school. There was no teacher at the school at the time. Her classmates raised the alarm and called her family members. They picked Neha up and took her to hospital, where doctors declared her dead. After her death, the family accused the teachers of negligence and delaying treatment. The family members also staged a protest with the body for around three hours. Family members calm down after SDM's intervention The family members calmed down after SDM Khadda Santram reasoned with them. They alleged that the village head had spread misinformation and exerted pressure to have the body buried without a post-mortem. Two days after the incident, the student's grandfather, Jawahir Bharti, asked District Magistrate Sanjay Chauhan to have his granddaughter's body exhumed and subjected to a post-mortem. Following his request, an order was issued to have the body exhumed. At around 5 p.m. on Friday, the body was exhumed in the presence of the Khadda SDM (Judicial/Magistrate) and Khadda Circle Officer Ajay Srivastava. It was then sent for a post-mortem. The post-mortem report emerged on Saturday, stating that the cause of the girl's death was a heart attack. Villagers were stunned to hear that the young girl had died of a heart attack. The family members were inconsolable after seeing the girl's body. Father says his daughter would have been alive if she had received timely treatment At around 5 p.m. on Saturday, the father lit his daughter's funeral pyre near the Dharamsamadha temple. He broke down and wept bitterly. He said, "If my daughter had received the right treatment on time, she would have been among us today." The father accused the school administration of negligence and delaying treatment. BSA suspends teacher After the girl's death, the school administration was also accused of negligence. Following this, Basic Education Officer Anil Kumar suspended teacher Yogendra Srivastava on Thursday. A two-member inquiry committee was also formed. The committee has been asked to submit its report within a week. Khadda CO Ajay Kumar Srivastava said: The post-mortem found that the cause of the girl's death was a heart attack. Her viscera has been preserved. He said that if the family submits a written complaint, an impartial investigation will be conducted and necessary legal action will be taken.

stories.title: Former IAS Divya Mittal to enter politics or move abroad?:Will reveal her decision in 2 days; new post offers 4 options
stories.summary: Will former IAS officer Divya Mittal enter politics or move abroad? She will reveal this after two days. She wrote on X, "What should I do next? I have read it. Four types of speculation are being made." First-the children are young. I will now stay at home. I will get a good package. I will move abroad again. I have written a book on the IAS. I will start a coaching institute. The ticket must already have been confirmed. I will enter politics. I will tell you about this at 8:30 a.m. on 29 September. Divya Mittal resigned from the service on 30 August. Her resignation was accepted on 14 September. Divya had left her job in London to join the civil services Divya is originally from Rewari, Haryana. After studying at IIT and IIM, she took up a job in London. It was there that she met Gagandeep Singh. The two had a love marriage. However, a few years later, the couple quit their jobs in London and returned to India. Divya began preparing for the UPSC examinations. She cleared the IPS examination on her first attempt without coaching. She was allotted the Gujarat cadre. Divya continued preparing for the IAS examination even during her IPS training. The following year, in 2013, she was selected for the IAS. Divya's husband is from Punjab and cleared the UPSC examination on his first attempt Divya's husband, Gagandeep Singh, comes from Giddarbaha in Punjab's Bathinda district. He completed a BTech in Chemical Engineering from IIT Delhi from 1998 to 2002. He then studied management at IIM Bangalore from 2003 to 2005. Gagandeep cleared the UPSC examination in his first attempt in 2010. He was allotted the Indian Trade Service. Four years ago, in 2022, he resigned as Joint Director General in the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

stories.title: SIR विवाद पर CM योगी का विपक्ष पर हमला, बोले- कांग्रेस और विपक्षी दल लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों को नुकसान पहुंचा रहे
stories.summary: SIR Controversy: उत्तर प्रदेश के मुख्यमंत्री योगी आदित्यनाथ ने विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण (SIR) को लेकर कांग्रेस समेत विपक्षी दलों पर निशाना साधा है। उन्होंने कहा कि मौजूदा चुनाव आयोग पहली बार ऐसा अभ्यास नहीं कर रहा है। योगी ने बताया कि साल 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965-66 और 2003 में भी इस तरह के पुनरीक्षण किए गए थे। उन्होंने कहा कि इसके बावजूद कांग्रेस, समाजवादी पार्टी, आरजेडी और अन्य दल मौजूदा SIR को लेकर भ्रम की स्थिति पैदा कर रहे हैं। योगी ने विपक्ष के इस रुख को बेहद दुर्भाग्यपूर्ण बताया और कहा कि राजनीतिक हितों के लिए संवैधानिक संस्थाओं को कमजोर करना लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों के लिए नुकसानदेह है।

stories.title: Engineer found half-naked dead in Ayodhya chemical plant:Had told mother an hour earlier that manager was harassing him
stories.summary: The body of a 25-year-old engineer was found in a chemical plant's tank in Ayodhya on Saturday night. The body was floating in the water tank in a semi-naked condition. The discovery triggered panic at the company. Police and the family reached the spot after being informed. The incident took place in the area under the jurisdiction of Darshan Nagar Police Outpost. The engineer's family suspected some people at the company of murdering him. His mother said her son Ashish had called one hour before the incident. He had told her that the manager was harassing him. The manager had also submitted a resignation letter from his system. According to the family, Ashish had deep injury marks on his body. However, the police have not yet confirmed that it was murder. The incident took place at around 1 a.m. at Yash Paper Mill in the area under the jurisdiction of Darshan Nagar Police Outpost. See 2 pictures... Read the full story Ashish Shivhare, 25, lived alone in Ayodhya. He was a chemical engineer at Yash Paper Mill. He was originally from Lok village in the Bisanda police station area of Banda. His father, Anand Shivhare, makes and sells batasha sweets. His entire family lives in Banda. Ashish was the eldest of his siblings. His two younger brothers are Abhishek and Jatin. His two elder sisters are Gayatri and Jyoti. Both are married and live in Bengaluru. Pratibha is his youngest sister. Ashish was the only earning member of the family. Ashish completed his intermediate studies in Kanpur. After that, he completed a degree in chemical engineering in Punjab. Around three years ago, he started working as a chemical engineer at Yash Paper Mill in Ayodhya. No CCTV cameras had been installed at the scene Ashish's uncle, Sunil Shivhare, said his body was found naked in a tank at the treatment plant. He was lying face down. There were injury marks on several parts of his body. These marks have raised several questions. Ashish's uncle, Rakesh Shivhare, said that despite the factory being so large, CCTV cameras had not been installed at the incident site. The cameras previously installed there had also been removed. He alleged that a man named Abhishek Singh had taken ₹3 lakh from Ashish. Even after that, he continued demanding money from him and harassing him. Ashish had told his family several times that he was being harassed by the manager. Mother says son called at night to tell her about his troubles Ashish's mother, Kanka Shivhare, said her son had called between around 10:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. on Saturday night. He had said, "Mum, please speak to my manager. He is harassing me a lot." Ashish had said that the manager had typed his resignation himself using Ashish's laptop and sent it to the company. He learnt that the resignation had been sent after receiving an email at night. This left him panic-stricken. Mother said, "The claim about stock market money is false" After this, his mother called the manager. According to her, the manager said that Ashish was asking him for loan money. He was threatening to die by suicide if he did not receive the money. The mother told him that she did not need any money, only that her son should be safe. The manager said he would go look for Ashish. However, he later called to say that Ashish could not be found. His mother said the claim about money related to the stock market was false. She said Ashish had given ₹3 lakh to Abhishek Singh and was demanding his money back. Sister said-Manager would not grant leave Ashish's sister, who is studying in Bengaluru, said her brother often told her that the manager harassed him. He was made to work until late at night. Ashish wanted to quit his job and return home, but the manager would not grant him leave. He was unable to leave the job either. The family has filed a complaint with the police. They have demanded an impartial investigation and action in the case. Police said: Cause of death will become clear from the post-mortem report The police have sent the body for a post-mortem examination. They said the exact cause of death would be known after the post-mortem report is released. The scene is being examined. The police are investigating the case from all angles, including an accident and exposure to chemicals. Further action will be taken based on the facts uncovered during the investigation.

stories.title: Smriti Irani, Harish Dwivedi, Varun Gandhi may go Rajya Sabha:Announcement likely in October; BJP likely to win 8 out of 10 seats
stories.summary: The BJP is expected to win eight of the 10 Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh, while the Samajwadi Party is likely to secure two, with the BJP expected to announce its candidates in the first week of October. According to party sources, former Union minister Smriti Irani and former Basti MP Harish Dwivedi, who recently secured positions in the BJP’s national organisation, are almost certain to enter the Rajya Sabha from Uttar Pradesh. Why are Smriti Irani and Harish Dwivedi the leading contenders? The BJP has an established tradition of sending its national general secretaries to the Rajya Sabha. This gives the leaders an opportunity to put forward their views in Parliament. Their stature and protocol remain intact during organisational tours across the country. Smriti Irani served as the national president of the BJP Mahila Morcha from 2010 to 2013. In 2014, she contested the election against Rahul Gandhi from Amethi. Although she lost the election, the party, recognising her stature, entrusted her with the Human Resource Development (HRD) Ministry in the Modi government's first term. In 2019, she defeated Rahul Gandhi in Amethi to register a historic victory and became a Union minister again. After losing to Congress candidate Kishori Lal Sharma in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, she remained engaged in organisational work like an ordinary party worker. Recently, BJP national president JP Nadda entrusted her with the significant responsibility of national general secretary. Against this backdrop, the party is making full preparations to send her to Parliament (Rajya Sabha) from Uttar Pradesh's quota. Harish Dwivedi worked on the ground as a full-time RSS organiser until 2004. He later became the BJP Yuva Morcha's state general secretary and then its state president. He contested the Assembly election from Basti Sadar in 2012 but finished third. In 2014 and 2019, he was elected as the MP from Basti for two consecutive terms. His track record in the organisation has been outstanding; he served as national secretary in former national president J.P. Nadda's team, played an important role in the Assam and Rajasthan elections, and was recently appointed the party's national general secretary and given charge of major states such as Karnataka and Bihar. Given his rising stature in the organisation, his entry into the Rajya Sabha is considered almost certain. Plan to strike a caste balance for the 2027 elections With the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in mind, the BJP will pay special attention to social engineering in this Rajya Sabha election. According to sources, one or two Brahmin, one or two Thakur, three to four Other Backward Class (OBC) and one or two Dalit leaders may be given an opportunity for the eight seats. These 10 leaders are in the race for the remaining six seats

stories.title: ‘Votes are being deleted on large scale in Noida’:Akhilesh Yadav claims BJP hired private companies
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday urged the court to consider former Chief Election Commissioner S.Y. Quraishi’s demand for fresh elections in Bihar and West Bengal, saying it should take cognisance if questions are being raised over irregularities in the electoral process. He also accused the BJP of getting votes deleted across Uttar Pradesh, alleging that Samajwadi Party votes were removed at the booth level and that the BJP hired a private company to fill out Form 7 to get voters’ names deleted. On Sunday, Yadav also honoured around 18 wrestlers from various districts of Uttar Pradesh at the party office in Lucknow. Read the key points from Akhilesh Yadav's press conference... 1- Votes being deleted on a large scale in Noida Akhilesh Yadav said, "I have heard that votes are being deleted on a large scale in Noida. In the same way, votes of Samajwadis were deleted at booth level across the state. A large number of votes were deleted after people were made to fill out Form 7. In Lucknow, more than 100 votes were deleted under the name of a single person, whereas according to the rules, one person cannot have more than five votes deleted." Akhilesh said that Nandlal Nishad had been fielded from here. Votes were deleted using his signature, even though he did not even know how to sign. In 2022, officials deleted votes without following any rules or laws. In 2024, we were vigilant, which is why we managed to win in Uttar Pradesh. 2- Police Accused of Casting Votes in Plain Clothes During Bypoll Akhilesh also made allegations regarding the bypoll. He said that the police personnel in plain clothes had cast votes, describing the manner in which the bypoll had been manipulated. He said, "What can you expect from people who steal from temples and steal offerings?" 3- Those speaking in favour of the Election Commission are also involved in the scam On Chief Minister Yogi speaking in favour of the Election Commission, Akhilesh said, "If the Chief Minister is speaking in favour of the Election Commission, does that mean we should consider the Chief Minister involved in the election scam?" 4- On the Congress-Samajwadi Party's verbal spat, said, 'This fight is only for show' On the verbal spat between the Congress and the Samajwadi Party, Akhilesh said that they, too, were learning from their opponents. "This fight is only for show. We, too, have learnt from their strategy. We will fight together. Our sole aim is to remove the BJP." 5- If the BJP is removed, the water will be removed Akhilesh targeted the BJP government over waterlogging in Uttar Pradesh. He said, "If Uttar Pradesh is waterlogged, the BJP is responsible." From the mayor, MLAs and MPs to the government, the BJP is in power, but just look at the condition of the cities. Akhilesh said the BJP government had created a situation in which pumps would now have to be installed across Lucknow to drain the water. He said, "The water will recede only when the BJP is removed." 6- On Gyanesh Kumar's visit being cancelled, said, ‘It was a good decision’ Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav said it was good that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's visit to Uttar Pradesh was cancelled; otherwise, Gen Z would have protested in its own way. He said, "We had gone carrying a shroud for the Election Commission." Gyanesh Kumar's proposed programmes in Meerut and Varanasi were postponed in September. The Election Commission later described it as the normal process of changing the dates of programmes. 7- The government sends you to jail for showing the truth Akhilesh said this government is such that if you show it the truth, it sends you to jail. He alleged that a person from Baghpat was illegally detained at a police station for two days. That person has already received an honour from the President. He said so many videos had come from Gorakhpur that the government would now be unable to take action against anyone.

stories.title: Yogi targets SP-Congress over EVM remarks:UP CM says questioning CEC is inappropriate; winning is fine, but they blame EVMs when they lose
stories.summary: Amid the controversy surrounding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, CM Yogi held a press conference in Lucknow on Sunday and lashed out at the Samajwadi Party and Congress. He said, "The Congress, Samajwadi Party, RJD and other opposition parties are creating a huge uproar over this year's SIR exercise. This is unfortunate." He said: "They are defaming India by putting the Election Commission, the Chief Election Commissioner and every constitutional institution in the dock. Their intention to weaken democracy is extremely shocking. They should control their irresponsible actions. There is no place in a democracy for violence, vandalism and disinformation." He said, "If opposition parties win an election, it is a reflection of their own efforts. But when the public rejects them because of corruption, economic misconduct, bad policies and anarchy, they blame the Election Commission and EVMs. These parties should reflect on their childish statements." Read the CM's three key points 1- Opposition parties spread confusion over SIR The CM said these people were working to damage India's constitutional institutions. They had been part of every conspiracy to weaken democratic values for political gain. They had spread confusion over SIR. SIR had not been conducted for the first time. It had been conducted several times before in the country, including in 1952, 1957, 1961, 1965-66, and 2003. These people have been continuously attacking the Election Commission over this round of SIR. The Congress, which has ruled the country for the longest period, has been consistently putting the Election Commission in the dock. Instructions had already been issued regarding SIR that voters who had been left out were free to fill in the form. The Supreme Court has upheld the Election Commission's action regarding Form 6. 2- Congress questioned the Army's valour - this is not patriotism Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi had questioned the impartiality of India's judiciary in Cambridge. In 2019, the CAG had given its observation on the Rafale issue, and the Congress had questioned that as well. The Congress formed governments at the Centre and in several states through elections conducted using EVMs. Calling those same EVMs a black box and questioning India's electoral system and democracy is unfortunate. These people do not believe in constitutional and democratic values. Through their corrupt functioning, they have consistently compromised the country's security. They questioned the valour and courage of India's brave soldiers during the Balakot air strike and Operation Sindoor. This is not patriotism. The Opposition parties are engaging in similar acts at present. 3- Opposition parties should apologise to the common people and constitutional institutions All three Election Commissioners have clarified before the media the functioning of the Election Commission, the voters left out, and Form 6. There are no questions left now. Despite this, the Congress, the Samajwadi Party and their allies continue splitting hairs. This is unfortunate. Every adult in India has the right to vote, regardless of caste, region, language, or gender. Voters also have the right to have their names added to the electoral roll until a day before the election. Questioning such a completely transparent process is tantamount to weakening the democratic system. Opposition parties should apologise to ordinary people and constitutional institutions for their stance. Understand the full case related to the removal of the CEC... According to The Indian Express report dated 23 September, two Election Commissioners recorded written objections to the SIR at least 14 times over the past 10 months. Four of these objections were raised on the same day. However, the Election Commission had said that such objections were part of the normal process. All final decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously. Read what the opposition leaders had said...

stories.title: ‘Mayor sahab, get out of the car, is this Spain':Traders surround mayor during Gorakhpur waterlogging inspection with municipal commissioner
stories.summary: Traders in Gorakhpur confronted Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain and Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava on Saturday when they arrived to inspect waterlogging in the area. The traders surrounded the mayor’s car and said, “Mayor sahab, this is Spain. Get out of the car and step into the water. Only then will you understand the problem. The entire drain is clogged, but no one is listening.” ‘You sought votes here three years ago, but the problem remains’ The traders reminded the mayor that he had visited the same area and stepped into the water while campaigning for votes. They said three years had passed since then, but the area continued to get waterlogged whenever it rained. They told the mayor that despite repeated complaints, the waterlogging problem had not been resolved. Mayor assures traders of a solution The mayor listened to the traders while remaining seated in his car and assured them that the problem would be resolved. He then left the spot. A video of the incident has also surfaced. Now read what was shown in the video Gorakhpur received heavy rain on Saturday, leaving several roads waterlogged. Later in the evening, Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava and Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain travelled together to inspect the affected areas. When their vehicle reached Sahabganj grocery market, angry traders stopped it and raised slogans over the prolonged waterlogging problem. ‘Work is being done only on paper’: Traders A 2:13-minute video of the incident shows traders surrounding the mayor’s vehicle from all sides. The traders alleged that officials had been posted in the area for years, but no one had visited to listen to their problems. They said the mayor had visited the area for the first time since the election. The traders alleged that development work was being carried out only on paper and that waterlogging in Sahabganj market during the monsoon damaged goods worth lakhs of rupees. They said they had to bear the losses from their own pockets every year. ‘You will come today, but not again’: Traders The mayor’s driver told the traders that the work in Sahabganj market would be taken up after the rains. The traders responded, “You will come today, but you will never come again after this.” The traders also criticised the administration, alleging that authorities did not spend even ₹1 on solving their problems while traders were left to bear the financial losses. They said the mayor should have inspected the area before the monsoon. Mayor says pumps used to drain water from waterlogged areas Mayor Dr Manglesh Srivastava said, “Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain had been asked to speak to traders and find a solution to the waterlogging problem.” He said, “Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath would also be informed about the issue. Pumps were operated wherever possible to drain the accumulated water.” He added that said public participation was necessary to address such civic issues. Read what the traders said... ‘Waterlogging continues despite construction of new drain’: Traders’ association Traders’ association general secretary Manish Gupta said that rainwater continued to accumulate in the area despite the construction of a new drain. He stated that traders had repeatedly complained to the municipal corporation about the waterlogging, but no permanent solution had been found. At times, the old drain was blamed for the problem, while on other occasions, inadequate cleaning was cited as the reason. Gupta said temporary cleaning and water drainage arrangements were made whenever the problem arose during the monsoon, but no permanent solution had been implemented. ‘Waterlogging has caused losses of more than ₹10 crore’: Kirana Committee Umesh Chand Madheshia, former president and patron of the Kirana Committee said, “Traders were angry over the waterlogging and their frustration increased when the mayor’s vehicle reached the market.” He said, “Traders wanted officials to step into the water and see the losses caused by the flooding, but they remained seated in the vehicle.” Madheshia claimed that traders across Sahabganj market had suffered losses of more than ₹10 crore because of the waterlogging.

stories.title: Video of Premanandji’s disciple falling from a rooftop:Suddenly fell onto the road in front of passers-by in Vrindavan; suffered a head injury
stories.summary: A video has emerged showing a 25-year-old disciple of Sant Premanand Maharaj falling from the 4th floor in Vrindavan. It shows the disciple, Rasik Dulari Sharan, suddenly falling feet-first onto the road from a height of 40 feet. His head hits the ground and splits open. He begins writhing in pain. At the same time, two cyclists are passing by. One of them is a disciple wearing yellow clothes. Both are left stunned by the sight. In addition, a water-supply vehicle arrives at the same spot at that moment. Disciple Rasik Dulari Sharan committed suicide at 10:35 a.m. on 25 September. Dainik Bhaskar received the exclusive video today. After the post-mortem was conducted late on Saturday evening, his family cremated him on the banks of the Yamuna. His younger brother Manish lit the funeral pyre. During this, his mother and sister became unconscious while crying. See two pictures- Cut marks found on private parts during post-mortem Rasik Dulari Sharan Das's post-mortem was conducted by a panel of two doctors. It was also videographed. According to the preliminary report, injury marks were found on the body, on the head, legs, and waist. There were also cut marks on the private parts. The body was then handed over to the family. After the post-mortem, it was brought by ambulance to the Yamuna riverbank. His mother, Laung Devi, sister Machhla, brother Manish, and brother-in-law Sonu Patel arrived in vehicles. More than 10 people associated with the ashram also arrived. After the cremation, everyone left for the ashram. Rasik Dulari walked on the roof, then jumped Rasik Dulari had been living for 3 months in the four-storey Guru Kripa Kunj building in the Varaha Ghat area. The building belongs to Premanand Maharaj's trust, Keli Kunj. More than 50 disciples and sevadars associated with Premanandji's ashram live there. The building is 500 metres from Premanand's old Keli Kunj ashram. According to the police, at around 11 a.m. on Friday, Rasik Dulari Sharan went to the building's fourth floor. He sat there for some time and then fell from the building. He was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in critical condition, where he died. According to eyewitnesses, Rasik Dulari was bleeding from his private parts. A grinder bearing bloodstains was found in the room. It is suspected that the disciple had injured his private parts with the grinder. Mother said - We were not allowed to meet him Rasik's family members arrived after receiving information about the incident. On Saturday morning, his mother and sister broke down after seeing the body at the post-mortem house. His mother said, "I spoke to my son for the last time two years ago. We were informed that he had fallen. We came here in haste. We had come to meet him before as well, but we were not allowed to meet him. God will take action against those responsible." Took initiation from Premanandji two years ago and changed his name Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. He came to Vrindavan two years ago and took initiation from Premanandji. He subsequently changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. He knew electrical work, so he was assigned this service at the ashram. Deepak was the second of two brothers and one sister. The eldest was his sister, followed by Deepak. His younger brother is Manish. Their mother, Laung Bai, came to Vrindavan a year ago. She stayed elsewhere for five days. During this period, Deepak continued to meet her. He is also said to have completed a 3,000-km Narmada pilgrimage. Unanswered questions: Why did he commit suicide? Police examining mobile phone City SP Rajeev Kumar said, "The family has filed a complaint at the police station. They have alleged that they were not allowed to meet Rasik. Their allegations are being investigated." Meanwhile, CO Sandeep Singh said: The forensic team found some suspicious items in the room, which are being examined. The police are trying to find out who Rasik Dulari spoke to before the incident and the circumstances in which it took place. Mobile phone data is being examined for this.

stories.title: Cleanliness drive held at Namo Ghat in Varanasi:Namami Gange team administers pledge for a clean Ganga
stories.summary: Namami Gange organised a special cleanliness and awareness campaign at Namo Ghat on Sunday (27 Sept) to mark World Rivers Day and World Tourism Day. During the campaign, people were urged to take a pledge to keep the Ganga clean, with the message that clean rivers can help boost tourism. Volunteers clean Ganga riverbank, spread awareness Rajesh Shukla, Namami Gange Kashi region coordinator and cleanliness brand ambassador of the Municipal Corporation, led a volunteer team in cleaning the Ganga riverbank at Namo Ghat. He said clean rivers attract tourists, which in turn supports the local economy and tourism industry while helping maintain ecological balance. ‘Civilisation cannot grow without rivers’ Ganga volunteer Rajesh Shukla said no civilisation can develop without rivers. He described the Ganga as a symbol of India’s cultural heritage and said Indian civilisation and tourism are incomplete without the river. He administered the ‘Ganga Oath’ to those present and appealed to tourists visiting the Ganga to act responsibly by not throwing any kind of garbage or waste into the river. Hundreds of tourists participate in campaign Hundreds of tourists participated in the campaign. Those present included Namami Gange Kashi region coordinator Rajesh Shukla, Avinash Tiwari, Ruchi Pathak, Goldie Pathak, Avinash Pathak and Vishal Bhardwaj.

stories.title: Arms smuggler arrested in Gorakhpur:Police recover automatic pistol; he allegedly bought it from Lawrence Bishnoi gang
stories.summary: Cantt police arrested Karan Sonkar, an alleged member of an interstate illegal arms smuggling gang, in Gorakhpur on Saturday. An illegal .32-bore automatic pistol was recovered from his possession. In the same case, absconding accused Pramod Yadav, a resident of Unaula Khas in Bansgaon, and Raju Yadav, a resident of Mirzapur in Khorabar, surrendered before the court on September 24. Police are questioning the two accused and preparing to recover the pistols allegedly linked to them as part of the investigation. ‘I bought the pistol for ₹25,000’: Accused tells police According to police, Karan Sonkar, a resident of Kori Tola in Gorakhnath area’s Dharmshala Bazaar, told investigators during questioning that he had purchased the pistol from Shreyansh Yadav for ₹25,000. On September 14, the STF arrested five alleged arms smugglers, including Shreyansh Yadav alias Bablu, near Vindhyavasini Park in the Cantonment area. Police said Bablu had links with the Lawrence Bishnoi and Goldy Brar gangs. Four pistols, four magazines, a .32-bore revolver and cartridges were recovered from the accused. During interrogation, police gathered information about an interstate arms-smuggling network. STF Inspector Satyaprakash Singh subsequently registered a case against 31 accused in connection with the matter. Police to question two accused who surrendered in court Police said Pramod Yadav and Raju Yadav surrendered before the court on September 24. The investigating officer will visit the district jail on Monday to record their statements. After this, police will seek their remand from the court and begin the process of recovering the weapons based on their disclosures. Investigators will also question the two about whom they allegedly purchased the weapons from, how much they paid and what role they played in the interstate arms-smuggling network.

stories.title: Rain destroys crops across UP:3 killed in Lakhimpur, trees fall on roads in Bahraich; reports from 5 districts
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is reeling from heavy rain. Several districts have been receiving rain for more than 40 hours. Roads are waterlogged, farmers' crops have been submerged, trees have fallen in several places because of strong winds, and mud houses have collapsed elsewhere. The situation is extremely serious. Schools have been closed for children. Lakhimpur in Uttar Pradesh has been receiving continuous rain for the past two days. A mud house collapsed after water accumulated in a rural area. Three people died after being trapped under the rubble. Crops have suffered heavy damage in Jalaun because of the rain. Farmers said their sesame crop had been completely destroyed by the torrential rain. Several trees fell onto roads in Bahraich because of heavy rain and strong winds. Farmers' crops were uprooted. Farmers in the district have suffered significant losses because of the rain. Paddy crops were submerged in Sultanpur because of the heavy rain. Banana crops were also destroyed. As many as 1,070 electricity poles were uprooted. Eighty-nine transformers were also damaged. Three people died in Barabanki after houses and trees collapsed due to the rain, while six others were seriously injured. Farmers said the rain had destroyed six months of their hard work. In Deoria, paddy crops fell flat in the fields due to strong winds and rain. According to farmers, the paddy crops of more than 40 per cent of farmers were affected. This caused financial losses to the farmers. The threat of sudden flooding is looming over 32 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Farmers have suffered the greatest losses due to the rain. They are working in their fields even in the rain to save their crops. Read reports from six districts of Uttar Pradesh- Water fills fields in Lakhimpur Intermittent torrential rain over the past 36 to 48 hours has disrupted normal life in Lakhimpur Kheri. The continuous rain has caused waterlogging from the city to rural areas. Conditions are worse in the Rahmatpur and Neemgaon areas of Mitauli tehsil. Fields and roads in the areas along the Sharda and Ghaghara rivers have also been flooded. A mud house collapsed in Rahmatpur village in the Mitauli area because of the rain. Three members of the same family died after being buried under the debris. The deceased were identified as Mohan Kashyap (50), his wife Sarita (45) and their approximately eight-year-old son. Villagers say the culvert built for water drainage in the village has been blocked for a long time. As a result, rainwater is unable to drain out, and waterlogging in the low-lying areas is continuing to worsen. The villagers have demanded that the drainage system be restored. The impact of the rain has also begun to show on the crops. The standing paddy crop has started falling as water has accumulated in the fields. Farmers say that if the water is not drained soon, the paddy crop will rot. The sugarcane crop has also bent in the fields because of strong winds. Banana and oilseed crops have also been damaged. DM Anjani Kumar Singh inspected the situation in the city on Saturday amid continuous rain and incidents of waterlogging and fallen trees. The DM directed officials to ensure proper drainage. He also ordered the immediate removal of trees that had fallen at several places in the city. Power has been disrupted for the past 20 hours in Mailani town in Lakhimpur and several surrounding villages. Poles and wires were broken after trees fell in the Dudhwa Buffer Zone. House collapses due to rain in Jalaun Heavy rain that has continued for the past 36 hours in Jalaun has caused extensive damage to farmers' crops. The villages in the Konch and Orai tehsils have been the worst affected. Farmers said the rain had completely destroyed their sesame crop. They said they had not received any relief of any kind from the government. An old and dilapidated house suddenly came crashing down in the Kajipura neighbourhood of Jalaun's Kalpi town on Saturday morning. After their house collapsed, the poor family is facing a housing crisis. The family said their household belongings were destroyed when the house collapsed. They are not in a position to rebuild it. The affected family has demanded financial assistance and compensation. Meanwhile, a mud house suddenly collapsed in Udaotpura village under the Rampura development block. The entire incident was captured on camera. Toll-free number issued in Bahraich In view of the bad weather, heavy rain, lightning and thunderstorms in Bahraich, District Magistrate Rajesh Kumar Pandey has directed officials to remain alert. In all the tehsils of Bahraich, several trees fell onto roads due to rain and strong winds. The Forest Department is removing them. More than 30 electricity poles also fell in Tejwapur, Kaiserganj, Fakharpur and other areas. Banana, paddy and sugarcane crops spread over thousands of bighas were destroyed. In view of the situation, the District Magistrate has directed all officials to immediately share reports of the incidents on the WhatsApp group. Information should also be provided on the control room telephone number 05252-230132 and toll-free number 1077. The tehsil administration has been instructed to visit the affected areas and survey damaged houses, livestock, crops and other losses, so that relief can be provided to affected people at the earliest. Banana trees fell in Sultanpur Paddy crops in Sultanpur have been badly affected by continuous rain over the past 48 hours. Electricity poles have also fallen at several places. Around 25-30 per cent of the paddy crops in the Koorebhar, Dhanpatganj, Baldirai, Kadipur, Karaundikala, Jaisinghpur, Motigarpur, Bhadaiya and Dubepur block areas have been damaged by the rain. Farmer Raunak Singh said the standing paddy crop on his approximately four-bigha field had been destroyed by the rain. The crop had already produced panicles, and the grains were yet to develop. Meanwhile, the continuous rain affected the entire crop. Ram Ujagir Verma, a resident of Aanapur, said, "We had planted 800 banana trees, which were almost ready for harvest. Of these, 300 trees fell when they were fully mature." Anil Verma, a farmer from the Kurebhar block area, said six bighas of early paddy crop were nearing maturity. Of this, around two bighas of the crop had been flattened by the rain. Meanwhile, more than 1.5 lakh people in the Motigarpur block area are without electricity. Around 20 electricity poles have been uprooted in Motigarpur, Barausa, Pahadpur, Hamzabad, Indodach and Diyara, which are served by the Diyara power substation. More than 50,000 people connected to the Dhema, Saraiya, Gopalpur and Pandeybaba feeders have been facing a power crisis for two days. Paddy crop affected in Deoria Intermittent rain and strong winds over the past three days have affected both daily life and agriculture in Deoria. Strong winds and rain caused large quantities of paddy crops to collapse in the fields. According to farmers, the paddy crops of approximately more than 40 percent of farmers have been affected. Trees also fell at several places in the district because of the rain and strong winds. This disrupted traffic on the roads. The trees were removed from the roads with the help of local residents and the departments concerned. An old house collapsed amid rain in the Salempur area. People faced difficulties as electricity remained disrupted for 8 to 10 hours in more than a dozen neighbourhoods of Deoria headquarters. The prolonged bad weather has affected people's daily lives. Fields waterlogged in Barabanki Continuous rain for nearly 55 hours and strong winds have disrupted normal life in Barabanki. Three people have died in separate incidents amid the bad weather so far, while six people are reported to have been seriously injured. The continuous rain has increased the risk of mud houses and trees collapsing in rural areas. Continuous rain in Barabanki has affected farmers the most. The paddy crop had ripened and was standing ready in the fields, but strong rain and winds have flattened the crop in several areas. With water accumulating in the fields, fears of the paddy being damaged have increased. In view of the continuing bad weather, the challenge for the administration and relief teams has also intensified. People in rural areas remain concerned about mud houses, trees and electricity poles.
