stories.title: Crorepati businessman murdered, son wanted to frame uncle:Changed plan 20 days earlier; planted evidence at 3 Kanpur locations to frame daughter-in-law
stories.summary: A luxurious flat in Kanpur’s posh Kalyanpur area, contracts to supply medicines across Uttar Pradesh, and a turnover of Rs 60 crore, all this made people believe that Vineet Minocha’s family was living a prosperous and happy life. But the hatred that had grown among the family members was far more disturbing. On the night of September 5, Vineet was stabbed 17 times. He was tortured and killed, with the attackers continuing to assault him until his last breath. Within 24 hours, Kanpur Police stunned everyone by arresting his daughter-in-law Shalu. Police cited three reasons behind the murder: Shalu remained in jail for 20 days. Then, on September 24, police brought her husband Subrat before the media. The entire story changed. The killer was not Shalu, but her husband Subrat. According to police, Subrat had paid his former employee Vishal ₹6 lakh to carry out the murder. The conspiracy was not limited to eliminating his father. Subrat also wanted to frame his uncle, Puneet Minocha, for the murder. But he knew that he would not be able to mislead police against his uncle for long. So, through Vishal, he diverted the entire investigation towards his wife. For 25 days before the murder, he began creating evidence against his wife so that once the investigation started, police would naturally be led to Shalu. Read the complete conspiracy behind the murder of the millionaire businessman in today’s Sunday Big Story… What trick did Subrat use to create evidence against his wife? DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said Subrat had hated his father, Vineet Minocha, for a long time, but had started planning his murder around one to two months earlier. He knew that after his father was eliminated, his brother, Subrat’s uncle Puneet, would come after him and try to find out the truth behind his brother’s death. There could also be a dispute over the property. So, Subrat wanted to kill two birds with one stone, murder his father and make his uncle appear to be the killer. He shared the plan with Vishal. Vishal used to work at Subrat’s shop but had been fired by Vineet seven months earlier. While planning the murder, the two also knew that Puneet had a strong network in the city and would make every possible effort to prove his innocence. So, around 25 days before the murder, they changed their plan. Subrat decided to portray his own wife as the mastermind of the conspiracy. To create evidence, around 20 days before the murder, Subrat took his wife Shalu to Parade Chauraha, where they met Vishal. All three then went together in a car to Z Square Mall at Bada Chauraha for shopping. Subrat remained seated in the car while Shalu and Vishal went inside the mall to shop. The idea was to make Vishal appear with Shalu in public. Later, when police checked their mobile locations, Shalu’s location would appear alongside Vishal’s. Subrat then took both of them to the Banarasi Tea Stall on 80 Feet Road. From there, a duplicate key for a lock was also made at Lareb’s shop in Juhi Param Purwa. Subrat paid the ₹100 cost through Vishal. Subrat also accompanied Vishal to a doctor for his treatment. At the other two locations, he kept his wife with him but remained seated in the car, sending Vishal and Shalu together into public places. Murder night: Vineet mistook Vishal for a thief, forcing him to change the plan Then came the night of September 5, when Subrat had planned to have his father killed. Between 6 pm and 8 pm, Subrat called Vishal four times. Vishal knew he could not carry out the murder alone, so he also involved his friend Raj Kishore. As planned, Subrat left home with his wife Shalu at around 9.30 pm for a party. Before leaving, he switched off the CCTV cameras in the apartment. At 9.45 pm, Vishal and Raj Kishore entered the flat using the original key, which Subrat had already handed over to Vishal. The plan was based on the fact that businessman Vineet usually went to sleep by around 10 pm. Subrat had instructed Vishal and Raj Kishore to suffocate Vineet by pressing a pillow over his face. There was to be no sign of a struggle in the room, so that the family would assume in the morning that he had died a natural death from a heart attack. Vishal and Raj Kishore entered the businessman’s room and hid there. They waited until 11.30 pm, but Vineet was unable to sleep. When he finally entered the room and switched on the light, he saw Vishal. Thinking he was a thief, Vineet shouted, ‘Save me, thief… save me.’ Vishal panicked. He was carrying a knife and attacked Vineet with it. He stabbed him 17 times before fleeing the flat with Raj Kishore. This became the major mistake that led police to Vishal within just 14 hours. The two men had been captured on CCTV cameras installed outside the apartment. Subrat was already prepared for such a situation. As part of his plan, Vishal named Shalu before the police. Subrat had cleverly made Vishal receive calls from Shalu’s mobile phone. Kanpur Police arrested Shalu and sent her to jail within 24 hours without conducting an in-depth investigation. Uncle says, ‘I am shocked. Why did my nephew want to frame me?’ As questions continued to emerge in the case, Subrat and Vishal were confronted during their custody remand. Their conversations contained so many contradictions that police quickly realised the two were hiding something. During questioning in a closed room, Subrat broke down and confessed to the crime. Subrat told police that he wanted to blame for the murder on his uncle Puneet Minocha, but could not find any concrete reason to frame him. He then decided to have the allegations levelled against his wife Shalu instead. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Puneet Minocha. He said, I have been living separately from my elder brother Vineet Minocha for the past 37 years. My house is in Signature City, Nawabganj. I am in the construction business. I am also shocked that Subrat wanted to frame me because we rarely met. We never even had an argument, let alone a fight. Son says, ‘It’s good that I was arrested, otherwise I would have killed myself’ Subrat was arrested on September 24. He said, I have no regret about getting my father killed. He was a womaniser. My only regret is that he should not have been stabbed like this. I did not want him to be killed in such a manner. When Shalu was sent to jail, I felt guilty. I started taking sleeping pills. If the police had not arrested me, I would have committed suicide. Subrat further said, My father had affairs with several women. I was afraid that he might marry one of them and bring her home. She would then become a shareholder in the property. I was dependent on him even for every rupee, while my father used to show me pictures of himself partying with girls in Goa. I had a debt of around ₹40 lakh. My father gave me only ₹40,000 as pocket money. He treated me like an employee. Shalu may leave jail and return to her parents’ home After spending 20 days in jail, the way has now been cleared for Shalu’s release. Police are preparing to file a closure report in court regarding her role in the case. Shalu’s lawyer Shivakant Dixit told Dainik Bhaskar that no application had been filed by police in court till Friday. The court will remain closed on Saturday and Sunday. Shalu is therefore likely to walk out of jail by Monday.

stories.title: Degree colleges built in UP forests and fields:No proper access roads; students only come for exams, cheating arranged
stories.summary: Several private degree colleges in Uttar Pradesh have been opened in forests and deserted areas. Some do not even have a proper road leading to them. The apparent reason: so that officials cannot easily reach these colleges for inspections. Universities have also granted affiliation without proper scrutiny. These colleges are practically running on their own. Classes are not held regularly throughout the year, and students often come only for exams. Colleges allegedly allow students to use unfair means during exams, attracting students from far-off areas. Dainik Bhaskar investigated how these colleges came up in such locations, what their actual condition is, and how they charge students two to three times the prescribed fee while allegedly assuring them that they will pass. In three districts, we caught college principals, teachers and managers on hidden cameras while they discussed the sale of degrees and other arrangements. Our investigation found several major irregularities: These colleges in Auraiya, Farrukhabad and Etah offer courses ranging from BA and BSc to BEd and BTC. Here is the complete investigation. Auraiya: College in the middle of fields, no classes, not a single student Around 20 km from Auraiya district headquarters, Sri Krishna Saroj Mahavidyalaya is located in Kakore. There is no proper road from the main highway to the college. After travelling around 500 metres through fields, the building comes into view. The classrooms were locked and there were no students on the campus. We met principal Dr Anil Kumar Tiwari. A conversation with him on a hidden camera revealed how the college operates. Reporter: When did the college start and which university is it affiliated with? Principal: The college has been running since 2014. It has affiliation from Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur, for BA, BSc, BEd and BTC. Reporter: There is no road to the college? Principal: Gravel was laid here earlier, but because of objections from local people, the road could not be constructed. Reporter: How many students and teachers are there? Principal: There are currently 678 students and 18 teachers. Including other staff, around 30 people work here. Around 12 of them travel daily from Kanpur. Most are BEd and BTC teachers. They are supposed to stay till 3 pm, but if they say, ‘Sir, let us leave,’ we allow them to go. The only condition is that classes should not be disturbed. Reporter: So, are regular classes being held? Principal: Nobody comes regularly. Around 10–20% of students attend BEd and D.El.Ed classes. No one attends BSc classes. Reporter: Why? Principal: It feels awkward to say, but we have to allow cheating now. If we don't, we will fall behind and admissions will suffer. There is another college here with four times as many students as us. During exams, even if someone else appears in place of a student, the entire system has become like this. Reporter: What is the admission process? Principal: Whether government or private, the process is the same. Students have to register on the university website by paying Rs 300. After that, they can take admission in any college. Reporter: Private colleges ask students to send documents on WhatsApp. Is admission done on that basis? Principal: We do the same. We have students from as far as Hardoi. They send the documents, we submit them at the office and the admission is done. The money also comes online. Reporter: How much is the fee? Principal: The actual fee is Rs 1,800, but we charge Rs 6,000. One college charges Rs 12,000. The surprising thing is that despite charging Rs 6,000, we have only 600 admissions, while the college charging Rs 12,000 has 1,700 students. The reason is that it provides full facilities. Even if a student fails, they go to the university and get them passed. Naturally, students will go wherever they get more facilities. Everyone gets a scholarship. We only have to send the list to the Social Welfare Department. Reporter: Can a student even become a topper? Principal: Earlier, we used to prepare practical files overnight. Now students don't even know what a practical is. Reporter: Does this happen everywhere? Principal: Yes, but not in every college. Some colleges still maintain their reputation. But such colleges are now less than 1%. Reporter: Is there a rule that every course should have a separate building? Principal: Yes. Reporter: Then how are you running so many courses from one building? Principal: If you go by the rules, they are very strict. Reporter: Then how does the system work? Principal: One system is stronger than all the rules. The same system works everywhere. Our BA and BSc affiliation is from Kanpur University, while BEd is affiliated with Allahabad University. Their websites are separate, so this makes it possible. College manager’s offer: ‘You don’t need to attend classes, just come for exams’ Around 3 km from the Kanpur-Etawah Highway, Sumanrani Institute of Technology was found in the middle of fields in Bamuripur, Auraiya. There is only a dirt road leading to the college. When our team reached the campus, manager Ram Sagar Dwivedi and a clerk were leaving after shutting the college. They said they had closed it before 4 pm because there were no students. According to the staff, the college has 16 teachers and around 500 registered students. Our reporter asked about admission for his daughter. Reporter: We live in Lucknow. Our family is here. My daughter is preparing for NEET and we want her admission here. Manager: The site is currently closed everywhere. Send the documents and we will get the form filled. Reporter: Will she need to come to college? Manager: No, there is no need to come. She only needs to come for the exams. Reporter: What about practicals? Manager: Practicals happen anyway. If required, we will call you. Otherwise, it will be done. Reporter: How will the admission be done? Manager: Just send the documents. It will be done. Reporter: What is the fee? Will everything be included? Manager: The fee is Rs 3,500. The university also conducts an AI and cyber paper for which it charges Rs 500. That will be charged when the paper is held. Everything else will be taken care of. Farrukhabad college surrounded by water After travelling around 130 km from Auraiya, we reached Farrukhabad. On the Bareilly-Delhi Highway in Amritpur, we found Virendra Singh Katiyar Mahavidyalaya. The college was surrounded by water. We met an employee, Satish Singh, who agreed to show us the college while discussing admission. The classrooms in the basement were flooded. The material kept there had been shifted to the first floor. The college is affiliated with Chhatrapati Shahu Ji Maharaj University, Kanpur. Its records show around 200 students and 10 teachers. Reporter: Is anyone at the college? We wanted to take admission. Employee: No one is here. Tell me. Is it BSc, BEd or BTC? Reporter: BSc. Employee: It will be done. Reporter: We live in Lucknow. We want admission for our daughter, who lives here. Employee: Send the documents on WhatsApp. It will be done. Reporter: Do you have a prospectus? Employee: What will you do with a prospectus? We only need four photographs, a photocopy of the Aadhaar card, email ID, photocopies of Class 10 and 12 marksheets and a mobile number. Reporter: Will she have to travel here every day? Employee: No. She does not have to come every day. You will be called for exams, practicals or if there is any problem. Reporter: What is the fee? Employee: Rs 4,000 per semester. Practical fees are separate. Tell us in advance because our centre is different. We personally deposit the money for every student there, for the cheating facility. Reporter: The student won't fail, right? Employee: We cannot guarantee that. If the student keeps writing, meaning the hand keeps moving on the paper, they won't fail. Reporter: If the student doesn't attend, how will they study? Employee: Get a notebook for them. There is no problem even if the student doesn't come. Reporter: Are classes held here? Employee: Yes, students who want to study can come. Reporter: Do you have teachers? Employee: There are 10 teachers. Reporter: How many students? Employee: Students don't come. Reporter: How many are enrolled? Employee: We have capacity for 240 students. There are currently 200. Reporter: You are saying the student can attend or not attend. But 75% attendance is also required, right? Employee: We have to show 75% attendance for every student. We have no choice. We have to manage it. Reporter: What is the principal's name? Employee: In government colleges, principals are gazetted officers. Our principal lives in Farrukhabad. His name is Pushpendra Gangwar. Reporter: Does he not come? Employee: No… he does come. Reporter: Can a student score first division or 75% marks? Would that cost extra? Employee: No, there is no extra charge. The student just has to keep writing. All facilities will be provided. Reporter: Is cheating allowed? Employee: Yes, that's what I'm telling you. We have a setting. Their students come to our centre and our students go to theirs. Reporter: So the exam centre is at another college? Employee: Our Ram Niwas Degree College is right next to this one. Reporter: Which university are you affiliated with? Employee: Kanpur. Reporter: Is that facility only for practicals or everything? Employee: Everything. The student will not face any problem. They will pass. Reporter: Can't the marks be increased? Employee: It's not about marks. Our students score up to 85%. Etah: Muddy road to college Around 115 km from Farrukhabad, we found a college in a deserted area in Sarai Aghat, Etah. Lala Ram Ladaite Ram Shri Devi Mahavidyalaya has no proper road. The college is around 500 metres from the main road, but our car could not move ahead because of the poor condition of the road. We then rented a motorcycle from a local resident. The road was so bad that our feet got stuck in potholes while travelling. Using the excuse of washing our feet, we entered the college campus, where we met Brijendra Singh, who identified himself as a teacher. The condition of the college suggested that regular activities had not been taking place there for a long time. The college is affiliated with Aligarh’s Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University. For admission, only documents need to be submitted Reporter: Whose college is this? Teacher: It belongs to Umesh Master. He also has an intermediate college on Aliganj Road. Reporter: What is taught here? Are admissions open? Teacher: BA and BSc are offered here. Admissions are open. Reporter: Can we get the admission form? Teacher: Just bring the documents. It will be done. Class 10 and 12 marksheets and Aadhaar card. Reporter: Do students have to attend regularly? Teacher: If the student wants to come, they can. Otherwise, just take admission. Bring the student when there is an exam or practical. Reporter: What is the BSc fee? Teacher: Rs 3,500 per semester, or Rs 7,000 a year. Reporter: Do students pass? Teacher: Yes. We give the practical marks. External teachers come, but it gets managed. Don't worry about marks, we will get good marks for them. Reporter: If we pay more, can the student get a better rank? Teacher: Rs 7,000 for one year. Everything will be taken care of in that. Reporter: Will the student come first? Teacher: There is no problem. Aligarh University is better than Kanpur. Reporter: If we pay Rs 3,500, is everything the college's responsibility? Teacher: Everything is included in this. Reporter: How will she write the exam? Teacher: Everything will be managed. No separate payment is required. Many students don't even come. The examiners who come enter the marks themselves. Etah: College gate locked, overgrown bushes suggest it had been shut for days In Naktai Khurd of Etah's Aliganj tehsil, Shri Hiralal Memorial College is located around 500 metres inside an area that looks like a forest. The college gate was locked and the ground was covered with overgrown bushes. It appeared that the college had not opened for several days. No one arrived even after we waited for some time. The college is affiliated with Aligarh's Raja Mahendra Pratap Singh State University. Around 12 teachers and 650 students are registered there. Colleges exploiting relaxed rules How do such colleges open in deserted areas? Why is there no monitoring? The government wants everyone to have access to higher education, so some rules are relaxed. Colleges take advantage of this. Before granting affiliation, a committee visits the college to check whether it meets the required standards. After affiliation is granted, there is generally no further inspection. If a complaint is received, the university forms a fresh panel, after which an inspection can be conducted. How much funding do these colleges receive and from whom? In most universities in UP, the semester fee for BA or BSc is around Rs 1,000–1,200, or about Rs 2,400 a year. Colleges add up to 80% as tuition fees and charge Rs 6,000–7,000 a year. A fixed charge is also collected from students before exams. This adds up to a substantial amount. How do these colleges make money? Suppose a course fee is Rs 4,000 and 300 students are registered. That means the college gets Rs 12 lakh per semester from one course. Even after deducting university fees, teachers' salaries and other expenses, around Rs 8 lakh remains per semester. Why do students take admission in such colleges? Three types of students generally choose such colleges: The answers are based on a conversation with Professor Dr VK Katiyar, general secretary of the Kanpur University Principals' Association.

stories.title: Floods in 32 districts despite El Niño:Will winter be severe too? UN calls it an extreme weather danger zone
stories.summary: The weather department had predicted below-normal rainfall in Uttar Pradesh this year, with several districts likely to face drought-like conditions. The situation remained similar in July and August, but the weather changed dramatically in September. On September 26, the weather department said Uttar Pradesh had received 2% more rain than its normal quota. Not just that, 32 districts, including Varanasi, Prayagraj, Bahraich, Unnao and Barabanki, are facing flood-like conditions. Now, people are wondering whether the prolonged rain means winter will arrive early this year. So, has the impact of El Niño ended? Will winter really arrive early? Will Uttar Pradesh face a harsh winter this year or will temperatures remain normal? Read the UP Explainer… Question: How did the weather suddenly change? Has the impact of El Niño ended? Answer: No, El Niño is still active. This is why Uttar Pradesh has received normal rainfall overall, but the district-wise picture is very different. Question: If El Niño is still active, how did UP receive more-than-normal rainfall? Answer: Local weather systems also influence the monsoon. These factors balanced out the negative impact of El Niño and brought good rainfall to 60 districts of UP. Two seasonal factors became active during this period: A) Positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD): A positive IOD occurs when waters in the western Indian Ocean, near Africa, are warmer than normal, while waters in the eastern Indian Ocean, near India and Indonesia, are cooler. What did it do? The difference in water temperatures pushed warm air away from India. This helped create low-pressure systems around the Bay of Bengal, resulting in large amounts of moisture and cloud formation. B) Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO): MJO is a massive band of clouds, strong winds, and heavy rainfall that moves around the world. What did it do? When the MJO passed over the Indian Ocean, it strengthened the monsoon system forming over the Bay of Bengal. This led to sudden heavy rain and flood-like conditions in UP, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh in September. Question: Could El Niño also cause a severe winter in UP this year? Answer: Generally, no. El Niño is usually associated with warmer conditions rather than colder winters. However, a statement by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has raised concerns about extreme weather. On September 3, 2026, he said El Nino had pushed the world into the danger zone of extreme weather. Extreme weather can include severe heat, severe cold or extreme rainfall. According to the WMO, the impact of El Niño is expected to continue until February 2027 and peak between November and January. This is also the period when India experiences winter. Normally, El Niño tends to shorten the duration of cold weather. Its possible impact can be understood as follows: Question: What if the ‘extreme weather’ scenario actually happens? Answer: Local weather factors have played a role in bringing normal or above-normal rainfall to parts of UP and the rest of the country. If similar local factors become active during winter, UP could still experience severe cold. Three factors could lead to this: Factor 1: Strong western disturbance: Western disturbances are one of the biggest local weather controls for winter in India. These storms originate around the Mediterranean and bring winter rain to northwest India, including Rajasthan, Punjab, Delhi, Uttarakhand, western UP, and Jammu Kashmir, along with heavy snowfall in the Himalayas. Impact despite El Niño: Heavy snowfall in the mountains could send icy winds towards the plains, including UP, Bihar, and Punjab. This could rapidly lower temperatures and result in severe or normal winter conditions. Factor 2: Snow cover over Eurasia and the Himalayas: The amount of snowfall over Eurasia, the northern parts of Europe and Asia, and the Tibetan Plateau in October-November directly influences India's winter. Impact despite El Niño: If the snow cover over Eurasia becomes wider and denser than expected, the winter jet stream could shift towards India. Extremely cold winds from Siberia and Central Asia could then reach India and reduce the warming impact of El Niño. Factor 3: Anticyclone: A high-pressure area, or anticyclone, generally develops over central or northwest India during winter. Impact despite El Niño: If the anticyclone remains strong, skies will stay clear. This will increase ‘radiation cooling’ at night, when heat from the earth escapes into space, making nights much colder. Dense fog could form in the morning and keep daytime temperatures from rising significantly. Question 5: What if UP experiences a milder winter because of El Niño? Answer: A ‘warm winter’ caused by El Niño could become a major challenge for agriculture.

stories.title: Father alleges son-in-law killed daughter, granddaughter, then hanged them:'He had affair with nurse in Ghaziabad, beat wife daily'; questions how she could hang herself from cot
stories.summary: The bodies of a mother and her 3-year-old daughter were found hanging from the same ceiling hook in Ghaziabad. While the in-laws have described the incident as suicide, the woman's father has alleged that his daughter and granddaughter were murdered. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, the woman's father alleged that his son-in-law was having an affair with a nurse. He said whenever his daughter objected to the relationship, her husband would brutally assault her. He alleged that she was beaten and harassed continuously for two days before the incident. The father also raised questions over how the two bodies were found hanging. He said the nooses around the mother and daughter's necks were identical and both bodies were hanging in almost the same position. His daughter's one leg was bent and resting on a wooden cot, but there was no stool or chair nearby. He questioned how his daughter could have reached the ceiling hook, which was considerably higher than the cot. He alleged that his son-in-law killed his daughter and 3-year-old granddaughter and then staged the scene as a suicide. Husband works as technician at Max Hospital The incident took place on Friday evening. The post-mortem examinations were conducted on Saturday evening, after which the bodies were handed over to the families. Preeti, daughter of farmer Awadhesh Singh, a resident of Chaklavanshi village under Maki police station in Unnao district, married Anirudh alias Sonu, a resident of Sankheda under Bilgram police station in Hardoi, on June 16, 2021. Sonu works as a technician at Max Hospital in Ghaziabad. Anirudh, 33, lived in a rented house in Shankar Vihar with his wife Preeti, 30, and their 3-year-old daughter Akshita. Father says claim of breaking door is false, no video available Anirudh claimed that at around 6.30 pm on Friday, he had gone out to get drinking water and medicine for his wife. During this time, Preeti allegedly locked the room from inside. When he returned, he found the door locked. He said he looked through the window and saw his wife and daughter hanging from the noose. He claimed that his wife had killed their daughter before taking her own life. Police officials said people had told them that the door was broken open before the police arrived at the spot. However, Preeti's father Awadhesh Singh questioned this claim. He said there was no video showing anyone breaking the door from outside. According to him, the claim that the door was broken open was false. Father asks how two bodies were hanging at same level Awadhesh Singh said the nooses used for Preeti and her daughter were the same and both bodies were found hanging in a similar position. He said one of Preeti's legs was bent and resting on the cot. No stool or chair was visible nearby. He questioned that if a video of the scene had been made, a stool or chair used to reach the ceiling should have been visible or fallen nearby. He asked how Preeti could have climbed to such a height and tied the noose. He also said her face was facing downwards, which raised further suspicion. Husband allegedly beat Preeti after returning from Balaji temple Preeti's father said Anirudh's conduct was not proper and that he had been constantly harassing his daughter. The family had returned after visiting Mehandipur Balaji in Rajasthan. Despite this, Anirudh allegedly assaulted Preeti on September 24. She called her family and told them about the incident. The next day, September 25, another argument took place at the house, during which Anirudh allegedly beat her again. The father alleged that Anirudh subsequently killed both Preeti and Akshita and hanged their bodies. Anirudh's sister says door did not open despite repeated knocking Anirudh's sister Rinki lives with her family on the lower floor of the same house. She said her daughter went upstairs to Preeti's room on Friday evening. The room was locked from inside. Her daughter knocked on the door for a long time, but there was no response. She then looked through the window. Rinki said her daughter was frightened after seeing what was inside. She ran downstairs and said, Mummy, come quickly. Look upstairs, Mami and Akshita are hanging. Rinki said she went upstairs and saw her sister-in-law and niece hanging from the noose. She then called her brother Anirudh. Everyone together broke open the door, after which Anirudh informed the police control room. Husband says they often fought over his alleged affair During police questioning, Anirudh said his wife used to doubt him. He claimed that she suspected him of having an affair with another woman. He said they often argued over his use of the mobile phone at night. He also said they had returned from Mehandipur Balaji on September 24 and that Preeti had argued with him again the following afternoon.

stories.title: BJP organisation general secretary Dharampal angry over fake reporting:Gives district presidents ultimatum; says, ‘Stop sending fake data, laxity will not be tolerated’
stories.summary: The BJP has begun tightening its preparations for the upcoming Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. State general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh has warned the party's district presidents in clear terms that any kind of negligence or delay in election preparations will no longer be tolerated. On Saturday, Uttar Pradesh BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary and state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh held an important meeting in Lucknow with the district presidents and district in-charges of the Awadh region. At the meeting, Dharampal Singh expressed strong displeasure over fabricated paperwork and issued clear instructions to work on the ground. Five key points from the meeting 1. Stop fabricated reporting- Dharampal Singh said in a stern tone that district presidents must immediately stop sending ‘fed’ and fabricated data to the party headquarters. Only genuine and accurate ground reports should be sent to the state leadership. 2. Task for district in-charges- District in-charges have been instructed to visit the districts themselves and hold meetings down to the booth level. They have been asked to work in better coordination with local workers. 3. Special focus on weak booths- Fresh work should begin in the seats and booths where the BJP lost in the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha elections, taking lessons from past mistakes. 4. Voter-list in-charge to be appointed for every booth- Assembly in-charges and vistarak workers will be appointed in the coming days. Workers from other states will also be sent. A 'voter-list in-charge' will be appointed for every booth, and instructions have been issued to prepare the list. 5. Inactive workers to be removed- The organisation has made it clear that only loyal and useful workers should be activated and assigned responsibilities. These prominent leaders were present at the meeting Several senior leaders, including Awadh region president Awadhesh Dwivedi, region in-charge Dilip Patel, general secretary Rajeev Mishra, Awadhesh Katiyar, Rahul Raj Rastogi, Dr Vimal Singh, Neeraj Sharma, Nitin Mittal, Reshu Bhatia, Trayambak Tripathi, Dr Neeraj Singh, Vijay Bahadur Pathak, Anoop Gupta and Santosh Singh, were present at the important meeting.

She said, "Their alliance appears to be one in which, whether hearts meet or not, hands must meet. Within this alliance, they are challenging one another from each other's strongholds." Not a single programme is being held jointly, yet they talk about contesting the elections together. We are enjoying watching all this. Somewhere, their mutual coordination has broken down. The NDA alliance is going to achieve a record victory in the upcoming elections. Anupriya Patel attended a workers' conference in Ghatampur, Kanpur, on Saturday. Speaking at the programme held at Captain Sukhwasi Janta Memorial College, she said, "Kanpur is my birthplace. Coming among you feels like coming among family. It is because of your love that Apna Dal has emerged as a political party in Uttar Pradesh." During the event, MLA Saroj Kuril welcomed Anupriya by presenting her with a 101-kilogram garland of flowers. See 3 pictures She says-NDA alliance is as strong as a fist Anupriya said, Dr Sonelal Patel founded the party in 1995. When Apna Dal (S) won nine seats in the 2017 Assembly election, Jai Kumar Jackie was made a minister. At present, Apna Dal (S) has 13 MLAs in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Apna Dal (S) entered the Lok Sabha. The people of Mirzapur considered Kanpur's daughter, Anupriya, their own daughter and elected her. She said, "The NDA is a strong fist of five parties. Our party does not compromise on its principles. The NDA will also record a victory in the 2027 Assembly election." Our workers are always among the people Anupriya said, Our party is fully prepared for the 2027 elections. Our workers remain among the people all 365 days of the year and have continued to do so for 5 years. At present, our workers are focused on rectifying any shortcomings in the organisation. SP-Congress engaged in spreading confusion and lies Anupriya said, Once again, the NDA alliance is set to face parties that want to pursue their political interests by spreading lies. The SP and Congress are busy spreading confusion and falsehoods. Beware of these impostors in the upcoming election. These people are coming back to loot the country. When they were in government, they placed no value on the backward classes and Dalits. We raised the demand for reservation for backward classes in NEET Anupriya said, There was no reservation for the backward classes in the NEET examination. The demand was being raised. At that time, the UPA government had the Samajwadi Party's support. When we sent Apna Dal to the Lok Sabha, we raised the demand with the Prime Minister. After this, the Prime Minister implemented reservation in NEET. This is a party of justice that fights for justice. Therefore, make it stronger. The Samajwadi Party government had not conducted a caste census because it had no intention of counting the backward classes. Yet, its leaders loudly claim to be well-wishers of the backward classes. The massive turnout in the rain shows that the leader has worked Apna Dal (S)'s Bindki MLA Jai Kumar Jackie also addressed the people. He described Anupriya Patel as an embodiment of feminine strength. He said, Our party will play an important role in the Assembly elections. MLA Saroj Kuril said, "There has been development in the Ghatampur area. I am the daughter-in-law of this place. I have worked among the people not as an MLA, but as a servant. If I get another opportunity, I will contest the election and serve the people.

stories.title: CJP to launch protest from 2 October:Legal Affairs Head says CEC Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) will launch an agitation from 2 October. The campaign will begin in Mumbai and extend to several cities in Uttar Pradesh. CJP's legal affairs head, Ratna Singh, outlined the complete strategy in Lucknow on Saturday. She had arrived at Rajdhani Guest House. She said here, The organisation is preparing its teams in every state and district so that people can be mobilised around their issues. CJP recently also announced the launch of a nationwide legal aid network for its supporters. At present, we are going to launch an agitation from 2 October demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Legal aid network to be prepared for activists Ratna Singh said that legal assistance arrangements are essential for any movement or organisation. According to her, many people hold back from raising their voices out of fear of legal action. Keeping this in mind, CJP has launched a legal aid website. She also appealed to lawyers in Lucknow to join the organisation and provide legal assistance at the grassroots level. She said the legal team's objective is to provide assistance to people associated with CJP who face legal difficulties. To this end, a network of lawyers and volunteers is being established in different states. Described itself as a pressure group, not a political party Ratna Singh said that CJP currently has no intention of entering electoral politics. Describing the organisation as a "pressure group", she said its objective is to build pressure on public issues and raise people's voices through movements. On its public platform, CJP also presents itself as a political-social movement and a group active on civic issues. He said the organisation had announced that it would launch a movement from 2 October over issues related to the election process and the Election Commission. CJP has made several demands, including the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and reforms to the electoral process. The organisation said the movement would begin in Mumbai. Demand to repeal the 2023 law on election commissioners Ratna Singh also reiterated the demand to repeal the 2023 law relating to the appointment, service conditions and tenure of the Chief Election Commissioner and other election commissioners. She said the new law should ensure transparency and enable the participation of civil society. The 2023 law had repealed the relevant 1991 law. Door left open for support from opposition parties Asked about support for the movement from opposition parties, Ratna Singh said that the CJP is not against the opposition. She said that any organisation or individual wishing to join the movement would be welcomed. However, she ruled out the possibility of the CJP fielding candidates in the 2027 Assembly elections. On allegations, Ratna Singh says the truth will emerge after the investigation On the allegations related to the organisation, Ratna Singh said that these were currently only allegations and that the truth would emerge only after the investigation. She declined to comment on the matter immediately. Focus on bringing young people into the organisation in Lucknow The meeting also focused on bringing young people and volunteers into the organisation. Ratna Singh said teams were being formed in every district comprising people who could provide legal assistance, handle policy-related work, carry out ground-level work and participate in movements. She said increasing the participation of young people to raise local issues at the local level was a key objective of the organisation.

stories.title: SP and BJP councillors clash in the municipal corporation house:SP councillor says, "A Brahmin will hit you with a slipper"; BJP councillor says MLA Amitabh Bajpai is a thief
stories.summary: There was a major uproar at a meeting of the Kanpur Municipal Corporation House convened on Saturday to elect six members of the executive committee. A confrontation broke out between BJP councillor Vikas Jaiswal and Samajwadi Party councillor Rajat Kaushik Bajpai over the delimitation of wards. What began as a verbal argument escalated into a physical fight. BJP councillor Naveen Pandit and other councillors caught Rajat Kaushik Bajpai as he rushed to attack Vikas Jaiswal. BJP councillor Vikas Jaiswal raised ‘tap thief’ slogans in the House. Referring to Aryanagar Samajwadi Party MLA Amitabh Bajpai, he said, ‘Amitabh Bajpai is a thief.’ Rajat Kaushik responded, ‘You showed a slipper to a Brahmin. A Brahmin will hit you with slippers.’ During this, expelled BJP councillor Pawan Gupta also entered the House. He asked Mayor Pramila Pandey and Municipal Commissioner Arpit Upadhyay whether he could participate in the election of the executive committee members. He was told that he could not. See the pictures... Concern over disruption had existed beforehand Officials and the mayor had already feared disruption in the municipal corporation House. Accordingly, an ACP, forces from several police stations and the PAC were deployed at the municipal corporation even before the House session began. Police personnel remained alert outside and behind the municipal corporation premises as well. The police brought the minor commotion under control. BJP councillors clash with each other During the House proceedings, BJP councillors Laxmi Kori, Vikas Jaiswal and Alok Pandey reached the area near the dais. They alleged that a young man accompanying councillor Alok Pandey had been mistreated and accused of theft. They were speaking to the mayor. At that point, other BJP councillors objected to the uproar. Meanwhile, BJP councillor Akarsh Bajpai came to the dais and told the mayor that troublemakers disrupting the House should be removed by the police. Five BJP councillors and one SP councillor elected to the executive committee The House had been convened to elect six members of the executive committee. After uproar in the House and debates on several issues, six members were eventually elected unanimously. They included five BJP councillors and one SP councillor. Rajat Kaushik was elected from the SP. He was the one who had clashed with a BJP councillor during the House proceedings. Besides him, Vandana Sharma, Kaushal Mishra, Adarsh Gupta, Jitendra Chaurasia and Satish Yadav were elected from the BJP. Issues of garbage and dilapidated roads raised The issue of dilapidated roads and filth was raised during the House proceedings. Councillor Aarti Bajpai from Panki spoke about the lack of cleanliness in the area. Meanwhile, Councillor Kaushal Mishra from Vinayakpur said that the Public Works Department roads were in poor condition. People also hold the Municipal Corporation and councillors accountable over the dilapidated roads. He demanded that the Municipal Corporation install boards on the Public Works Department roads stating that ‘this road does not belong to us’. Govind appointed chief whip and Neeraj whip Leader of the councillors' group Naveen Pandit said that, as directed by the mayor, councillor Govind Mohan Shukla had been given the responsibility of chief whip, a post that fell vacant following the death of councillor Yashpal Singh. Meanwhile, councillor Neeraj Raksel was appointed whip. SP councillor says God gave them two hands, and gave us two as well Samajwadi Party councillor Rajat Kaushik said that development works by Vikas Jaiswal were continually encroaching on municipal corporation properties in the boundary area of his ward. He said that three months ago, he had submitted a memorandum and complaint to the Municipal Commissioner, asking that if the ward delimitation report sent to the government included that area as part of his ward, he should be informed. He said Vikas Jaiswal continually made inappropriate remarks, used abusive language and behaved rudely with everyone. He said that if Jaiswal continued to pick fights in this manner, he would respond in the same language. He would respond to him in whatever manner he wanted. If Jaiswal understood the language of love, he would respond with love; and if Jaiswal thought he was a very powerful strongman, God had given him two hands and had given Kaushik two as well. He said Jaiswal showed his slippers to the MLA and picked fights with one person or another. Now, none of his misbehaviour would be tolerated. He would be answered wherever and however he wanted, in whatever situation he chose. SP goons have started hooliganism in the municipal corporation BJP councillor Vikas Jaiswal said that there was a plan for the canal embankment which the KDA developed in 2003 and handed over to the Kanpur Municipal Corporation. During the previous term, the mayor had gone there to perform the ceremony for a wedding hall, and MLC Salil Vishnoi and all of us were present. Subsequently, a proposal was also passed in 2021 under Table No. 343 for a place to park a hearse, a deep freezer and 100, meaning ambulances. Today, I was sitting at that same wedding hall when these Samajwadi Party goons started hooliganism in the municipal corporation. When they engage in hooliganism, that is fine. But when you respond to their hooliganism, they roam around after taking off their clothes and slippers. This is the face of the Samajwadis. They are in the habit of engaging in hooliganism. The face of the Samajwadi parties is hooliganism.

stories.title: Acharya Pramod building Kalki Dham gets threat from US:Caller says, ‘Stop spreading superstition or we’ll blow you up’; seeks security from Sambhal SP
stories.summary: Acharya Pramod Krishnam, the presiding head of Kalki Dham, has received a death threat. On Saturday, Acharya Pramod said in Sambhal that he received a call from a US number on his personal mobile number on the night of 24 September. An audio message followed. The caller identified himself as Kulveer Singh Sidhu. He also claimed to be associated with the terrorist organisation Babbar Khalsa. The audio message said, ‘Stop spreading this hypocrisy of yours, or you will be blown up any day. You have only a few days left to live.’ It is also claimed that a bomb blast was threatened. Acharya Pramod Krishnam has demanded that an FIR be registered against the person who issued the threat and that the mobile number be investigated. Uma Raman Tripathi, president of the Shri Kalki Dham Trust, sent a letter to the Sambhal SP, reporting the matter. A copy of the complaint was also sent to the DGP, ADG Security and ADG Law and Order. Acharya said: I received a threat to blow me up with a bomb Kalki Dham is located in Echoda Kamboh village, 50 kilometres from the district headquarters. Its peethadhishwar is Acharya Pramod Krishnam. He spoke to the media on Saturday. He said, I had been receiving calls from foreign numbers for the past few days. I did not answer them. Two days ago, I received an audio message in Punjabi. The information has been shared with the Uttar Pradesh Police, the Home Ministry, the Punjab Police and the Sambhal SP. The person who issued the threat threatened to blow me up with a bomb. He called my work hypocrisy and said I should stop it. He threatened to kill me if I did not stop working for Sanatan. He also said an attack would be carried out with bombs and rocket launchers. Acharya says-If I am murdered, construction of Kalki Dham must not stop SP says investigation under way Sambhal SP Vikas Chandra Tripathi said that a message had been received from Delhi on the acharya's phone. The police are investigating the matter. Who is Acharya Pramod Krishnam? Acharya Pramod Krishnam was born on 4 January 1965 in Enchora Kamboh village in Sambhal. He belongs to a Brahmin family. Pramod Krishnam has also contested elections twice on Congress tickets. He contested the 2014 election from Sambhal and the 2019 election from Lucknow. However, he lost both times. Pramod Krishnam is said to have been the most prominent Congress leader in supporting the construction of the Ram temple. Because of this, the Congress expelled him from the party. However, the stated reason for his expulsion was anti-party activities. More than his politics, Pramod Krishnam is discussed in connection with Shri Kalki Dham in Sambhal, Uttar Pradesh, which he built in his village.

stories.title: Man who strangled wife in Jhansi arrested after encounter:Gave her alcohol before killing her; victim was bleeding from eyes, mouth
stories.summary: Police arrested Shivani's husband, Yash Thakur, in a brief encounter 26 days after the 27-year-old woman from Datia was murdered. Yash opened fire at the police team during a cordon operation near Simardha village late on Thursday night. The police retaliated, shooting Yash in the leg. A ₹25,000 reward had been announced for information leading to his arrest. According to the police, Shivani's body was found on 30 August in a room in Awas Vikas, Jhansi. The post-mortem confirmed that she had died of strangulation. After the murder, Yash locked the room from outside and fled. The police had been searching for him since then. See the pictures related to the incident... Fired at police, shot in the leg in retaliatory action SP City Preeti Singh said, "The Sipri Bazaar police received information at around 1 a.m. on Thursday that Yash had come to Jhansi on a scooter. Police teams subsequently surrounded him near Simardha village. When the police team tried to stop Yash, he opened fire." He was shot in the leg in the retaliatory action. The police arrested him after he was injured and sent him to hospital for treatment. During questioning, Yash confessed to killing his wife. The accused told the police, "On the night of 30 August, we drank alcohol and had dinner together. We then had an argument, after which I killed my wife. After the incident, I latched the door of the room from outside and fled." They became friends on Instagram and married for love within two months Yash told the police that he had become friends with Shivani on Instagram around two years ago. He had messaged her after watching one of her reels. As their conversations grew, they exchanged mobile numbers. Their friendship then turned into love. Around two months later, they got married for love. According to Shivani's sister Muskan, they had been married for around one and a half to two years. They often argued after their marriage. Yash suspected Shivani over her use of her mobile phone and Instagram. He also questioned her about having cash with her. This issue frequently led to arguments between them. Shivani had started living in Jhansi after a dispute Shivani was originally from Indergarh in Datia district. After her marriage, she lived with Yash in Gwalior. The family alleges that after the marriage, Yash used to assault Shivani over trivial matters. After this, Shivani had been living for around three months in a rented room in Awas Vikas, near Fauji Tiraha in Jhansi, with her sister Muskan and brother Aniket. Yash would also occasionally come to Jhansi to meet her. There was a dispute at night before the murder Shivani's sister Muskaan said, "On the night of 30 August, Yash was speaking ill of members of our family. He was hurling abuses at Shivani. Yash also made objectionable remarks about her and her father." As the dispute escalated, their maternal uncle Santosh, who lived nearby, counselled them both and defused the situation. Afterwards, the family members went to their respective rooms. She was in the inner room. At around 1.30 to 2 a.m., Yash asked for his bag and some belongings. After handing over the bag, she locked the room from outside. Sister kept calling out at 5 a.m., but the door did not open Muskaan said that at around 5 a.m., she needed to use the washroom. She called out to Shivani and Yash several times to open the gate, but received no response. When the gate still did not open after she had called out for around half an hour, she fell asleep. At around 9 a.m., her brother Aniket reached home and opened the gate. Shivani was found dead inside the room. When Muskaan was asked how Shivani might have died, she said, "They must have killed her-her brother-in-law must have done it." The family took Shivani to the Medical College, where doctors declared her dead. Father alleged dowry demands and assault Shivani's father, Santram Vanshkar, had accused Yash of demanding money as dowry and assaulting his daughter. The family had also accused Yash of using casteist slurs. Based on a family member's complaint, the police registered a case against Yash under charges including dowry death and the SC/ST Act. Further investigation is under way.

stories.title: Fortuner crashes into tanker in Kanpur, Crorepati trader killed:SUV broke divider and entered opposite lane; he was trapped in steering
stories.summary: In Kanpur, a speeding Fortuner went out of control and collided with a tanker loaded with gas cylinders. A catechu trader died in the accident. The collision was so severe that the front of the Fortuner was completely destroyed. The accident caused a traffic jam on the Kanpur-Prayagraj Highway. Police reached the spot and, with the help of local residents, pulled the trader out of the Fortuner and took him to hospital. Doctors there declared him dead. The police then informed the trader's family and sent the body for post-mortem examination. The accident took place at around 10:30 a.m. on Saturday in the Maharajpur police station area. The deceased has been identified as Pawan Agarwal (60). First, look at two pictures... Businessman was on his way from home to the factory Pawan Agrawal, who lived in the Swaroop Nagar police station area, owned a catechu factory in Chaudgara. He also owned a Hindustan petrol pump. His family comprises his wife, two sons and a daughter. According to the police, Pawan Agrawal was travelling to his catechu factory in a Fortuner. As soon as he reached near Chandrika Dhaba at Maholi Mor, his Fortuner suddenly went out of control. As a result, the vehicle broke through the divider and entered the opposite lane. At the same time, an Indane Gas tanker travelling from Prayagraj towards Mathura approached from the opposite direction. A young man named Raju was driving the tanker. He was travelling in his lane. Raju applied the brakes and tried to stop the tanker, but the Fortuner was travelling so fast that it could not avoid colliding with the tanker. Maharajpur police station in-charge Janardan Singh said, All aspects related to the accident are being investigated. The damaged vehicles have been moved to the side of the highway and traffic has been restored to normal. Further action is being taken in the case.

stories.title: 98-year-old grandmother dances after grandson wins medal:Aligarh’s Gulveer bags Asian Games silver; she says, ‘I’ll dance again when he returns home’
stories.summary: Aligarh athlete Gulveer Singh has won a silver medal at the Asian Games being held in Japan. His 98-year-old grandmother, Gendo Devi, was overjoyed at her grandson's achievement. She danced so much that she began to lose her breath. She said, "I no longer have that energy or strength in my body, but when my Golu comes to the village, I will dance again." Gulveer, a resident of Sirsa village located around 40 kilometres from the district headquarters, won the silver medal in the 10,000-metre race at the Asian Games. Earlier, he had won a bronze medal at the Hangzhou Asian Games held in China in 2023. The family is now looking forward to Gulveer's next two races. His elder brother Monu said that two races were still remaining. The family is confident that the younger brother will return with a gold medal this time. Has not returned to the village for 10 months, expected to return in October Gulveer has been away from the village for around 10 months. Amid preparations for the Commonwealth Games and the Asian Games, most of his time was spent training and competing. Gulveer's success is a matter of pride for his mother, Lakshmi Devi, and grandmother, Gendo Devi. They also feel a sense of disappointment that Gulveer has still not returned home. The family hopes he will be able to come home in October, after his commitments at the Asian Games are over. His grandmother says she will dance again when she sees her grandson in person this time. Gulveer is the youngest of three brothers; his father is a farmer Gulveer has risen from a very ordinary farming family to international athletics. His father, Pappu Singh, is a farmer. Gulveer is the youngest of three brothers. Naresh is older than him, while Monu is the eldest. Gulveer's wife is Babita, and they have two daughters: two-and-a-half-year-old Pari and six-month-old Saavi. So dedicated to sport that he did not attend his sister's wedding Gulveer's dedication to sport is also linked to his family's sacrifice. His sister was married in February this year. Gulveer could not attend the wedding. To ensure that his sister did not feel upset, he kept reassuring her over the phone that he was coming. At times, he told her he was on a flight, and at others, that he was on the way. The family also continued to assure his sister of the same. But Gulveer did not reach the wedding even by the time his sister's farewell took place. In the end, she was told the truth: Gulveer was busy preparing for competitions and taking part in them. Because of this compulsion, he could not attend the wedding. It was an emotional moment for the family. At that time, Gulveer's focus was on preparing to run for the country. Once known as a village of bandits, Sirsa now has a new identity as a village of runners Sirsa village's identity has also changed. At one time, the village was known as a village of bandits. Now, international runner Gulveer Singh has become Sirsa's new identity. The children of the village are also dreaming of becoming athletes like Gulveer. Villagers say that a village which has produced an internationally acclaimed runner for the country should also have facilities of the same standard for athletes to practise. Gulveer wants an athletics stadium to be built in the village Villagers have been demanding the construction of an athletics stadium in Sirsa for practice for the past several months. Gulveer has also raised the issue with elected representatives. Gulveer says that if the village gets a better track and training facilities, athletes from nearby areas will not have to travel far for training. Gulveer had told the media that after returning home, he would ask the state's Chief Minister and officials to build a stadium in the village. His dream is that the children of Sirsa should not have to leave home to progress, and that the next generation from the village should also win medals for the country. For now, all eyes in Sirsa are on Gulveer's next two competitions. The family is hoping for gold. Meanwhile, 98-year-old grandmother Gendo Devi is waiting for her Golू to return home. She wants to celebrate wholeheartedly this time when her grandson is in front of her.

stories.title: Jhansi man strangled wife after finding money in her purse:Killed wife after party; couple met on Instagram and later had a love marriage
stories.summary: “I became friends with Shivani on Instagram two years ago. Our friendship soon turned into love. We got married just two months later. After our marriage, she started spending more time on her phone and Instagram. She became distant. I often found a lot of money in her purse. “I started suspecting her character. She would not answer when I asked her about it. We began arguing over this frequently. Upset, she moved to Jhansi to live with her sister and brother. I went to meet her on August 30. We had a party that night. We argued during the party and, in anger, I strangled her. After she died, I locked the room from outside and fled.” This was the statement of Yash Thakur, the accused in the murder of 27-year-old Sudha alias Shivani, who was living in Jhansi. Police arrested him late on Friday after shooting him in the leg. He had been absconding since the murder, and a reward of Rs 25,000 had been announced for information leading to his arrest. The case was reported from the Sipri Bazar police station area in Jhansi. Shivani was from Indergarh in Madhya Pradesh's Datia district, while Yash is a resident of Gwalior. Shivani was the eldest of four sisters Shivani was from Indergarh in Datia district. Her father, Santram Vanshkar, sells fruit from a cart, while her mother, Rekha, works as a domestic helper in Delhi. Shivani was the eldest of four sisters. She stayed at home after completing her studies. Her younger sisters Preeti and Neha are married. She also had a sister, Muskan, 18, and two brothers, Aniket, 17, and Kapil, 14. Shivani's sister Muskan said she had met Yash Thakur, a resident of Gwalior, on social media around two years ago. They started talking and their friendship soon turned into a relationship. Yash worked at a clothes shop. The two told their families about their relationship. After receiving their families' consent, they got married around one-and-a-half years ago. Allegations of assault after marriage According to Muskan, Shivani moved to Gwalior with Yash after their marriage. After some time, he allegedly started assaulting her over minor issues. Distressed by this, Shivani rented a room near Awas Vikas Fauji Tiraha in Jhansi. Her sister Muskan and brother Aniket also lived with her there. Their father and younger brother Kapil stayed in their village. Yash would visit Jhansi occasionally. A day before Raksha Bandhan, Shivani went to Gwalior with her brother Kapil. She returned to Jhansi with Yash two days later, while Kapil went back to the village. Couple argued before the murder Muskan said Shivani and Yash had an argument on the night of August 30. She alleged that Yash made objectionable remarks about the family. According to her, he told Shivani that he had slept with her sister and also threatened to beat her father with a slipper. As the argument escalated, their maternal uncle Santosh, who lived nearby, intervened and calmed Yash down. Aniket then went to his uncle's house. The situation later became normal. Muskan went to sleep in her room, while Shivani and Yash slept in another room. Husband asked for bag, then locked room from outside According to Muskan, Yash asked for his bag between around 1:30 am and 2 am as he wanted to take some belongings. After she handed him the bag, Yash allegedly locked the room from outside. At around 5 am, Muskan tried to open her room's door to go to the bathroom, but it would not open. She called out to Shivani and Yash for around half an hour, but received no response. She then went back to sleep. At around 9 am, her brother Aniket returned home and opened the door. Shivani found dead inside room Aniket said the door of Shivani's room was locked from outside. After opening it, he found Shivani lying dead on the floor. Blood was coming from her ear and there were marks on her neck. The door of the other room was also locked from outside. Aniket opened it and woke Muskan. Neighbours and other family members then gathered at the house. Shivani was taken to the medical college, where doctors declared her dead. The post-mortem examination confirmed that she died of strangulation. Accused claims he suspected wife after marriage According to police, Yash told investigators that he had messaged Shivani after seeing one of her reels on Instagram. She replied, after which they started talking. Their friendship later turned into a relationship, and they got married around two months later. Yash reportedly told police that he loved Shivani but did not like some of her behaviour after their marriage. He said she spent a lot of time on her phone and Instagram. He claimed that he began suspecting her character. According to police, Yash said this led to frequent arguments between them. On the night of August 30, they sat together, drank alcohol and ate chicken. They then had an argument, during which he allegedly strangled Shivani. Family also alleges dowry harassment Shivani's family also accused Yash of harassing her over dowry. Her father, Santram Vanshkar, alleged that Yash demanded money as dowry. He said Yash would assault Shivani when his demands were not met and allegedly subjected her to caste-based abuse. Based on Santram's complaint, police registered a case against Yash under charges including dowry death and provisions of the SC/ST Act. Rs 25,000 reward announced; arrested after police encounter SP City Preeti Singh said police had been searching for Yash after the murder. The SSP had announced a reward of Rs 25,000 for information leading to his arrest. At around 1 am on Friday, police received information that Yash had arrived in Jhansi on a scooter. The SWAT team and Sipri Bazar police then laid a trap near Simardha village. According to police, Yash opened fire at the police team when he realised that he had been surrounded. Police retaliated, shooting him in the leg and injuring him. He was subsequently arrested.

stories.title: UP water tank collapses to be probed:ED to examine contracts-payments of 13 companies; irregularities alleged in Jal Jeevan Mission
stories.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has sought complete details of tenders, contracts, payments and bank accounts linked to 13 major companies and organisations involved in the Jal Jeevan Mission in Uttar Pradesh on Saturday. The ED's Lucknow unit has sought the information from the Uttar Pradesh Jal Nigam (Rural) as part of its investigation into the construction of water tanks under the scheme. The investigating agency is examining how the contracts were awarded and which accounts received money withdrawn from the government treasury. Agency is also scrutinising records from 2012 to 2019 This case is not limited to the Jal Jeevan Mission. According to ED sources, the investigation covers work carried out from 2012 to the present. Between 2012 and 2017, when the Samajwadi Party government was in power in the state, Azam Khan was the Urban Development Minister and the Jal Nigam came under this department. The ED is already investigating a money-laundering case linked to Azam Khan, his family and the Johar Trust. The ED is now working to establish the links between the old contracts and the Jal Jeevan Mission. What is on the ED's radar? The ED is trying to understand how the entire operation was carried out. It has asked the Jal Nigam several questions: It is clear that the ED's investigation will not be limited to the companies that secured the contracts, but will also examine how the government funds were ultimately used. Details sought of collapsed and leaking water tanks The Central Government launched the Jal Jeevan Mission in 2019. Under the mission, major efforts were made to provide water to villages across Uttar Pradesh. However, complaints of water tanks collapsing and leaking were received from several districts. The ED has sought a complete list of tanks that have collapsed or been declared unsafe since 2019. It has sought not only details of the accidents, but also soil test reports, structural designs, drawings, cement and steel inspection reports, third-party inspection reports, and the names of the officials who approved their quality. Johar University VC Questioned for 8 Hours As part of the investigation, the ED questioned Johar University Vice-Chancellor Zaheeruddin for around eight hours in the Johar University case. The officials asked pointed questions about his appointment process, his stake in the Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust and the transactions related to construction work carried out on the campus.

stories.title: Yogi meets PM Modi in Delhi:UP CM will also meet Nitin Nabin; Rajya Sabha election likely to be discussed
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath is on a visit to Delhi. He met Prime Minister Narendra Modi at his residence at around 12:30 pm on Saturday. He also brought a list of projects in the state that are scheduled to be inaugurated or launched by the PM in the coming days. He will also meet BJP national president Nitin Nabin. According to sources, they may discuss the Rajya Sabha and MLC elections. Candidates for six MLC seats are yet to be finalised. The CM may also discuss the names of potential candidates. Rajya Sabha voting to be held on 16 October Voting for 10 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh will be held on 16 October. The results will also be announced on the same day. In addition, voting for 11 Teacher and Graduate MLC seats will be held on 23 October. The votes for the MLC election will be counted on 27 October. Of the 10 Rajya Sabha seats, eight are held by the BJP, one by the Samajwadi Party and one by the Bahujan Samaj Party. So far, no party has announced its candidates. Of the 11 MLC seats, eight are held by the BJP and three by the Samajwadi Party. The Samajwadi Party has announced candidates for all 11 seats. The BJP and Congress have fielded candidates for five seats each.

stories.title: Akhilesh bids final farewell to Ram Govind Chaudhary:Says Samajwadi movement suffered a loss; Minister Dayashankar also pays tribute
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav paid his last respects to senior party leader and former Uttar Pradesh Leader of the Opposition Ram Govind Chaudhary in Lucknow on Saturday (26 Sept) morning. Yadav laid flowers on Chaudhary’s mortal remains and appeared emotional during the ceremony. Akhilesh said Chaudhary’s death was a major loss for the socialist movement and the Samajwadi Party. Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh also paid tribute to the veteran leader. Ram Govind Chaudhary dies at PGI Lucknow Chaudhary died late on Friday (25 Sept) night while undergoing treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI) in Lucknow. Reports differ on his age, with some sources putting it at around 74 and others at around 80. The veteran leader had served as Leader of the Opposition in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly from 2017 to 2022 and had also served as a minister in the state government. Akhilesh had met Chaudhary during hospitalisation in 2025 In December 2025, Akhilesh Yadav visited Chaudhary at a Lucknow hospital while he was undergoing treatment. During the meeting, Chaudhary told party leaders that the election had to be won and that Akhilesh should be made Chief Minister. Akhilesh said, ‘Ram Govind Chaudhary was a leader of the socialist movement’ Joined the socialist movement during his student days Ram Govind Chaudhary was born on 9 July 1946 in Ballia district. His father was Dwarika Chaudhary and his mother was Tileshwari Devi. He completed his postgraduate and LLB studies at TD College in Ballia. Jailed for 25 months during the Emergency Chaudhary became associated with socialist ideology during his student days. During the Emergency, he participated in the Total Revolution movement and was jailed. While most activists from Ballia were released after 19 months, Chaudhary remained in jail for 25 months. Remained close to Mulayam Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav Chaudhary was considered close to Mulayam Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav. Throughout his political career, he consistently raised issues related to education and the backward classes. In recent years, he remained active as the Samajwadi Party’s national secretary. stories.title: 25-year-old Premanandji disciple dies by suicide:Jumps from 4th floor, injury marks found on body; police begin probe
stories.summary: A 25-year-old disciple of saint Premanand Maharaj died after allegedly jumping from the fourth floor of a building in Vrindavan, Mathura. The incident took place at Guru Kripa Kunj in the Varah Ghat area. According to the police’s preliminary investigation, Rasik Dulari Sharan went to the terrace on Thursday evening and sat there for some time before jumping. He was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in critical condition, where he later died. Injury marks found on body, grinder recovered from room Police found injury marks on Rasik Dulari Sharan’s body during the investigation. A grinder was also recovered from his room. Police are investigating whether the injuries were self-inflicted and whether the grinder was used in the incident. Eyewitnesses also reported seeing severe injury marks on his body. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. Incident took place near Premanand Maharaj’s old ashram The incident occurred at Guru Kripa Kunj in the Varah Ghat area, around 500 metres from Premanand Maharaj’s old ashram, Keli Kunj. Police will send the body for post-mortem examination today. See two pictures Rasik Dulari Sharan was initiated by Premanand Maharaj two years ago Rasik Dulari Sharan was originally from Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. He came to Vrindavan around two years ago and was initiated by Premanand Maharaj. After this, he changed his name from Deepak Lodhi to Rasik Dulari Sharan. Deepak had two brothers and one sister. He was the middle child, with an elder sister and a younger brother, Manish. His mother, Laung Bai, came to Vrindavan around a year ago and stayed at another location for five days, during which she regularly met Deepak. According to the information available, he had also completed the Narmada Parikrama. Electrician by profession, given room at Guru Kripa Kunj Rasik Dulari Sharan was skilled in electrical work and was assigned related responsibilities at the ashram. Around three months ago, he was allotted a room on the fourth floor of Guru Kripa Kunj. Around 50 disciples associated with Premanand Maharaj also live in the building. Police examine mobile data and CCTV footage for clues Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said police reached the spot after receiving information from the hospital and inspected the scene. A forensic team was also called to examine the site, where some suspicious items were found in the room. Police investigate calls made before the incident Police are examining whom Rasik Dulari Sharan spoke to before the incident and the circumstances leading up to it. Mobile phone data and CCTV footage are being analysed to gather further clues. Premanand Maharaj shifted from Keli Kunj Ashram in May Saint Premanand Maharaj previously lived at Keli Kunj Ashram but left on 18 May. Since then, he has been staying at Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram. The new ashram is around 3 km from Keli Kunj via the Yamuna route and about 18 km by road. Yamuna Bihar Kunj Ashram spread across nearly 5 acres Located along the Yamuna in Velvan, the ashram is spread across nearly 5 acres and is surrounded by trees and plants. Maharajji last visited Keli Kunj on Radha Ashtami Premanand Maharaj visited Keli Kunj on Radha Ashtami, where he celebrated Radha Rani’s birth anniversary with great fanfare and stayed until the afternoon. He then left for the new ashram and has not visited Keli Kunj since.

stories.title: Gorakhpur municipal commissioner rebukes officials:Expresses displeasure over sanitation in Ward 35; supervisor’s salary withheld
stories.summary: Municipal Commissioner Ajay Jain inspected Ward 35, Jungle Salik Ram, on Friday and reviewed ongoing construction, drainage, sanitation and door-to-door waste collection. He expressed displeasure over the condition of sanitation and waste-lifting arrangements and directed that the salary of sanitation supervisor Mohammad Idris be withheld until further orders. Councillor Sudhir Yadav, the executive engineer, assistant engineers from the construction and waterworks departments, the zonal officer, sanitation inspector and other officials were present during the inspection. Drain construction inspected, engineers asked to speed up work Jain inspected drainage construction at several locations and checked the depth and quality of the work. He directed engineers to speed up the construction while ensuring compliance with prescribed quality standards. He also inspected the drain near the Nishad Party office and directed the PWD engineer to take immediate steps for its repair. Roads and parks to be developed as per local requirements The Municipal Commissioner directed officials to construct roads in parks and other locations where required. He also asked Construction Division-2 to complete patchwork in the Shatabdipuram area at the earliest. He ordered the immediate removal of shuttering material, construction materials and debris lying near the drains. He also stressed regular drain cleaning to prevent blockages and waterlogging during the rains. Old Padri Bazar toilet to be developed as aspirational toilet Jain directed officials to develop the old toilet at the Padri Bazar intersection as an aspirational toilet according to local requirements. He also instructed officials to take steps to beautify the nearby pond and repair parks in the surrounding area. Door-to-door waste collection system found unsatisfactory The Municipal Commissioner expressed displeasure over the door-to-door waste collection system and ordered officials to inspect the registers of waste collection vehicle drivers. He directed all waste collection vehicles to reach the ward on time, make two to three trips and transport the collected waste to the GTS. He also stressed the need to improve revenue collection along with waste management. Sanitation supervisor’s salary withheld over poor arrangements Jain found the ward’s sanitation arrangements unsatisfactory and held the concerned staff responsible for the lapses. He directed that sanitation supervisor Mohammad Idris’s salary be withheld until further orders. He also ordered officials to verify the attendance of sanitation workers and improve the system after finding that garbage collection vehicles were not reaching the ward on time. Officials told to complete public works within deadline Jain instructed officials to ensure there was no negligence in sanitation, drainage or construction work. He directed them to prioritise public amenities, complete projects within the stipulated time and maintain the required quality standards.
