stories.title: ‘They replaced knee she walked on’:Elderly woman’s son in Lucknow alleges signatures taken on blank paper as formality
stories.summary: A family has claimed that a doctor operated on the wrong leg of an elderly woman at a private hospital in Lucknow on Monday. Rajeshwari, a resident of Rajajipuram, was admitted for surgery on her left knee, which had been causing her problems for several days, but her son Manoj Kumar alleges that the doctor operated on her right knee instead. According to the family, she was admitted to a private nursing home on September 8 and shifted to Health City Hospital (Remedy Medicity) the next day under the Ayushman scheme. The family further alleged that ₹65,000 was charged separately for the implant and that they were threatened when they questioned the doctor about the alleged mistake. Manoj said that he went to the ICU to meet his mother the day after the operation. During the meeting, Rajeshwari allegedly told him that the doctor had operated on her other leg. The family then questioned the doctor about the surgery, following which they allegedly faced threats. The family has raised questions over how the wrong leg was operated on and why the surgery was performed on the leg that was not reportedly causing the problem. They have sought an explanation regarding the alleged medical error and the circumstances surrounding the surgery. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the victim's son and gathered details of the entire incident. Read the report... 'They operated on the other leg instead of the one that was hurting' Manoj says that, before the surgery, his nephew was made to sign some plain sheets of paper and forms in the name of completing paperwork. The hospital is now saying that it had already been explained that the surgery would be performed on this leg. Manoj alleges that Dr C.P. Gupta is responsible for such serious negligence involving his elderly mother. Following the negligence, his mother has become completely bedridden. She is now unable to do any of her own work. Manoj filed a complaint against the doctor at the Gomtinagar police station. He also submitted a complaint to the CMO's office, but says that no action has been taken in the matter so far. ₹2.5 lakh deducted from Ayushman card; neither police nor CMO listening Earlier, the elderly woman's grandson Ayush had said that his grandmother, Rajeshwari (70), was admitted to Aadya Hospital on 8 September for surgery on her left knee. Saying that the surgery would involve higher expenses, they shifted her to Health City Hospital on 11 September for the operation under the Ayushman card scheme. Dr C.P. Gupta performed the surgery that evening. The operation was supposed to be performed on the left knee, but the right knee was operated on instead. She was discharged on 14 September. During this period, ₹65,000 was deposited in cash and a payment of ₹2.50 lakh was made through the Ayushman card. After being discharged, she submitted an application in Gomti Nagar on the same day requesting that an FIR be registered, but the FIR was not registered. She then submitted an application to the CMO on 16 September, but no action was taken. She has now lodged a complaint with Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. Read what was written in the complaint: In his complaint to the police, the elderly woman’s son, Manoj Kumar, alleged that his mother was hurriedly taken to the operation theatre, where preparations were made to perform surgery on her right knee. She reportedly questioned the medical staff, saying that the problem was in her left knee and asking whether it would be treated. According to the complaint, the doctors present in the operation theatre allegedly told her to remain silent. When she asked them to call her family members, they allegedly refused. The doctors then administered anaesthesia and proceeded with the surgery. Manoj claimed that after the operation, the family learned that the doctor had operated on the right knee instead of the left knee. Videos recorded by the family members have emerged The family members of the elderly woman who was affected had recorded several videos of the entire incident. Those videos have now emerged. In one video, the family members can be seen alleging that the doctor verbally abused them when they went to complain. In another video, the doctor can be heard saying, "You people are harassing the doctor; this is a non-bailable offence." In another video, the family members are seen calling the police. They can be heard saying that the doctor performed the wrong operation here and is now hurling abuses. Another video shows the elderly woman who was affected. She is sitting on a bed, with several people present there. When asked, the elderly woman pointed to the knee that is causing her pain. Her leg appears to be moving in the middle. Hospital leased to another group Health City MD Dr Sandeep Kapoor said in a video statement, "We have leased our Vijay Khand hospital to the Remedy Medicity Group." Care is essential when treating the elderly Dr Ashish Kumar, in-charge of the KGMU Limb Centre and head of the Department of Orthopaedics, said, "There is a belief that surgery is performed first on the leg or knee in which the patient has greater difficulty. Apart from this" The recovered amount must be returned within seven days Lucknow CMO Dr NB Singh said an expert doctors' panel had been formed to investigate the matter. The investigation found evidence that the elderly woman's relatives had signed a consent form at the doctor's clinic. The form mentions only the operation on the right leg. There is no clinical problem with the knee in that leg after the surgery either. Attempts were made several times to contact Dr CP Gupta, who performed the surgery in this case, and obtain his version, but he could not be reached.

stories.title: Dumper-car collision in Pilibhit kills 3:Two women among dead; two children injured, car had Uttarakhand number plate
stories.summary: Three people died after a dumper and a car collided violently in Pilibhit at around noon on Monday. The deceased included two women, while two children were injured in the accident. The collision was so severe that the car was badly damaged, leaving the driver trapped inside. After the accident, passers-by informed the police and ambulance services. With the help of local residents, the police took the injured to hospital. The police had to make considerable efforts to rescue the driver trapped inside the car. The accident took place on the Puranpur-Khutar Highway, around 42 kilometres from the district headquarters. The car (UK 18 A 6243) was travelling from Puranpur to Khutar. Meanwhile, a dumper (UP 31 BT 5892) coming from the opposite direction collided with the car. The words "Gaurakshak Dal" were found written on the back of the car. Puranpur CO Vidhi Bhushan Maurya said that the identities of the deceased were being established. The dumper driver fled the scene, leaving the vehicle behind. See pictures of the accident... Story being continuously updated...

stories.title: Akhilesh says, ‘Deputy CM will be rebuked again’:Fake teacher votes being made in Agra; asks, ‘You know who DM is linked to?’
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav took a jibe at Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak while addressing a press conference at the Samajwadi Party office in Lucknow on Monday, saying, “He will be reprimanded again.” Yadav also alleged that votes were being made in the names of fake teachers in Agra. Referring to the Agra District Magistrate, Manish Bansal, he said, “You know whom the Agra district magistrate is connected to.” According to available reports, Bansal is the son-in-law of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The SP chief said, "Muslim brothers showed patience to protect the spirit of India. They have faith in the country's Constitution. You are taking away their rights. You are not allowing them to go to court. This tradition is wrong. You cannot bulldoze the law. Ultimately, those who have broken the law will certainly be punished. Remember, you were calling our house illegal. The BJP has carried out the most illegal construction." Read Akhilesh's key points 1-The real crisis is the BJP; people are ready to remove it Akhilesh said, "The real crisis is the BJP. People are ready to remove it this time. Find out about the floods and how much loss the farmers suffered. People's homes and houses collapsed. More than 80 people lost their lives." BJP will be punished for the way Shankaracharya was treated The Samajwadi Party chief said, “The BJP will be punished for the way Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand was treated. He was not allowed to bathe in the Ganga. Just think-they engage in politics over dead bodies. Was the count of those who died at the largest Kumbh Mela in Hinduism accurate? If the Chief Minister is a true cow lover, he should keep 100 cows. Our society has been serving cows for 500 years.”

stories.title: Mayawati alleges Chandrashekhar was made to win through EVM rigging:Targets EC; says votes must not be counted for another candidate
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) national president Mayawati launched a direct attack on Azad Samaj Party national president and Nagina MP Chandrashekhar Azad on Monday. She claimed that Chandrashekhar was made to win the election in Nagina by rigging the EVMs. Chandrashekhar had no significant support base in the constituency. Former Chief Minister Mayawati spoke to news agencies at the BSP office on Monday. Questioning the use of EVMs, she said that the BSP had opposed their use from the very beginning. The party had approached the Supreme Court seeking voting through ballot papers. On the controversy surrounding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the BSP chief said: There should be no doubt in people's minds about free and fair elections in the country. The vote cast by a voter for a particular candidate should be counted in favour of that candidate, and not counted for someone else. Read the key points from Mayawati's press conference... 1- Votes should be counted in favour of the candidate chosen by the voter Mayawati said the Constitution has given every citizen of the country the right to vote. Through this right, people choose a government of their choice. Under Article 324 of the Constitution, the Election Commission has been entrusted with the responsibility of conducting elections. Every voter should be free to vote for the candidate or party of their choice, and their vote should be counted for the candidate or party for whom they voted. Voters should not have any doubt that their vote has gone to someone else or that it has been counted in favour of another candidate or party. 2- 'People will lose faith in democracy' Mayawati said that doubts among voters about the election process would weaken their faith in democracy. The Election Commission should dispel all such misconceptions so that people's confidence in the election process remains intact. For nearly five decades, elections in the country were conducted using ballot papers. After voting, the ballot papers were opened and counted in the presence of representatives of political parties. Later, voting through EVMs was introduced. When the Congress was in power at the Centre, the BJP had also raised questions about EVMs. At the time, the BJP had said that an EVM was a machine and that the electronic chip inside it could be tampered with. The former chief minister said that a book related to EVMs had also been published at the time and questions had been raised about the use of the machines. After coming to power, instead of ending the EVM system, the BJP continued it. 3- 'Fear that Dalit and backward-class votes could be influenced' Mayawati said the BSP was formed to serve the interests of oppressed people, Dalits and members of the extremely backward classes. People remain apprehensive about the votes of these communities because of EVMs. The lack of trust in EVMs among party supporters is also affecting their inclination to vote. 4- Chandrashekhar works at the BJP's behest Mayawati claimed that Chandrashekhar Azad had no significant support base in Nagina, yet he won the election. She alleged that he was helped to win through manipulation of EVMs. He works at the BJP's behest. He turns up to meet officials and hold protests. He misleads young people. These youths are then forced to ruin their futures by becoming embroiled in court proceedings. 5- Questions also raised over VVPAT The BSP chief said her party had challenged the EVM-based election process in the Supreme Court. Following this, the VVPAT system was introduced alongside EVMs. However, she said this too had not allayed her concerns. Not all VVPAT slips are counted during the counting of votes cast through EVMs. This makes it impossible to give voters complete assurance that their vote was credited to the candidate or party they had voted for. Any electronic machine can give rise to doubts. Therefore, the Election Commission should put in place a system that gives voters complete confidence in the integrity of their vote and its accurate counting. 6- "There is anger in the opposition; such a situation should not arise" Mayawati said misconceptions persisted among people over several issues related to the elections. The Election Commission was responsible for clearing them up. There was anger in the opposition over this as well, and such a situation should not arise. The BSP chief expressed hope that the Election Commission would seriously consider her concerns and put in place a system that would ensure everyone's confidence in free and fair elections in the country. Chandrashekhar won Nagina by more than 1.5 lakh votes In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Chandrashekhar Azad contested the Nagina seat on the Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram) ticket. According to Election Commission data, he received 5,12,552 votes. He defeated the BJP's Om Kumar by a margin of 1,51,473 votes. Chandrashekhar received 51.19% of the vote. In this election, the Samajwadi Party's Manoj Kumar received 1,02,374 votes, while the BSP's Surendra Pal Singh received 13,272 votes. Chandrashekhar's victory enhanced his political stature, and he entered the Lok Sabha.

stories.title: Congress workers write ‘traitor’ outside CEC’s Agra home:Smear black paint, clash with police in Lucknow; women bring bangles in Kashi
stories.summary: Congress workers have taken to the streets across Uttar Pradesh demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. In Agra, Congress workers smeared black paint on the wall outside Gyanesh Kumar’s residence and wrote, “Gyanesh Kumar, traitor, vote thief.” In Lucknow, police stopped Congress workers who were marching to gherao the Election Commission office, leading to a confrontation. The protesters climbed onto the barricades and there was heavy pushing and shoving. When police tried to remove them, some workers lay down on the road. Police lifted them by their legs and put them into vans and buses before taking them to Eco Garden. In Kashi, Congress workers hit a poster of the Chief Election Commissioner with shoes. Women workers joined the protest carrying bangles. A scuffle also broke out between Congress workers and police in Gorakhpur. Police tied a rope outside the DM’s residence to block their way. Congress Mahanagar president Raghavendra Chaubey said the election process was not conducted fairly. He alleged that there were large-scale irregularities in the voter list. Party workers raised slogans calling him a "vote thief". Women arrived carrying bangles and said the Election Commissioner should wear them. Party office-bearers also hit his posters with shoes and slippers. Meanwhile, Congress workers in Prayagraj will stage a protest following a call by the All India Congress Committee. They will take out a protest march at 12 noon from near the Gandhi statue at Balson Chauraha. They will walk to the Collectorate while raising slogans and submit a memorandum to the District Magistrate. Earlier, on Friday, Congress workers had burnt a poster of Gyanesh Kumar while raising slogans. They have demanded his resignation. Students had also staged a protest against the Chief Election Commissioner in Prayagraj and warned of further agitation. Two Election Commissioners raise 4 major questions 1. Changes in Form-6: Both questioned the requirement for new voters to provide details of their own or family members’ names in the previous SIR list. Sandhu called it illegal and demanded its removal. 2. Control of voter data: Both questioned why control over the voter database is increasingly shifting to Delhi and why states’ access is being restricted. 3. 1.6 million appeals in Bengal: Sandhu asked who filed around 1.6 million appeals over the deletion of names and who authorised them. 4. 97 voters in Goa: The 97 voters found eligible during the verification could not be included in the final list due to a software problem.

stories.title: ‘Toti chor will keep stealing, water will keep flowing’:Yogi takes swipe at Akhilesh; says ‘need not worry, appointment letters will be distributed every week’
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath handed joining letters to 1,375 gram panchayat officers in Lucknow. During the event, two women candidates became emotional. Lucknow's Shruti Srivastava said in a choked voice, "I became pregnant. I was worried about my child's future, but I have no reason to worry now." Gorakhpur's Beauty Shahi said, "My family's financial situation is not good. It will improve now." Her voice, too, faltered as she said this. Earlier, Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said, "Lord Hanuman alone had gone to Lanka and set it on fire. He had returned after assessing the full strength of Ravan. You are 1,375 people. Tell me, will you set the Lanka of the Samajwadi Party and Congress on fire or not? Do not worry; we keep setting fires on our own every day." 6,672 people got jobs in 10 days Rajbhar says Shivpal’s aides used to set rates for jobs as soon as vacancies were announced Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said the department has changed under CM Yogi Adityanath’s vision. Before 2017, it was considered limited to paperwork and sanitation. Today, he said, the department has become a major driver of development across 57,000 gram panchayats. He said 6,581 gram panchayat officers had been recruited, honorariums for panchayat assistants had been increased, and modern panchayat secretariats developed. Banking services are now available locally, he said, so people no longer have to visit tehsils or blocks. Rajbhar said, “It is CM Yogi’s contribution that people got jobs without paying money.” He alleged that under the Samajwadi Party government, whenever a job was issued, “Shivpalji’s aides would go across the state and fix the rate for jobs. If you paid money, you got a job.” Rajbhar says, “Congress-SP are actually dead; they have to be wiped out in 2027”. Rajbhar said that if people want jobs without paying money, they should make Yogi the CM for a third term. He said Congress and SP leaders claim that nothing is happening because “the power of their glasses must be low”. He also claimed that the proportion of girls attending school had risen from 40% a decade ago to 100% today. Referring to law and order, Rajbhar said CM Yogi had warned that those who harass women would face “Yamraj”. He alleged that Congress and SP were pursuing “politics of opposition and hatred” rather than ideology, while people wanted politics based on brotherhood. He said, “In 2027, SP has to be wiped out, and Congress has to be reduced by half.” Using the example of Hanuman setting Lanka on fire, Rajbhar asked the gathering of 1,375 people whether they would “burn the Lanka of SP and Congress”. He added, “Don’t worry, we keep setting the fire every day on our own.” Minister Shahi says, “We will not let anyone remain below the poverty line” Agriculture Minister Surya Pratap Shahi said 9.5 lakh youths in Uttar Pradesh had got jobs without bribery, corruption or recommendations. He said Mahatma Gandhi's dream of India was now being realised. “Congress leaders used to contest elections in Gandhi's name but did not improve conditions in villages,” he said. Under the Modi-Yogi governments, roads have been expanded to villages, Shahi said, adding that Uttar Pradesh is the fastest-growing state in the country. More than 3 crore individual toilets have also been built, he said. “The responsibility of changing the fortunes of villages and villagers is now being handed over to you. We will not let anyone remain below the poverty line and will bring everyone out of the BPL category,” Shahi said.

stories.title: SP leader arrested for promising bank employee ‘IAS job’:Praised her beauty, character; hiding at relative’s house in Aligarh
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Rajan Ahmed Rizvi, who told a woman bank employee, "I will get you made an IAS officer through the CM quota", has been arrested in Mathura. He had been absconding for 12 days and was hiding at a relative's house in Aligarh. Acting on a tip-off, Mathura police raided the house and arrested him on Sunday. SP leader Dr Rajan Rizvi, 38, had been continuously harassing the woman bank employee. He followed her, conducted surveillance of her house and somehow obtained her private number to send her objectionable messages. Distressed by the harassment, the bank employee filed a case at Mathura Kotwali on 16 September. The SP then hastily removed Dr. Rajan Rizvi from the post of state general secretary of its Minority Assembly. ASP says Court granted bail to SP leader ASP Ashna Chaudhary said, "On Sunday, the Kotwali police and the SWAT team raided Dharramafi village in the Quarsi police station area of Aligarh. Ahmed Rizvi was found hiding there. He was brought to Mathura from there. He was produced in court here, where he was granted bail." Read the SP leader's WhatsApp message to the bank employee If my words hurt you, I apologise. I did not say anything to you that was against propriety. I respect you greatly. You are a woman with an extraordinary aura. Along with being beautiful, you have a very good character. In other words, 'You are a complete woman'. Given your personality, I do not like you having this job. If the SP forms the government, I will try to get you made an IAS officer through the Chief Minister's quota on a deputation basis. Meeting during a morning walk The woman is a customer service associate at a government bank in Mathura. Her husband is an officer in the Forest Department in Mathura. The accused SP leader, Dr. Rajan Rizvi (45), lives right next to the Forest Department office. He holds a PhD and is a professor at Faiz-e-Aam Degree College. He has been active in the SP for a long time. He has also previously served as the city president. He has a wife and a daughter. The woman said that she had met the Samajwadi Party leader during her morning walk. After that, he began coming to the bank every day and staring at her. He also obtained her private mobile number and started sending her objectionable messages repeatedly. When she, troubled by this, asked him to stop, he began offering to get her made an IAS officer. When she blocked his number, he started obtaining private information about her and her husband. Read the allegations made by the woman in the FIR...

stories.title: DSP dies on expressway after Creta crashes into truck:Promoted from inspector 6 months ago; first posting was in Barabanki
stories.summary: A Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) who was injured in a road accident in Uttar Pradesh’s Etawah died during treatment on Sunday night. His Creta crashed into a truck from behind on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway on Saturday. DSP Narendra Singh, 55, and his gunner, Constable Yogendra Singh, suffered serious injuries in the accident. The impact was so severe that the front of the car was badly damaged and parts of the vehicle were scattered across the expressway. Both men were trapped inside the car. After receiving information from passers-by, police reached the spot and cut open the car doors to rescue them. They were rushed to Saifai PGI, where they were admitted for treatment. Narendra Singh died at around 11.20 pm on Sunday. The accident took place near Kauwa Rampura village in the Usrahar police station area, around 47 km from the district headquarters. Singh was originally from Noida and had been promoted from inspector to DSP around six months ago. His first posting after the promotion was in Barabanki. He is survived by his wife, a son and two daughters. His gunner remains in critical condition. See two pictures of the incident DSP was travelling from Lucknow to Agra Barabanki SP Arpit Vijayvargiya said Narendra Singh was originally from Baraula in Sector 49 of Gautam Buddh Nagar (Noida), where his family lives. Singh himself was staying in a government quarter. On Saturday, he left for Agra with his gunner for some work. The Creta, registration number UP 16 FH 0027, was being driven by Constable Yogendra Singh, while the DSP was seated beside him. The accident occurred near Usrahar. According to eyewitnesses, the collision with the truck caused parts of the car’s engine to hit both the DSP and his gunner. The vehicle was badly damaged. The truck driver fled the spot with the vehicle. Expressway security personnel and Usrahar police reached the location after receiving information and rescued the two injured men. They were taken by ambulance to Saifai Medical University, where they were undergoing treatment. Family members reach Saifai Following the DSP’s death, Saifai police reached the medical university after receiving information from the administration. Police took custody of the body and kept it in the mortuary at the university. According to the police, the inquest proceedings and post-mortem examination will be carried out by Monday afternoon. Singh’s brother and two daughters also reached Saifai on Sunday. The family was distressed following his death.

stories.title: Villagers clash at power station in Varanasi:Protested over power cuts ; dispute erupted after shutting another feeder’s supply
stories.summary: There was an uproar over a power outage at the Gajokhar electricity substation in Varanasi's Pindra tehsil area on Sunday night. Angry over the lack of electricity in several villages connected to the Hiramanpur feeder for three days, villagers reached the substation at around 8 p.m. They demanded that the power supply to other feeders also remain shut until electricity was restored to their feeder. When officials did not arrive at the spot, the villagers had the power supply to the other feeders shut as well. This also cut off electricity to Gajokhar village and other areas. Following this, villagers from other villages reached the substation. They got into an argument with the villagers who were already staging a sit-in there. Villagers clash over switching off electricity It is being reported that after the dispute between the two sides escalated, a fight broke out on the substation premises. The two sides have accused each other of throwing objects and engaging in violence. A Scorpio vehicle was also allegedly damaged. As soon as information about the commotion was received, Phulpur SHO Ajay Raj Verma reached the spot with a police team. The police pacified both sides and brought the situation under control. Electricity supply through the other feeders was restored afterwards. Several electricity poles were damaged in the storm Gajokhar SDO Amit Kumar Singh said several electricity poles had broken and been uprooted in the storm and rain three days earlier. As a result, power supply was disrupted in several villages connected to the Hiramanpur feeder. He said the villagers had been told that work was underway to restore the electricity supply, but they remained adamant that officials be called to the spot. When the officials did not arrive, they had the power supply to other feeders switched off as well. SDO says pole had been replaced by evening SDO Amit Kumar Singh said the damaged pole had been replaced by Sunday evening. Power supply to the Hiramanpur feeder is expected to be restored by Monday morning. Following this assurance, the villagers left the electricity substation. According to Phulpur police, neither side has filed a written complaint so far. The matter will be investigated, and appropriate action will be taken once a complaint is received.

stories.title: Rivers swell in UP, 600 families leave homes:Bridges submerged in Gonda-Budaun; schools shut in 8 cities
stories.summary: After four days of continuous rain in Uttar Pradesh, rivers are in spate. Eight rivers are flowing above the danger mark, while several villages have been flooded. The Gandak (Narayani) river in Kushinagar flooded after water was released from Nepal. Around 1,400 families in two villages have been affected, with 600 families forced to leave their homes and live on the embankment. In Gonda and Badaun, water is flowing over small bridges. People are crossing the bridges through 2-3 feet of water. In Sitapur, the water levels of the Sarayan and Pirai rivers have risen 30 cm above the danger mark. People are using tractors and JCB machines to move their belongings to safer places. In Unnao, people are forced to stay on the roofs of houses and shops. Meanwhile, the weather is clear in most cities, including Lucknow, Kanpur, Prayagraj and Varanasi, on Monday. The sun was seen after 96 hours. However, schools have been closed in eight districts due to waterlogging and the heavy rain alert. Schools up to Class 12 have been closed in Bareilly, Lakhimpur Kheri, Pilibhit, Sambhal, Bijnor and Moradabad, while schools up to Class 8 have been shut in Gonda and Jaunpur. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 46 districts today as well. Earlier, the spell of rain stopped across the state from Sunday evening. In Barabanki, a 150-year-old mosque that had been hanging over the Saryu river for 30 days was washed away. In Unnao, water accumulated on the Ganga Expressway had to be pumped out. The Rashtra Prerna Sthal complex in Lucknow was flooded. In Hardoi, an ADM's vehicle got stuck in the mud.

stories.title: 30-year-old ‘Miss Pretty India’ found hanging:9 lakh Facebook followers; Varanasi native wrote, ‘Love yourself’
stories.summary: Social media influencer Nidhi Tiwari, a resident of Varanasi, committed suicide by hanging herself. The 30-year-old had previously won the 'Miss Pretty India' title in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh. Her body was found on Sunday morning in a room at her home in Singrauli's Bhusa Mod area. According to police, Nidhi had shared an emotional post on Facebook before taking her own life. She had 9,28,000 followers on Facebook and 7,12,000 on Instagram. She made dance reels to songs and shared them on Facebook and Instagram. Her final post read: Love yourself Before committing suicide, Nidhi shared an emotional post on Facebook. In it, she wrote, "No one completed this incomplete heart; I completed it myself. That is why people say, love yourself, not someone else. Search for yourself within yourself. How long will you keep searching for yourself in someone else?" Argument over the phone with a Delhi-based youth at 8 p.m. Nidhi's mother, Lata Tiwari, said, "At around 8 p.m. on Saturday, Nidhi had an argument over the phone with a youth named Sonu Singh, who lives in Delhi." Nidhi then shared an emotional post on social media and locked herself in her room. Between 9 p.m. and 10 p.m., the family knocked on the room door. Nidhi refused to eat and asked them to leave her alone. The family then went to sleep. The family said, "The room door did not open for a long time on Sunday morning. Suspecting that something untoward had happened, we informed the police." When the police reached the spot and looked inside through the window, they saw Nidhi's body hanging from a noose. Nidhi lived with her mother and younger sister Nidhi Tiwari's neighbour Bhupendra Singh told Dainik Bhaskar over the phone that Nidhi lived with her mother and younger sister in the Bhusa Morh area. Her younger sister is a student. Nidhi's father, Ashok Tiwari, has been living separately from the family for around 15 years. He said Nidhi was one of four sisters. Her elder sister died by suicide after jumping into a well around five years ago. One younger sister is married and lives in Banaras. Won the 'Miss Pretty India' title in 2024 Nidhi Tiwari was highly active on social media. She made and posted reels, which were widely liked. Her social media accounts had lakhs of followers. She also attended local events. She had won titles at several beauty contests. In 2024, Nidhi won the 'Miss Pretty India' title. Her dream was to work as an actor in films. Phone calls and social media activity under investigation Morwa police station in-charge Dr Gyanendra Singh said, "Acting on information from the family, a police team reached the spot. The body was sent for a post-mortem examination. After the post-mortem, the body was handed over to the family. The police have recorded statements from the family." Nidhi's phone call details and social media activity are also being scrutinised. The police are trying to find out whom Nidhi had been in contact with before her death and what all aspects were connected to her last conversation.

stories.title: CM Yogi to arrive today on a 3-day visit:He will listen to the Shrimad Bhagwat Katha at Gorakhnath Temple and attend the tribute meeting
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath will arrive in Gorakhpur on Monday afternoon for a three-day visit. He will attend various programmes over the next three days. He will attend an award ceremony organised by a media organisation at Digvijaynath PG College. Before that, he will visit the residence of late senior advocate Krishna Gopal Pandey in Daudpur to pay tribute to him. All subsequent programmes will be held at the Gorakhnath Temple complex. He will attend programmes organised to mark the 57th death anniversary of the late Mahant Digvijaynath and the 12th death anniversary of the late Mahant Avedyanath. On the morning of Tuesday, 29 September, the Chief Minister will address a tribute ceremony marking the 57th death anniversary of late Mahant Digvijaynath at Gorakhnath Temple, as part of the weekly death anniversary programme for the two late mahants. On Wednesday, 30 September, the Chief Minister will address a tribute ceremony held to mark the 12th death anniversary of his spiritual guru, late Mahant Avaidyanath. A 7-day Shrimad Bhagwat Katha is being organised at Gorakhnath Temple as part of the tribute week celebrations. Alongside this, a weekly seminar has also been organised during the first session. Experts are speaking on different contemporary topics each day. Meanwhile, some inauguration and foundation stone-laying programmes may also be scheduled. He may hold a meeting with officials at the Gorakhnath Temple.

Where is the SP-Congress alliance stuck?:Alliance final, but seat-sharing remains unresolved; what is Akhilesh hiding by saying ‘all is well’?
stories.summary: For nearly a week, Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress leaders have been engaged in sharp exchanges over their alliance. Speculation grew that the alliance was on the verge of a split. Then, on Sunday, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav made a statement. He said, We are fighting on the surface, but we are united internally. This is part of our strategy. Now questions are being raised: If the alliance is already decided, what is the purpose of this war of words? Why is the seat-sharing formula still not being finalised? What exactly is Akhilesh trying to hide? Read the full UP Explainer… Question: Why are questions being raised over everything not being well between SP and Congress? Answer: Such questions have been raised since July. At that time too, the controversy began with a statement by Congress MP from Saharanpur Imran Masood. His recent remarks have also triggered the latest round of tension. On September 21, he said, How active Akhilesh ji is has no meaning. If there has to be an alliance, then do it; otherwise, we are going ahead with our preparations. There is no atmosphere anywhere in the country without Congress, so don’t even think of moving ahead without Congress. Question: If the war of words is a strategy, what will it achieve? Answer: The statements are not part of a joint SP-Congress strategy but are part of Congress' pressure politics. However, Akhilesh is calling it a joint strategy to send a message that ‘everything is fine within the alliance’. Question: Why are SP and Congress unable to reach an agreement on seat-sharing? Answer: Akhilesh Yadav and Rahul Gandhi held a closed-door meeting on July 20 to discuss seat-sharing. Priyanka Gandhi was also present. According to sources, Akhilesh told Rahul that Congress would have to name its candidates for the seats it wanted in UP, because the election had to be won at all costs. Question: By saying ‘everything is fine between us’, what is Akhilesh trying to hide? Answer: Senior journalist and political analyst Harshvardhan Tripathi says Akhilesh is not trying to hide anything by making such a statement. Rather, he is trying to protect himself from being blamed if the alliance breaks. Both Akhilesh and Rahul are in favour of the alliance. At least, this appears to be the case from Akhilesh's actions. Question: What will happen if the SP-Congress alliance breaks? Answer: Both parties will suffer from this. However, Congress is likely to face greater difficulties than SP, while the BJP would directly benefit. This can be understood in three points: (A) Congress will face an existential challenge (B) SP's Muslim vote could split (C) Anti-incumbency against BJP could weaken

stories.title: Negative RSS report could cost MLAs their tickets:Sangh takes charge of UP polls; feedback on legislators being gathered across 6 regions
stories.summary: The Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) has taken charge of preparations for the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Workers of the Sangh and its affiliated organisations are working on two fronts on the ground. First, they are gathering feedback on sitting MLAs and ticket aspirants. Second, they are creating an electoral atmosphere. The Sangh's growing influence at the Centre and in the state clearly indicates that if an incumbent MLA or ticket aspirant receives a negative report from the RSS, their chances of getting a ticket could be severely affected. The Sangh is preparing to take tough decisions at any level to help ensure the return of the Yogi government for a third consecutive term in Uttar Pradesh. Read the full report... Deliberations from Delhi to Lucknow on MLAs' ground support The RSS and BJP are aiming to form the government in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in 2027. Top functionaries have become active as part of the preparations. BJP national general secretary (organisation) BL Santosh, national general secretary Vinod Tawde and RSS joint general secretary Arun Kumar held discussions on the election strategy in Delhi. After this, Santosh and Tawde held a meeting with RSS functionaries in Lucknow. The functionaries shared their assessment of the ground situation involving the government, BJP and MLAs and gave their suggestions. Report card being prepared for every seat The RSS is preparing a report on every Assembly seat in each district. The assessment is mainly focused on two aspects: Detailed reports from the Kashi, Awadh, Gorakhpur, Kanpur, Meerut and Braj regions will be submitted to the central leadership and are expected to form a key basis for ticket distribution. Apart from these reports, displeasure among RSS functionaries could also become a factor in denying a ticket. On the other hand, candidates strongly backed by RSS functionaries could see their claims gain strength. Lesson from 2024: Ignoring feedback proved costly According to BJP sources, during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the RSS and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had suggested changing candidates on several seats and had flagged negative reports about several MPs. Ignoring this feedback and relying on the old faces proved costly for the party. BJP's tally in Uttar Pradesh fell from 62 seats to 33. This time, the Sangh is not willing to take any risk. Two major challenges before BJP and RSS Separate strategy being prepared for all six regions Meetings are being held across western UP, Braj, Kanpur-Bundelkhand, Awadh, Gorakhpur and Kashi. The Sangh, party, and government are simultaneously reaching out to the ground and collecting feedback. Key organisational and government decisions are being taken after discussions with eastern region regional pracharak Anil Kumar and western region regional pracharak Mahendra Kumar. Based on this ground report, separate strategies will be prepared for all six organisational regions. RSS has significant influence over BJP Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt says the RSS has considerable influence over the BJP from the Centre to Uttar Pradesh. The influence of the Sangh can also be seen in the BJP's national and state teams. He further says that national general secretary BL Santosh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and state general secretary (organisation) Dharampal Singh are taking political decisions related to the party and government only after consulting eastern region regional pracharak Anil Kumar and western region regional pracharak Mahendra Kumar.

‘Hang him for killing my daughter’:Jhansi mother says husband smashed daughter's phone days after love marriage, kept her locked at home
stories.summary: “My daughter Shivani truly loved Yash Thakur. One day, my daughter told me about their relationship and proposed marriage. Both families agreed. Around one-and-a-half years ago, the two had a love marriage. But after a few days, my son-in-law Yash started suspecting my daughter. He started beating her. Because of his suspicion, he broke my daughter’s mobile phone just 24 days after their marriage. We kept thinking that her marriage would settle down, but Yash’s behaviour did not improve. Troubled by frequent arguments and beatings, my daughter came to Jhansi and started living here three months ago. Yash also used to come here. On the night of August 30, he strangled my daughter to death. We want justice for our daughter. Just as my daughter was killed, Yash Thakur should also be hanged. He should be given the death penalty. We will fight for this.” This was said by Rekha Vanshkar, whose daughter Sudha alias Shivani (27) was killed in Jhansi. By late Friday, police arrested Yash Thakur after shooting him in the leg. A reward of ₹25,000 had been announced for him. The case is from the Sipri Bazaar police station area of the city. Shivani became friends with Yash while studying in Gwalior Shivani was a resident of Indergarh in Madhya Pradesh’s Datia district. Her father, Santram Vanshkar, sells fruits from a cart, while her mother, Rekha, works in homes in Delhi. Shivani was the eldest of six siblings. After completing her studies, she stayed at home. Her younger sisters Preeti and Neha are married. The family also includes one sister, Muskan (18), and two brothers, Aniket (17) and Kapil (14). Mother Rekha Vanshkar said, “My daughter Muskan was studying in Gwalior and Shivani was staying with her. During this time, Shivani got acquainted with Yash Thakur. They fell in love with each other. Around one-and-a-half years ago, they had a love marriage. After the marriage, my daughter started living with her in-laws in Gwalior. Yash worked at a clothes shop.” Mother says, ‘They taunted her for being Dalit’ The mother said, “Around a year ago, Yash beat my daughter with a hockey stick. When I went to bring my daughter home, Yash pointed a gun at me. He said that if Shivani left the house, he would kill her and also kill himself. We thought that my daughter’s marriage should not be ruined, so we came back. “Yash and his family knew before the marriage that we belonged to the Dalit community. But after the marriage, Yash and his mother started taunting her. His mother would tell her son to leave her, saying that he had married a girl from a lower caste. “The mother also said that her daughter was taunted over dowry. We had given whatever we could afford at the wedding. But dowry was also demanded several times. We are poor, so we could not fulfil their demands. We gave as much as we could. “Just two months ago, we had got my daughter an old mobile phone worth ₹60,000 on instalments. I was paying the instalments. After the murder, Yash also took the mobile phone with him.” Sister says, ‘Shivani and Yash had an argument before the murder’ Shivani’s sister Muskan said, “Troubled by suspicion and beatings, my sister Shivani rented a room near Awas Vikas Fauji Tiraha in Jhansi. My brother Aniket and I also started living with her. Meanwhile, my father and younger brother Kapil lived in the village. Yash would come to Jhansi occasionally. A day before Raksha Bandhan, Shivani went to Gwalior with her brother Kapil. Two days later, she returned to Jhansi with Yash, while Kapil went back to the village. “Muskan said there was an argument between her sister and brother-in-law Yash on the night of August 30. Yash was making objectionable remarks about the family. He told Shivani that he had slept with me. He also said he would beat our father with a slipper. “As the argument escalated, our maternal uncle Santosh, who lived nearby, arrived. He calmed everyone down. After this, my uncle took Aniket to his house. It was already late at night, so everyone went to sleep. I slept in my room, while my sister and brother-in-law slept in the other room. “At around 12.30am, I got up to drink water. Everything was normal. I also spoke to my sister and she spoke to me normally. Later, I wished my sister good night and went to sleep.” He asked for his bag at night, then bolted the door from outside Muskan said, “At around 1.30am to 2am, Yash knocked on my door and asked for his bag. After this, Yash secretly bolted my room from outside. At around 5am, when I tried to open the door to go to the bathroom, it would not open. “For around half an hour, I called out to my sister and brother-in-law, but there was no response. The cooler was running. I called my sister, but her number was switched off. I thought they might be sleeping, so I went back to sleep. At around 9am, our brother Aniket reached home. Both rooms had been bolted from outside.” Yash Thakur did not love my sister Muskan said, “My sister truly loved Yash, but he did not love my sister. We did not know that he would ever do something like this to my sister. My sister told me many times that he was very suspicious. “I will not go back to him now. I will stay with you people. He used to beat me a lot. Whenever they went somewhere, they would lock the house from outside so that my sister could not leave the house. They never even took her out anywhere. He did not give her any money for expenses. That is why our parents used to send money. “We want justice. It would be very good if he is given the death penalty. Otherwise, he should at least be sentenced to life imprisonment. We want him to remain in jail for the rest of his life.” Brother added, ‘Shivani’s body was found in the room’ Aniket said, “When I reached home, I saw that the door of my sister Shivani’s room was bolted from outside. I opened the bolt and went inside, and my sister’s body was lying on the floor. Blood was coming from her ear and there were marks on her neck. “The other room was also bolted from outside. I opened it and found Muskan sleeping. I woke her up. After this, people from the neighbourhood and family members reached the spot. Shivani was taken to the medical college, where doctors declared her dead. The post-mortem confirmed that she died due to strangulation.” ₹25,000 reward, arrested after being shot in the leg SP City Preeti Singh said, “After the murder, police were searching for Yash Thakur. The SSP had announced a reward of ₹25,000 for him. At around 1am late on Friday night, police received information that Yash had come to Jhansi on a scooter. Following this, the SWAT team and Sipri Bazaar police cordoned off the area near Simardha village. “After finding himself surrounded, Yash opened fire at the police team. In retaliatory action, he was shot in the leg and injured. He was subsequently arrested by police.”

stories.title: Pradeep Mishra returns to Barsana after 27 months:To narrate Katha at Radha Rani Temple where he once apologised; pandal ready for 50,000
stories.summary: Pandit Pradeep Mishra’s Shiv Mahapuran Katha begins in Barsana, Mathura, on Monday. On Sunday evening, Mishra visited the Radha Rani Temple, folded his hands and sought blessings. This is his first visit to Barsana since he apologised at the temple 27 months ago over remarks about Radha Rani. The pandal has been set up at a ground on Ghazipur Sanket Road, near Prem Sarovar, around 3 km from Barsana. Arrangements have been made for more than 50,000 people. The Katha will be held from September 28 to October 4, from 1pm to 4pm. It is being organised by Shri Vitthalesh Seva Samiti, Sehore. Organisers warn against fake VIP passes Shri Vitthalesh Seva Samiti has issued a warning that there is no provision for VIP passes for the Katha. The organisers have appealed to people to report anyone demanding money in exchange for fake passes or claiming to arrange entry through fraudulent means. What happened 27 months ago? 9 June 2024: Remarks about Radha Rani spark controversy During a discourse in Omkareshwar on June 9, 2024, Pradeep Mishra made remarks about Radha Rani’s birthplace, marriage and family. He said Radha Rani was from Rawal rather than Barsana and made other comments about her family. The remarks went viral and drew opposition from saints and people in Braj. Premanand Maharaj also criticised Mishra over his comments. 29 June 2024: Mishra reached Barsana to apologise Following the opposition, Pradeep Mishra visited the Radha Rani Temple in Barsana on June 29, 2024. He apologised for his remarks about Radha Rani’s birth and marriage and sought forgiveness from the people of Braj. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar at the time, Mishra said he had come because of the love of the people of Braj and apologised if his words had hurt anyone. Saints expected at Shiv Mahapuran Katha Several saints are expected to attend the Katha, including Swami Gurusharananand Maharaj, Ramesh Baba Maharaj, Vinod Das Baba Maharaj, Yoga Rishi Swami Ramdev, Jagadguru Vishnu Swami Sampradacharya Santoshacharya Maharaj Satua Baba and Mahant Balaknath Yogi Maharaj.

stories.title: Eight-time SP MLA Ram Govind Chaudhary dies:Breathed his last at Lucknow PGI; Akhilesh Yadav and other SP leaders pay tribute
stories.summary: Senior Samajwadi Party leader and former Leader of Opposition in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly Ram Govind Chaudhary died late on Friday night. He breathed his last at the Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences (PGI) in Lucknow. He was 80. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav expressed grief over his death. Akhilesh wrote- "The death of senior Samajwadi Party leader and former Leader of Opposition Ram Govind Chaudhary is extremely sad. May God grant peace to his soul. May the grieving family be given the strength to bear this loss. Heartfelt tribute." Treatment was under way at Lucknow PGI According to the family, he had been ill for some time. He was undergoing treatment at the PGI in Lucknow. His condition suddenly deteriorated late on Friday night. The doctors tried to save him, but he died. He is survived by his wife, Kalawati Devi, and a son. As soon as news of his death emerged, a wave of grief swept through his supporters and Samajwadi Party leaders in Ballia and Lucknow. Samajwadi Party leaders and workers are paying tribute at his residence and at the hospital. Samajwadi Party general secretary Shivpal Singh Yadav also expressed grief over his death. Joined the socialist movement as a student Ram Govind Chaudhary was born on 9 July 1946 in Ballia district. His father was named Dwarika Chaudhary and his mother was named Tileshwari Devi. He completed his postgraduate and LLB studies at TD College, Ballia. Chaudhary had become associated with socialist ideology from his student days. During the Emergency, he took part in the Total Revolution movement and was also jailed. At the time, most activists from Ballia were released from jail after 19 months, but Ram Govind Chaudhary was released after 25 months. Lost the 2022 election from the Bansdih seat In the 2022 Assembly election, Ram Govind Chaudhary lost the election from the Bansdih seat to the BJP's Ketki Singh. Ram Govind Chaudhary was considered a prominent leader of the socialist movement. He was close to Mulayam Singh Yadav and Akhilesh Yadav. He consistently raised issues related to education and the backward classes. In recent years too, he remained active as the Samajwadi Party's national secretary. He continued to question the government's policies. Political career gained momentum after meeting Chandra Shekhar During the 1977 Lok Sabha election, Ram Govind Chaudhary met former Prime Minister Chandra Shekhar. After being released from jail, Chandra Shekhar was impressed by his work and made him a close associate. Chaudhary's political career then progressed rapidly. Ram Govind Chaudhary was elected as an MLA several times. He contested the Bansdih Assembly seat on a Samajwadi Party ticket. He served as the Basic Education and Child Development and Nutrition Minister in Akhilesh Yadav's government from 2012 to 2017. He then served as the Leader of the Opposition in the Assembly from 2017 to 2022.

After receiving information from Premanand Ji’s disciples, police immediately reached Sarvodaya Hospital, where Rasik Dulari had been taken for treatment. During the investigation, police found injury marks on Rasik Dulari’s private parts. A grinder was also found in his room. Police are investigating whether he had used it to injure himself. According to eyewitnesses, Rasik Dulari’s penis had also been severed. He had lost a considerable amount of blood. See 2 pictures- Rasik Dulari received initiation from Premanandji in 2015 Dinesh, an electrician from Jabalpur, took initiation in September 2015 and changed his name to Rasik Dulari Sharan. Since June, he had been living at Guru Kripa Kunj, which is associated with the Keli Kunj Ashram. Around 50 disciples associated with Sant Premanand Maharaj also live in the building. Rasik Dulari Sharan was alone in his room at the time of the incident. On Thursday evening, Rasik Dulari Sharan went to the roof of the building’s fourth floor. After sitting there for some time, he jumped from the building. He was taken to Sarvodaya Hospital in a critical condition, where he died. Police, who arrived after being informed, sent the body for a post-mortem examination. Police investigate whether it was murder or suicide Vrindavan Circle Officer Sandeep Singh said Sarvodaya Hospital had informed police about the young man’s death. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and the family has been informed. The forensic team and Vrindavan police inspected the scene. He said the death was being investigated from both the suicide and murder angles.

stories.title: Fortuner overturns in rain, police couple save 5:Kannauj district panchayat chief trapped inside car, rescued by breaking windows with rifle
stories.summary: A Fortuner overturned after breaking through the divider on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Kannauj during heavy rain on Friday afternoon. Five people, including Sultanpur district panchayat chairperson Usha Singh, were trapped inside the car. Screams rang out at the scene after the accident. A constable and his wife, who were passing by at the time, stopped after seeing the accident. The constable immediately began trying to rescue the people trapped inside the car. When the car doors would not open, he smashed the windows with his rifle. The constable's wife sought help from drivers of vehicles passing nearby. The five people, including the district panchayat chairperson, were then pulled out of the car one by one. All those injured in the accident have been admitted to hospital. The accident took place at around 2 p.m. in the Talgram area. Here are two pictures of the accident- Now, the full details- Sultanpur District Panchayat chairperson Usha Singh was travelling from Lucknow to Noida in a Fortuner car. The car was being driven by Vikas Yadav, a resident of Sultanpur's Dhanpatganj. Also travelling in the car were Ayush Verma from Lakhimpur, gunner Head Constable Arvind Kumar and Geetanjali Singh from Noida. The car reached near kilometre 171 on the Agra-Lucknow Expressway. Meanwhile, the driver lost control of the car due to the heavy rain and its speed. The car went out of control and collided with the divider. It then broke through around 20 metres of fencing, entered the other lane and overturned. All five people in the car were injured in the accident. Constable couple saved the lives of 5 people Meanwhile, female Constable Archana Singh, posted at the Asha Jyoti Centre in Kannauj, was travelling from Saurikh to Kannauj with her constable husband, Amit Teवतिया. On the way, they saw the overturned Fortuner on the expressway. They immediately stopped their vehicle and reached the spot. Five people were trapped inside the car. The car doors would not open. Amit Tewatia immediately began the rescue operation. He broke the car windows with his service rifle and created a way to get the people out. All of them were brought out. People trapped in the car were brought out after the windows were smashed After this, the two informed the control room about the accident. As soon as the information was received, Ambulance 172, the police from the police station and a team from UPEIDA reached the spot. UPEIDA security officer Manohar Singh and the safety vehicle team helped with the rescue operation. Injured Usha Singh, Ayush Verma and Arvind Kumar were sent by ambulance to Tirva Medical College for treatment. The other injured people were given first aid at the scene. Station House Officer Ranjana Pandey said the accident was being investigated.

stories.title: Ram Mandir employee was first to spot donation theft:Claims 67 people involved, video sent to Champat Rai; chargesheet reveals 10 major findings
stories.summary: Police have filed a 73,480-page chargesheet in court in the case involving the theft of offerings from the Shri Ram Mandir in Ayodhya. It states that employee Anand Kumar Chaudhary was the first to see money from the offerings being stolen. He sent a video to Champat Rai, the trust’s then general secretary. The date was 4 June 2026. The chargesheet states that 67 employees could be involved in the theft. In the video, employees can be seen hiding bundles of notes around their waists. This was the first incident after which the layers of the ongoing theft began to unravel. Champat Rai was not in Ayodhya at the time. After reaching Ayodhya the next day, on 5 June 2026, Dr Anil Mishra, Gopal Rao and Dr Narendra showed the CCTV footage from the room. It clearly showed the employees’ actions. In the 73,480-page chargesheet, police have presented evidence against eight accused, including CCTV footage, digital evidence recovered from mobile phones, witness statements, cash deposits in bank accounts, property purchases and recovery evidence. Here are the 10 major revelations from the chargesheet… 1. The theft was committed by employees involved in sorting and counting, not outsiders In the chargesheet, police stated that no outsider had access to the donations or offerings. The theft was allegedly committed by employees responsible for counting and sorting them. CCTV footage was considered important evidence. The investigation report contains evidence showing different accused tampering with banknotes in the counting room, taking out money and helping other accused in the operation. 2. Mobile chats contained conversations about hiding and removing bundles of notes Police said text messages recovered from mobile phones, along with CCTV footage, were important evidence. According to the report, messages were found between Anukalp Mishra, Avinash Shukla and Lavkush Mishra about keeping, hiding, exchanging and moving bundles of cash. The CDRs contain evidence of continuous communication between the accused. 3. Police admit assets were bought with stolen offerings Police linked bank accounts and assets to track the money allegedly stolen from offerings. The investigation found information about cash deposits in the accounts of several accused and their relatives, as well as the purchase of land and houses, cars, motorbikes, cameras and jewellery. Police stated that these items were bought with money stolen from offerings. 4. Avinash Shukla was seen most often on CCTV According to police, CCTV footage showed Avinash Shukla, alias Shani, removing donation and offering money himself 85 times and helping the other accused four times. Police have claimed that ₹20.39 lakh, $4,424, silver and gold jewellery, and later a Brezza car were recovered based on information provided by him. 5. Lavkush bought land and a house worth ₹43.43 lakh During the investigation, police alleged that Lavkush Mishra bought land worth ₹22.52 lakh in his wife Supriya Mishra’s name and spent around ₹20.91 lakh constructing a house on it. The total amount was stated to be around ₹43.43 lakh. Police also linked this to money allegedly accumulated through the theft of offerings. CCTV footage showed Lavkush removing money himself four times and helping his co-accused 52 times. 6. Anukalp’s father acquired a ₹55 lakh house with offering money The investigation also looked into the financing of a house worth around ₹55 lakh purchased in the name of Anukalp Mishra’s father, Ravindra Mishra. According to the report, details emerged of a ₹29.5 lakh bank transfer and a ₹25 lakh cash payment. The investigation also found that money was deposited through the accounts of relatives and acquaintances and later used to purchase the house. 7. Around ₹78.55 lakh in cash found in Karunesh’s accounts The chargesheet mentions cash deposits totalling around ₹78.55 lakh in the SBI account of Karunesh Pandey’s wife, Rupa. It also details cash deposits in his brother’s accounts. Police have claimed that CCTV footage showed Karunesh committing the crime himself twice and helping the co-accused 68 times. 8. ₹20.93 lakh in cash deposited in the accounts of Ramashankar Mishra’s family According to the investigation, around ₹20.93 lakh in cash was deposited into various bank accounts belonging to Ramashankar Mishra and his family members. In addition, police gathered information about the purchase of a plot for ₹42 lakh, a camera worth around ₹1.03 lakh and jewellery. 9. Ramashankar Yadav’s role was not limited to counting Ramashankar Yadav, alias Tinnu, has been described in the chargesheet as having been associated for a long time with the process of handling the trust’s donations and offerings. According to the report, around ₹8.48 lakh in cash was deposited into his accounts. It also mentions an Ertiga car, a Bullet motorcycle and property worth ₹9.50 lakh. Police said they recovered ₹4 lakh, the Ertiga and the Bullet based on information provided by him. 10. Champat Rai and Dr Anil given clean chit Former general secretary Champat Rai, trustee Dr Anil Mishra and Gopal Rao, who served as the Mandir’s administration head, have been made government witnesses. Police have dismissed claims that valuable jewellery went missing from the Mandir. The key points are contained in the 59-page chargesheet, while the remaining pages mention evidence related to the investigation and statements by the accused and witnesses. After the theft of offerings came to light, a case was registered on 25 June against Ramashankar Yadav Tinnu, Anukalp Mishra, Lavkush Mishra, Manish Yadav, Karunesh Pandey, Ramashankar Mishra, Avinash Shukla and retired bank employee Subhash Srivastava, based on a written complaint by trust member Krishnamohan and the SIT’s recommendation.

stories.title: Lover beaten, girlfriend chased and harassed in Buduan:6-7 youths caught couple in forest, threatened them and snatched ₹1,500
stories.summary: Six to seven youths in Uttar Pradesh’s Buduan surrounded a boyfriend and his girlfriend after finding them in a compromising position in a forest, in an incident similar to one reported in Bihar’s Jamui. They chased and assaulted the couple before harassing the woman. The frightened couple begged them to let them go, but the accused did not relent. They continued filming the two and also snatched ₹1,500 from them. The accused fled the spot when passers-by arrived. The incident took place on 17 September. Police took cognisance of the matter after the video went viral on social media. Police identified the victims and arrested three accused. After learning about the incident, Bareilly Zone ADG Ramit Sharma and DIG Ajay Sahni also reached the spot. Instructions have been issued to arrest the remaining accused. The incident took place in the Ughaiti police station area, 43 km from the district headquarters. Watch the visuals related to the incident- Now, understand the full case On 17 September, a young man and woman went for a walk in the forest near Siddhbaroliya Temple, close to Saraibaroliya village. They were in a relationship. They had parked their bike a short distance away. After seeing the bike, six to seven people, including accused Sugendra Kumar, 24, a resident of Swarupur, and Saraibaroliya residents Bechain Jatav, 40, and Chhote Jatav, 32, surrounded and apprehended them. The accused began beating the couple while hurling abuses. During the assault, the woman was harassed. The accused also recorded a video of the incident. In the video, all the accused can be seen shouting. They beat both the woman and the man. They then snatched ₹1,500 from them and threatened to make the video viral. The accused released the couple around half an hour later when passers-by arrived. Police traced the victims through the bike’s number The accused posted the same video on social media on Thursday evening. Police then traced the victims using the number plate of their bike. During questioning, it emerged that the man was a resident of Sambhal district, while the woman was from the Ughaiti area. Police took written complaints from both of them. They then began searching for the accused based on the video. Police arrested three accused, Sugendra Kumar, Bechain Jatav and Chhote Jatav, from the forest near Saraibaroliya village on Thursday night. The police produced all three in court, which sent them to jail. Teams have been deployed to search for the other accused. SSP Ankita Sharma said — The entire case came to light on the basis of the video. Three accused have been arrested, while some unidentified suspects are absconding in the case. They too will be arrested soon. Now, about the Jamui incident — Student and female student dragged down from hill; crowd surrounded them and pressured them to marry “Get them married, get them married, take them to the temple.” There was a crowd all around, with torchlights shining and only people’s faces visible. No one was fully dressed — some were wearing lungis, while others were in half-dresses. They were muscular young men covered in mud. It was dark around them, and the entire area was deserted as evening had fallen... This is what a young man from the village adjacent to the scene of the incident said. He told the Bhaskar reporter the full story on the condition of anonymity. He said most of the people present were merely watching the incident, but when the accused began creating more trouble, some people rescued the two young people. Meanwhile, the SP said that eight accused had been arrested so far in the case. An encounter took place with the main accused. Raids are continuing to make further arrests. Even 40 hours after the incident, the police did not know about the case. They learnt of it only after receiving information from Delhi and Patna. When and how did the entire incident happen?

stories.title: Engineer son stayed on burning bus with mother:Both burnt alive in Noida fire; BJP leader’s wife and son were travelling to Mahoba
stories.summary: The wife and son of a BJP leader from Mahoba were burnt alive in a bus fire in Noida, with the son reportedly choosing to stay with his mother, who had difficulty walking and could not get off the bus like several other passengers, despite having the chance to escape. Even as the driver and conductor shouted, the son continued trying to save his mother until the very end. The bodies of the mother and son could not be identified on Thursday. After DNA testing, the family identified both bodies. The post-mortem examination revealed that the two had lost consciousness after the bus filled with heavy smoke and could not get out. According to the BJP leader, his son, an engineer with IndiGo Airlines, was travelling from Gurugram to Mahoba with his mother. Shashank was returning to Mahoba from Gurugram with his mother Neeraj Gupta is a resident of Charkhari in Mahoba. He said that his wife, Sunita Gupta, had been staying with their son Shashank in Gurugram for around a month. Shashank was an engineer with IndiGo Airlines in Gurugram. Sunita had been staying with her son to receive treatment for knee pain. Three days ago, Shashank's uncle Dhirendra Gupta suffered a heart attack. Sunita and Shashank were travelling from Gurugram to Mahoba to visit him. According to Neeraj, the two had set off on a bus operated by Raj Kalpana Travels because they could not get train reservations. They were sitting in the back seat of the bus. Shashank tried to save his mother when the bus caught fire Neeraj said that when the bus caught fire, passengers began getting out and running outside. A stampede-like situation developed. Sunita had difficulty walking, so she could not flee. Shashank kept trying to get her out. The driver and conductor also told Shashank to get out, but he refused to leave his mother behind. He said he would come out only with his mother. The bus filled with so much smoke that the mother and son lost consciousness According to Neeraj, the bus quickly filled with smoke after it caught fire. It was difficult for Sunita to get out. Shashank kept trying to save her. The driver and his mother told him to get out, but he refused to leave without his mother. The mother and son lost consciousness inside the bus after it filled with heavy smoke. They were burnt alive in the fire. According to the family, passengers had complained of a burning smell before the bus caught fire, but the bus was not stopped in time. The accident would not have been so serious if the bus had been stopped. Mother and son identified through DNA testing and physical descriptions Neeraj Gupta said that his wife and son's bodies had been burned so badly that identifying them was difficult. The identities of both bodies were confirmed through DNA testing. The bodies are being brought to Mahoba. My son, Shashank Gupta, was an engineer with IndiGo Airlines in Gurugram. His younger son, Nikhil Gupta (22), is studying. Now read what happened in the Noida bus fire A sleeper bus caught fire on the Yamuna Expressway in Noida on Wednesday night. There were 35 passengers on board, nine of whom were burnt alive. Several passengers broke the windows and jumped out to save themselves. According to eyewitnesses, there was a strong smell of something burning in the bus some time before the accident. One passenger said he informed the driver and conductor, but his warning was ignored. The two began smoking in the cabin. After some time, flames started coming from near the driver's seat. The fire quickly spread throughout the bus. Passengers began screaming inside. Some were breaking windows, while others were trying to get out through the smoke. Several passengers managed to escape, but nine people were burnt to death.

stories.title: Mock drill for terror attack at Taj Mahal:70 personnel rush in after report of 2 terrorists entering; both neutralised in 40 minutes
stories.summary: A mock drill was conducted at Agra’s Taj Mahal on Friday morning to assess security arrangements, simulating two terrorists entering the monument’s riverside area and opening indiscriminate fire. The exercise also simulated one security personnel being injured, following which security agencies swung into action, personnel took up positions and the two terrorists were killed in retaliatory action. The mock drill continued from 10:30 a.m. to 11:10 a.m. The CISF, Uttar Pradesh Police, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), fire service, bomb disposal squad, dog squad, LIU and medical team took part. Around 70 personnel took part in the entire exercise. Its objective was to assess the preparedness and coordination among security agencies in the event of a terrorist attack-like situation at the Taj Mahal. See 2 pictures... Practice held for indiscriminate firing At 10:30 a.m., information was received that two terrorists were firing in the riverside area of the Taj Mahal. The exercise simulated a CISF personnel stationed on the riverside being injured. As soon as the information was received, the CISF control room was alerted. All security agencies were then informed. The CISF Quick Response Team (QRT) surrounded the two terrorists as they were moving towards the rear of the Taj Mahal. Security agencies cordoned off the entire riverside area. The two terrorists were firing from hiding. The personnel also retaliated. The operation continued for around 40 minutes. The CISF then conducted an exercise in which it carried out an operation and eliminated both terrorists. Meanwhile, the Uttar Pradesh Police cordoned off the area outside the Taj Mahal. A medical team provided first aid to the injured personnel at the scene. Joint teams searched the entire area After this, joint teams from the CISF, Uttar Pradesh Police, BDDS and the dog squad searched the entire area. During the mock drill, the procedures for reporting an emergency, cordoning off the area and coordination among the security forces were tested. In addition, the response operation, providing medical assistance to the injured, and the search operation were also practised. The mock drill was conducted under the supervision of Rishi Kaushik, Commandant of the CISF Taj Mahal unit. After the exercise ended, officers from all the agencies held a meeting and reviewed the entire operation. According to officials, the drill was aimed at testing the preparedness and coordination of security agencies in a situation resembling a terrorist attack on the Taj Mahal. The mock drill lasted around 40 minutes.

stories.title: Ajay Rai climbs barricades in Lucknow:Congress workers clash with police in rain during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: Congress workers protesting in Lucknow, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, clashed with police on Thursday. The confrontation led to pushing and shoving as the protesters attempted to march towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and the Chief Minister’s residence. The police stopped the protesters with barricades about 200 metres into their march. Angry over being stopped, Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai, MLA Aradhana Mishra and other party workers climbed the barricades and raised slogans. A scuffle then broke out between the police and Congress workers. Congress leader Shiv Pandey suffered an injury to his leg. He alleged that he was injured by a police baton. The situation remained tense at the spot, with Congress workers continuing their protest in the rain. Women protesters were also seen carrying posters with the slogan, “Vote Chor, Gaddi Chhod”. CEC’s Meerut, Varanasi visits postponed The Election Commission has postponed two programmes in Uttar Pradesh that CEC Gyanesh Kumar was scheduled to attend. The first programme was scheduled in Meerut on September 25, while the second was planned in Varanasi on September 28. The EC said both programmes had been postponed on September 21 and that the decision was not related to the ongoing controversy. See four pictures of the protest... What is the controversy over removal of the CEC? According to a September 23 report by The Indian Express, two Election Commissioners had raised written objections over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) at least 14 times in the past 10 months. Four of these objections were raised on the same day. The Election Commission, however, said such objections were part of the normal procedure and that all final decisions, including those related to the SIR, were taken unanimously.
