stories.summary: European waters have recorded their hottest summer, with rising temperatures affecting marine habitats and species. The Bay of Biscay experienced a significant temperature rise, with marine heatwaves extending throughout the season. Kelp forests in northern Spain have sharply declined, impacting local marine ecosystems. Additionally, octopus populations are surging in southern England, affecting traditional fishing yields. Non-native species are also expanding into the Mediterranean, altering local food chains and competitive dynamics.

India to join SCO national coordinators meeting in Islamabad

This gathering will endorse the event calendar for Pakistan's upcoming presidency leading up to the Council of Heads of State summit. Although there are ongoing bilateral tensions, India continues to engage with the SCO, particularly focusing on initiatives addressing terrorism.

In 1993, a project set out to reconnect wildlife habitat from Yellowstone to Canada's Yukon
stories.summary: The Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative is proudly nominated for Prince William's Earthshot Prize in 2026. This groundbreaking effort aims to reinstate a vital 3,400-kilometre wildlife corridor through the majestic Rocky Mountains. Achieving over 200 wildlife crossings and safeguarding around 24 million hectares, Indigenous involvement is key to strengthening conservation practices here. Looking forward, the initiative hopes to secure an extra 20 million hectares by 2030.

California acquired 640 acres near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation
stories.summary: California state officials secured 640 acres of desert land near Pioneertown for western Joshua tree conservation. Researchers identified this land as suitable for the species despite climate change. The California Department of Fish and Wildlife completed the acquisition with funds from the Western Joshua Tree Conservation Fund. Collaboration with Native American tribes is planned for long-term stewardship of the property.

stories.title: Sister Stephanie Baliga: From aspiring elite runner to nun raising $2.6 million, and she’s still running
stories.summary: Sister Stephanie Baliga once dreamed of becoming an elite runner before finding her calling as a nun. She has since used the Chicago Marathon to raise more than $2.6 million for Mission of Our Lady of the Angels, helping feed families in need. Now, she continues running and fundraising through Team OLA.

stories.title: A $45 million San Francisco mansion once owned by Larry Ellison kept its new buyer secret for a year
stories.summary: Private equity mogul Chuck Esserman has made headlines by purchasing a lavish mansion in San Francisco for $45 million, making it the most expensive home sale in the city for 2025. Formerly owned by Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, who bought it for just $3.9 million 37 years ago, the estate boasts stunning renovations and breathtaking views of the Golden Gate Bridge, reflecting its rich legacy.

stories.title: Rhode Island federal judge orders revival of $7 billion Solar for All program canceled in 2025
stories.summary: A Rhode Island federal judge has ordered the revival of the $7 billion Solar for All program after the Trump administration’s EPA canceled it in August 2025. Judge Mary S. McElroy ruled the agency overstepped its authority in terminating the Biden-era initiative, which aimed to expand solar access for low-income households nationwide.

stories.title: ‘Shake the prisons’: Hamas warned Israel before October 7 attack, says ex-defence minister Gallant
stories.summary: Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar reportedly sent a warning to Israel before the October 7 attack. Former defence minister Yoav Gallant stated that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu received international alerts about this threat. Gallant expressed that such warnings should have been prioritized as critical security issues. He claimed that Netanyahu excluded senior security officials from crucial discussions during the conflict.

stories.title: An 8,000-acre South Carolina forest was bought for conservation after drawing developer interest
stories.summary: Georgetown County School Board voted in favor of state plans to acquire two large land parcels for conservation. These lands would contribute to the creation of Carvers Bay State Forest and protect Arcadia East. The Board Member emphasized the importance of preserving natural spaces amid residential growth in the region. Conservation efforts received backing from local organizations and government councils expressing commitment to environmental protection.

stories.title: ‘They wanted everything up front’: Trump’s UN envoy says Iran was not negotiating in good faith to end war
3 killed, 4 injured after fight erupts into gunfire at Detroit strip club in US
stories.summary: Three individuals lost their lives while four others sustained injuries in a shooting at a Detroit strip club. The confrontation, which occurred early on Sunday morning, stemmed from an argument between several patrons. Detroit Police Chief Todd Bettison confirmed that the three deceased victims were all men. Authorities are actively investigating the case and have received multiple complaints about the venue this year.

stories.title: Charles Baker started garage business for his son in 1980; it has helped 12,500 plus workers
stories.summary: Charles P. Baker III, who died at 101, co-founded Baker Industries with his wife Louise in 1980 after their son struggled to find suitable work. What began as a two-person garage business grew into a workforce development nonprofit that has hired, trained and mentored more than 12,500 people who faced barriers to employment.

stories.title: Nepal battered by severe rain: 21 dead, 5 missing as floods, landslides worsen
stories.summary: In Nepal, heavy rainfall has caused devastating floods and landslides, resulting in 21 lives lost and extensive damage. Authorities have evacuated around 3,000 residents from perilous areas to guarantee their safety. This deluge follows the earlier Bhotekoshi floods, which had a death toll of over 1,400. As rescue efforts continue, landslides have disrupted operations in several districts, and tourists in vulnerable areas are being advised to take precautions.

stories.title: Louisiana neighbors' land fight over 70 feet ends with $15K damages after dead cow appears
stories.summary: In a prolonged conflict stemming from years of camaraderie, two families in Louisiana found themselves locked in a bitter legal battle regarding their property lines. The Colvins asserted ownership over a disputed 70-foot timberland strip, triggering rising tensions. Ultimately, the court sided with the Joneses, affirming the original boundary marked by an aged fence while ordering the Colvins to halt disruptive actions and compensate for damages.

stories.title: F-35 fighter jets, 200+ airmen arrive as US participates in India's Tarang Shakti air exercise
stories.summary: Six American F-35 fighter jets and over 200 US airmen arrived in Jodhpur to participate in Exercise Tarang Shakti. This exercise features the participation of more than 40 countries and strengthens international cooperation in military operations. US Ambassador Sergio Gor and Indian officials observed a joint demonstration by Indian and US Army personnel. The exercise emphasizes deepening bilateral training and trust among participating nations.

stories.title: US rejects Iran's claim of capturing underwater drone, calls move 'desperate'
stories.summary: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps has reported the capture of a US underwater drone in the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz. In response, the US military dismissed this assertion, clarifying that the drone in question had experienced a malfunction prior to any claims from Iran. This development follows Iran's earlier announcement regarding another US military drone capture.

stories.title: Karnataka flags drug landing cost-MRP gap at hospitals of up to 52.6 times; seeks Centre's intervention
IndiGo A321 suffers tail strike during go around at Bangalore; plane lands safely in second attempt
stories.summary: On Sunday, an IndiGo Airbus A321 operating flight 6E 6542 experienced a tail strike during a go-around. The incident occurred while attempting to land in gusty weather at Bengaluru airport. All passengers and crew were safely disembarked, and the aircraft is undergoing maintenance checks. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is investigating the incident and has engaged with IndiGo regarding pilot training enhancements.

stories.title: Yellowstone rangers remove 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026
stories.summary: Yellowstone rangers removed more than 20,100 pieces of trash from geothermal areas in 2026, along with over 5,000 rocks and sticks and 280 visitor hats. Staff also collected coins worth more than $18. Among the unusual finds were AirPods, golf tees, an inhaler, Invisalign retainers, fake nails and children’s toys.

stories.title: 'Will never bow our head': Iran embassy invokes Baahubali to echo Pezeshkian's defiant UN speech
stories.summary: Highlighting the parallels between resilience and heroism, the Iranian Embassy in Hyderabad unveiled a video featuring President Masoud Pezeshkian's UNGA address likened to the epic tale of Baahubali. The embassy conveyed Iran's steadfastness against external pressures, as exemplified in Dr. Pezeshkian's rejection of U.S. sanctions. He asserted Iran's commitment to dialogue while maintaining a robust defense posture, amidst escalating U.S.-Iran tensions.

stories.title: CJP says Mumbai Police denied permission for Oct 2 protest, launches ‘Jail Bharo Andolan’
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party is gearing up for a protest in Mumbai after being denied police permission. Founder Abhijeet Dipke announced plans for a Jail Bharo Andolan on Gandhi Jayanti. This announcement follows reports of CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka and volunteers facing detention in Assam. NCP (SP) spokesperson Anish Gawande condemned the detentions, labeling them illegal and unconstitutional. The CJP remains dedicated to advocating for social issues despite these setbacks.

Parvesh Verma slap row: Man files complaint, police reveal prior FIR against him
stories.summary: Delhi Police has received a complaint regarding an alleged incident involving Minister Parvesh Verma. The complaint states that Verma slapped a man during a road inspection in Tilak Nagar. AAP leader Jarnail Singh was present and questioned the quality of the road when the incident occurred. Verma disputes the allegations, claiming the video does not show the full context.

stories.title: Pennsylvania teacher’s $5,000 donation helps turn China’s Maowusu desert into a forest of 50,000 trees
stories.summary: Pennsylvania teacher Ronald Sakolsky reunited with Chinese farmer Yin Yuzhen 26 years after donating $5,000 to support her tree-planting efforts in Inner Mongolia. His contribution helped Yin expand her work in the Maowusu Desert, which has since become a forest of around 50,000 trees, turning their friendship into an enduring environmental story.

stories.title: In 2020, a New Jersey man lost his job and began mowing lawns for free; six years later...
stories.summary: After losing his job, Brian Schwartz founded a remarkable volunteer initiative named I Want To Mow Your Lawn. This program offers complimentary lawn care services to seniors, veterans, and others in need. Through a digital platform, volunteers across all 50 states now connect with those requiring assistance, resulting in a thriving community of over 2,000 compassionate participants who collectively enhance the spirit of service and support nationwide.

stories.title: From 39th to 10th, India breaks into WorldSkills top league
stories.summary: At WorldSkills Shanghai 2026, India proudly secured the 10th position, reflecting remarkable strides in the global skills competition landscape. The nation earned six silver medals, demonstrating growth in a variety of fields. Significant first-time achievements in Dental Prosthetics and Digital Interactive Media Design were particularly noteworthy. With 70 competitors involved, India's investment in skill development is evident, promoting an enriched skilling ecosystem through global participation.

stories.title: $888 million for ads: US Republicans ramp up sends to defend 39 House seats once deemed 'safe'
stories.summary: Republicans are investing significantly in House races previously deemed secure as they confront emerging electoral challenges. Spending has surged to $888 million in advertising compared to $666 million by Democrats. Economic pressures are impacting traditionally Republican districts and may influence voter sentiments. Republican strategists are concerned about potential losses and are campaigning vigorously. Maintaining their House majority is now a priority for GOP leaders ahead of the elections.

In 2018, Jon Bon Jovi paid $10 million for a Palm Beach home, demolished it and rebuilt; 2 years later
stories.summary: Jon Bon Jovi recently sold his exquisite Palm Beach residence for nearly $20 million, a significant increase from the $10 million he initially invested in the land. On the same day, he invested $43 million in a lavish oceanfront property extending over 10,000 square feet, featuring high-end amenities such as a swimming pool and private courtyard. This move underlines the increasing demand for luxury real estate in Palm Beach.

In 1988, Ohio attorney Neil McKown secretly bought 155 neglected acres; 38 years later...
stories.summary: Neil McKown purchased an overgrown 155-acre property in Shelby, which began a family farming journey. As the years progressed, the McKown family expanded their land holdings and improved their farming practices. Sam McKown, Neil's son, now manages the farm's daily operations and focuses on quality hay production. The family emphasizes conservation, practicing sustainable land management and engaging with the community.

stories.title: NEET leak fallout: CISF to guard NTA’s confidential exam areas
stories.summary: Responding to the alarming issue of exam paper leaks, the National Testing Agency has fortified its security protocols. A dedicated team of 29 CISF personnel is now assigned to the agency's new office for rigorous oversight. In addition to advancing cybersecurity measures, the NTA is revisiting its entire examination-cycle systems to thwart unauthorized access. Independent audits will also be conducted, aiming for a significant improvement in examination integrity moving forward.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu govt rolls back law and order department’s RTI exemption amid backlash
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu government faced backlash after it issued a notification that exempted the Public (Law and Order) Department from the Right to Information (RTI) Act. Critics, including numerous political leaders, argued that such an action would jeopardize transparency and obstruct public access to crucial law records. In response to widespread criticism, the government promptly withdrew the exemption, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the RTI Act.

stories.summary: Christa Barfield left healthcare after a 2018 trip to Martinique inspired her to become a farmer. She now runs FarmerJawn Agriculture, a 128-acre Black-owned farm in West Chester, Pennsylvania, and employs 26 people. Her operation also has urban and suburban locations, with CornerJawn, a food and medicine store in Kensington, scheduled to open on October 1.

RAF Fairford alert: Several arrested, homes evacuated near US air base - key details
stories.summary: Several men were arrested near RAF Fairford on suspicion of violations under the Explosives Act. Residents of the nearby village of Whelford were evacuated to a leisure center in Cirencester. Police established a cordon around the area while an Army explosive ordnance disposal team assessed several vehicles. Counter-terrorism police are leading the investigation but have not confirmed a link to RAF Fairford.

'We trusted EC in 2017': Akhilesh alleges poll officials deleted SP votes in 2022
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav has accused the Election Commission of deliberately deleting votes belonging to the Samajwadi Party. He argues that this malpractice has been ongoing for years but is only now gaining attention. In his statement, he noted that voters from the 2019 elections were unjustly denied the opportunity to vote in 2022. This controversy follows recent revelations about objections within the Election Commission regarding the electoral rolls revision.

stories.title: 'Marriage does not advance a child’s age': Delhi HC rejects Muslim personal law defence in POCSO case
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has taken a firm stance by ruling against a man who married a 16-year-old under Muslim personal law, emphasizing that this does not exempt him from POCSO charges concerning sexual activity. While the girl asserted her consent, the court reiterated the importance of legal safeguards for minors. Attempts to contest the FIR based on her claims were rejected, underscoring the inviolability of child protection laws.

stories.title: Kapil Sibal alleges ‘unilateral’ EC decisions, seeks action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
stories.summary: Kapil Sibal has raised concerns over the Election Commission's decision-making under Gyanesh Kumar during a ten-month period. His allegations include that decisions were made unilaterally, bypassing other commissioners and statutory protocols. Sibal has called for an investigation into the electoral rolls and recent elections conducted in Bihar and West Bengal. In response, the Election Commission acknowledged concerns and proposed several corrective measures to address them.

Gorakhpur was among the worst-affected areas, with continuous rainfall inundating several parts of the city. Ravi Kishan, however, inspected waterlogged areas and took stock of the situation.

Georgia nonprofit worker stole $96,713 meant for abused children, spent it on Netflix, lingerie, etc
stories.summary: Jennifer O’Neal, a former programme specialist at Georgia child advocacy nonprofit CASA of Polk & Haralson, pleaded guilty to stealing $96,713 between 2018 and 2022. According to the US Department of Justice, she used the organisation's funds for personal expenses including utility bills, Netflix, Six Flags, lingerie, softball gear and home theatre equipment. Her sentencing is scheduled for December 17, 2026.

'Tried to drag me out': TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh's car smashed, says guards drew guns to save him - video
stories.summary: Kunal Ghosh, a Trinamool Congress MLA, alleged an attempted murder on his way to a program in Kolkata. Armed men reportedly smashed his car window and attempted to drag him outside. This incident followed a previous attack on Saturday where his vehicle was damaged by protesters in Uttarpara. Ghosh accused the BJP of involvement and criticized the police response to these incidents.

stories.title: Vijay government exempts Tamil Nadu Public (Law & Order) department from RTI- what it means
Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG train in Gujarat, launches Rs 1,542 crore railway projects
stories.summary: Amit Shah inaugurated India's first LNG-powered train and several railway projects valued at over Rs 1,542 crore. The LNG-powered train utilizes a dual-fuel system, helping to significantly reduce diesel consumption. Shah also laid the foundation for the indigenous Kavach automatic train protection system, targeting enhanced railway safety. Additionally, the Sabarmati-Sarkhej railway line doubling project aims to improve connectivity and facilitate industrial growth.

California teens, 16 and 17, build AI system to detect fall risks in older adults, win $100,000
stories.summary: California teenagers Ruoqi Li and Jason Yang developed SafeStrides, an AI-powered fall-risk system combining smartphone camera tracking and wearable sensors. The system analyses walking patterns, provides instant risk assessments and offers mobility and home-safety guidance. Their engineering project earned them recognition as 2026 Davidson Fellows and a shared $100,000 scholarship.

stories.title: Bengal SIR row: CM Suvendu Adhikari pins blame on Mamata for deletion of 27 lakh voters
stories.summary: Suvendu Adhikari claimed the deletions were ordered by judicial officers following directions from the Supreme Court in a case filed by Banerjee herself. He accused the TMC leader of trying to shift responsibility after her defeat in the Assembly elections. The Election Commission has said 22.21 lakh of the deleted voters had filed appeals seeking their names to be restored.

stories.title: PM Modi recalls 2016 surgical strikes on Mann Ki Baat, says terrorism will get decisive response
stories.summary: During his radio address, Mann Ki Baat, Prime Minister Narendra Modi discussed key national issues, including the 2016 surgical strikes against terrorism, reaffirming India's strong stance and zero-tolerance policy toward cross-border threats. He called on citizens to contribute to the Census, emphasized cleanliness efforts linked to Mahatma Gandhi, and expressed support for the youth's battle against narcotics.

stories.title: ‘Congress part of every conspiracy’: CM Yogi hits out at opposition amid 'dissent within EC' row

stories.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier this week that he expected Prime Minister Narendra Modi to visit Canada in December. He also said negotiations on the trade agreement were making “good progress”. The possible December visit could coincide with the G20 Summit in Miami, which US President Donald Trump is scheduled to host on December 14 and 15.

Floating solar cuts seabed light in French Polynesia, with no detectable lagoon temperature
stories.summary: Floating photovoltaic platforms in a French Polynesian lagoon created substantial reductions in light reaching the seabed, which was studied for one year. Researchers monitored the environmental impact of four platforms and a control area during the study. They observed strong attenuation in ultraviolet radiation under the platforms, affecting diverse wavelengths. However, changes in water temperature remained statistically insignificant and below sensor accuracy levels.

Bodies of 4 Tangkhul Naga men allegedly killed by militants found near Myanmar border in Manipur
stories.summary: Four Tangkhul Naga men were found dead near the Myanmar border in Kamjong district, raising alarms after locals reported a militant attack on residents Thursday night. Authorities confirmed that the victims exhibited numerous bullet wounds, adding urgency to the investigation. This disturbing event feeds into the escalating unrest between Kuki and Naga groups in Manipur, a conflict that has been ongoing since February, even under heavy security measures.

NASA sent 12.5M tomato seeds to space in 1984; by 1990, 40,000 schools in 40 countries grew them
stories.summary: In 1984, NASA initiated the SEEDS project aimed at exploring how the space environment affects plant growth. Participants, comprising approximately 3.3 million students from diverse educational backgrounds worldwide, received kits that included seeds launched into space and Earth-based controls for comparison. Preliminary findings indicated a marginally enhanced germination rate for the seeds sent to space, though notable growth differences diminished during the plants' life cycles.

stories.title: Retired UK rail engineer turns East Sussex garden into 50-foot railway with solar-powered trolley
stories.summary: Adrian Backshall transformed his East Sussex garden into a working railway, inspired by his railway engineering career. The garden features a unique 50-foot railway with a solar-powered system and authentic railway memorabilia. Initially a lockdown project, it has evolved to include a Victorian-style carriage for entertaining guests. Backshall's project reflects a blend of history and engineering, following his retirement from Network Rail.

Belgian quarry uses solar panels and sheep in a project to produce clean power
stories.summary: A quarry in Florennes, Wallonia, is implementing an agrivoltaic project that integrates solar panels with sheep farming. This project installs 3,240 photovoltaic panels over 3.3 hectares, allowing sheep to graze underneath. It will generate 2.33 GWh of electricity annually, with some used by the quarry and surplus supplied to the public grid. The initiative aims to reduce the quarry's carbon footprint and support local agriculture.

stories.summary: In a heartbreaking turn of events, 14 servicemen from Kazakhstan tragically perished during a naval exercise hindered by harsh weather conditions. In the aftermath, five defense officials were detained over alleged negligence regarding navigation protocols. Rescue teams bravely recovered three soldiers from the Caspian Sea. President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has declared a national day of mourning to pay tribute to those who lost their lives.

stories.title: The Backstory: When 'Tau' Devi Lal won the PM race, and then gave it away with a twist
stories.summary: Emerging as a pivotal political leader during the 1989 governmental shift in India, Chaudhary Devi Lal first captured the deputy Prime Minister position via astute maneuvering within the Janata Dal party. His major influence was rooted in unwavering backing from Haryana's agricultural sector. Yet, infighting ultimately led to the VP Singh government's downfall.

stories.title: California crews uncover possible 45-million-year-old ‘thunder beast’ fossils in Oceanside
stories.summary: Fossilised bones from a large hoofed mammal were uncovered during an excavation project in Oceanside, California. Paleontologists are studying the remains, which may belong to a thunder beast or a swamp rhino. The discovery took place approximately 12 feet below the surface in the Santiago Formation's sedimentary rock. Researchers are working to determine the exact identity of the fossils found during construction.

Prosecutors said the company used customers’ insurance information to bill government-backed healthcare programmes for COVID-19 testing services that were never provided. Seyhun admitted helping submit fraudulent claims and agreed to forfeit $4.31 million.

This recall affects light-up glasses, crown headbands, sparkle headbands, and light-up ties sold from September 2016 to May 2026. Please ensure your children stop using these items and contact ABC Trading to obtain a refund. Dispose of these toys following local hazardous waste protocols.

23 Himveers battle weeks of gruelling Himalayan climbing to reach 24,131-ft Mt Abi Gamin & unfurl Tricolour
stories.summary: At more than 7,000 metres, Abi Gamin presents a combination of thin air, freezing temperatures, snow and glacier terrain. Weather conditions can also change rapidly at such heights. The ITBP said the expedition demonstrated the force's mountaineering skills, determination and team spirit. After weeks on the mountain, the team finally reached the summit on September 16.

stories.summary: A study by Colorado State University reveals that saffron flourishes under semi-shaded solar panels, yielding better results than those without shade. Projections suggest considerable net revenue from saffron and electricity production in five years, although challenges related to installation and upkeep remain for successful implementation.

stories.summary: Oregon has approved a $2 million purchase of Abiqua Falls, a famous 92-foot waterfall that was put up for sale by its private owner in February. stories.summary: A new primary school is being built in Castel Madama with a strong focus on sustainability and the use of reusable materials. About 70% of the waste from the existing school will be redirected to this project, promoting a circular economy. Designed with community needs in mind, the school will provide spaces for social and educational activities after hours. Accessibility is a priority, ensuring that all individuals can benefit.

stories.title: Massachusetts restores cranberry bog to protect rare trout that moves between river and ocean
stories.summary: Massachusetts is restoring Century Bog, a former cranberry farm in Plymouth and Wareham, to complete protection of Red Brook from White Island Pond to Buttermilk Bay. stories.summary: In response to Pakistan's statements at the UN Human Rights Council about Kashmir, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi asserted that Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India. Investigators have struggled to access details from Wakode's mobile phone, which is locked. The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is probing allegations of discrimination and harassment preceding his death. This has resulted in a marked decline in oil flows, affecting the global economy and forcing the US to reconsider its stance. Concurrently, India is exploring ways to capitalize on its geographical advantages against China.

An English artist paid £2,090 for a painting listed only as ‘in the style of’ Helen McNicoll
stories.summary: David Taylor made an astonishing find at a UK auction when he acquired an oil painting incorrectly attributed to Helen McNicoll for just £2,090. After expert examination, it was confirmed to be McNicoll's masterpiece, The Bean Harvest, appraised at £300,000. Canadian collector Pierre Lassonde later purchased the artwork for £174,000, ensuring its return to public viewing after a century, highlighting the often-hidden treasures lurking in regional auction houses.

Meet Lucas Rojas, 16, who turned one inclusive kickball game into a six-team league with 40+ players
stories.summary: Lucas Rojas launched LINKball, a vibrant kickball league designed to unite students with special needs and enthusiastic volunteers. Starting from a charity match, this initiative blossomed into a well-organized league of six teams. Acknowledging his impactful work, Rojas was awarded the $10,000 Gloria Barron Prize. Each season sees over 40 players and 60 volunteers engaging in the program, promoting inclusivity and teamwork through the joy of sports.

Delhi HC denies anticipatory bail to YouTuber Ajeet Bharti in casteist remarks case
stories.summary: Delhi High Court rejected Ajeet Bharti's request for anticipatory bail in a caste-related case. The court determined that a prima facie case was established under the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes Act. Bharti's remarks were deemed derogatory and part of a public social media discussion. His lawyer argued against the applicability of the SC/ST Act based on provocation.

The Backstory: When EC disagreements went public, from Seshan to Lavasa
stories.summary: The Election Commission is facing fresh scrutiny after an Indian Express report highlighted disagreements among its members over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise. The dispute recalls two earlier episodes of internal dissent: TN Seshan’s legal battle over the multi-member poll panel in the 1990s and Ashok Lavasa’s dissent during the 2019 Lok Sabha elections. Both cases shaped debates over the EC’s functioning and authority.

Michael Tilson Thomas’ 32-year home is now on sale for $9.85M
stories.summary: Michael Tilson Thomas’s residence in Pacific Heights is now on the market following his passing earlier this year. The mansion was a sanctuary for the musician and his husband Joshua Robison for nearly three decades. Built in 1906, the four-level home features a blend of architectural styles and modern amenities added over the years. Its spacious rooms hosted numerous distinguished guests from the music and architecture worlds.

'Manipulated the voter rolls': Mahua Moitra files police complaint against Gyanesh Kumar over SIR row
stories.summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra has filed a police complaint against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, alleging manipulation of voter rolls. Moitra raised specific concerns over unauthorized amendments to Form 6 related to voter registration. Her allegations came a day after a report stated that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the SIR.

Florida businessman’s 4 beach lots to become public after a decade and multiple lawsuits
stories.summary: Michael Holderness bought four beachfront lots on Florida’s Siesta Key in 2016 and 2017, leading to years of disputes with Sarasota County over public access and development. Under a settlement, the county will receive the four lots and make them public beach property, while Holderness gets a nearby parcel valued at nearly $2.8 million, $500,000 and permission to build a 5,000-square-foot home.

When the umpires disagree: 10 questions at the heart of the Election Commission row
stories.summary: The Election Commission is facing questions over reported disagreements between two election commissioners and the CEC on electoral-roll management, decision-making and access to voter data. The controversy has also revived broader concerns over how dissent is handled within the poll panel, the role of the CEC, the appointment of election commissioners and safeguards for voters during large-scale roll revisions.

stories.title: Ontario mother of 10 says she received C$6,300 from C$19,000 GoFundMe; sister charged with fraud
stories.summary: Maryanne Mullett, an Ontario mother of ten, sustained injuries while assisting stranded drivers in January 2026. A dedicated GoFundMe campaign raised about C$19,000 to assist her recovery and family needs. Unfortunately, she received merely C$6,300, leading to financial disputes. A family member faces fraud charges related to the funds, and Mullett has since launched a new fundraiser, highlighting the critical need for better protections in crowdfunding efforts.

stories.title: Florida gas prices surge as some stations charge over $5
stories.summary: Drivers in Florida are experiencing rising petrol prices, with some stations exceeding $5 a gallon. The statewide average has reached $4.29 per gallon, the highest since May. This increase is significantly influenced by rising global oil prices caused by geopolitical tensions. As crude oil prices rise, consumers in Florida and beyond are facing higher costs at the pump.

stories.title: 'Should act fairly': Calcutta HC slams EC for assigning 'envelope' symbol to rival TMC faction
stories.summary: In a recent ruling, the Calcutta high court expressed discontent towards the Election Commission concerning its symbol allocation to the Democratic Trinamool Congress. The court challenged the integrity of the symbol distribution process, pointing out the existence of numerous alternatives. Justice Krishna Rao remarked on the legal issues created by these decisions, leading to appeals from parties involved.

Miami Dolphins star Zach Sieler turned 250-acre Missouri property into outdoor classroom for kids
stories.summary: The Sieler Safe Haven Foundation, founded by Miami Dolphins star Zach Sieler and his wife Hannah in 2022, is developing their 250-acre Missouri property for agriculture, wildlife and outdoor education. The couple plans to raise cattle there while giving children hands-on experiences in farming, conservation, fishing, hunting and land management.

stories.title: Mexican immigrant couple closes Colorado restaurant after 31 years as children build their own lives
stories.summary: A Colorado couple who moved from Mexico in 1995 with their three children opened Los Tarascos and ran it for 31 years. Jose and Maria Caballero are now closing the Fort Collins restaurant, saying they have achieved the dream that brought them to the US: giving their children the chance to build independent lives and careers outside the family business.

stories.title: What is happening between Twitch streamers KitsuFox and Nosiiree? Breakup drama explained
stories.summary: During her live streaming session, KitsuFox revealed that her ex-partner, Nosiiree, had reached out to her even after she tried to block him. She mentioned that he unexpectedly appeared at her residence, causing her significant distress. In response, Nosiiree denied allegations of stalking during his own livestream, professing his love for KitsuFox and voicing concerns about their personal disputes becoming public knowledge.

California disabled shoppers allege mall stores pushed them into spending thousands; one spent $50,000+
stories.summary: Serious allegations have arisen against Bee & Co., claiming that the company coerced vulnerable customers, including seniors and individuals with disabilities, into making costly purchases. Rep. Brad Sherman is set to bring these alarming issues to the attention of California Attorney General Rob Bonta. Disturbingly, customers reported spending significant sums while feeling pressured to transact.

'If pardoned for one murder, I'd shoot Gyanesh': VIP chief targets CEC over SIR row
stories.summary: Mukesh Sahani expressed strong dissatisfaction with Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's conduct regarding the Election Commission's decisions. He accused the commission of operating under BJP influence and indicated potential consequences for its members. Sahani stated that those involved could face imprisonment after the elections in 2029, particularly highlighting Gyanesh Kumar. The Election Commission defended its processes, asserting that internal disagreements were normal and legal compliance was maintained.

stories.title: How China helped arm Iran before Trump rolled out the red carpet for Xi
stories.summary: China's role as a self-proclaimed peace mediator is put into question with its increasing military backing for Iran. Recent findings indicate a sharp rise in military component deliveries from China, along with a surge in cargo flights by Chinese airlines dedicated to supporting Iranian defense. This partnership adds layers of complexity to U.S.-China diplomatic exchanges in the context of escalating tensions.

stories.title: Engineers used 500,000 cubic yards of Mississippi River sand to build 7 islands and restore 270 acres
stories.summary: Engineers have successfully finalized a habitat restoration initiative at McGregor Lake, utilizing sand from the Mississippi River. This ambitious project involved the construction of seven islands, the enhancement of floodplain forests, and the protection of vital wetlands. The undertaking, spanning six years, has revitalized over 270 acres of aquatic habitats, significantly benefiting local wildlife and fostering greater biodiversity, all while striving to harmonize navigation and ecological preservation.

stories.title: SC asks EC to set timeline for resolving name, symbol dispute between TMC factions
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has urged the Election Commission to address the ongoing factional conflict within the All India Trinamool Congress. It has set a deadline for resolving the party's name and symbol, requiring a decision by Monday. Meanwhile, the Election Commission has temporarily assigned different names and symbols to opposing factions, both of which are vying for control of the party and its assets.

Australian homeowner blames six trees for damage to her 130-year-old home; court finds no link
stories.summary: A homeowner in Australia blamed six neighbouring trees for damage to her 130-year-old heritage home and sought $23,650.86 for repairs and tree removal. The NSW Land and Environment Court rejected her claim, finding that evidence did not establish a causal link between the trees and the damage, with moisture conditions and other factors identified as possible causes.

Protests are ongoing demanding an independent investigation into his death.

Daniel Levy got £27m after leaving Tottenham in 2025; total club earnings reach £88m
stories.summary: On September 4, 2025, Daniel Levy officially stepped down as the executive chairman of Tottenham Hotspur, receiving a £27 million payout that covered both his salary and bonuses. Over his impressive 25-year tenure, Levy amassed earnings of about £61 million. This brings his total compensation to an astonishing £88 million, which coincidentally matches the amount Tottenham earned from Harry Kane's transfer to Bayern Munich.

Putin says record turnout shows Russians back his military agenda in Ukraine

Preliminary results indicated that United Russia secured a significant majority in the Duma. The election included voting in Ukrainian territories claimed by Russia, which Ukraine considers illegal. Amid ongoing Ukrainian drone attacks, authorities extended voting days and allowed online voting in some regions.

$100 Pocket Muon Detector: Students build handheld CosmicWatch; sparks citizen-science network
stories.summary: CosmicWatch is a compact and affordable particle detector that can be used for research and education purposes. Developed by physicist Spencer Axani, it costs about $100 and can be assembled easily. The portable device detects muons, allowing students to investigate cosmic-ray interactions and environmental changes. Researchers have successfully utilized it in high-altitude experiments and various scientific studies.

Why Iran looms large over Trump-Xi talks in White House
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump is planning to address Chinese President Xi Jinping regarding China's support for Iran. The discussion will follow reports linking Chinese entities to lethal satellite imagery provided to Iran prior to an attack. This attack on US troops in Jordan killed three soldiers and wounded others, marking a significant escalation. The meeting will also cover other critical topics like trade, AI, and Taiwan.

stories.title: Donald Trump says Canada has too many immigrants, but the math doesn’t add up
stories.summary: Canada has recently admitted a record number of permanent residents, primarily focusing on economic immigration programs. In contrast, the US processes significantly more green cards through family-based categories than Canada does. India's immigrants play critical roles in both countries, particularly in skilled job sectors. Trump's comments regarding immigration have drawn criticism for being racially charged and factually inaccurate.

stories.title: She turned America’s waste paper into Chinese packaging: How Zhang Yin built her billion-dollar empire
stories.summary: Zhang Yin launched her paper-trading venture in Hong Kong in 1985 with a simple investment strategy. Spotting a lucrative market in collecting waste paper from the United States to ship to China, she founded America Chung Nam, eventually becoming the top exporter of this recyclable material. Expanding further, she created Nine Dragons Paper, seeing tremendous growth in China’s booming economy.
